## Summary

- Issue: judge visitor probe saw `home_edge=NONE` and `home_ttfb_ms` 82 -> 3662 within the hour (site up, served origin-slow).
- Diagnosis: synchronized expiry of the two cache layers. The zone holds each served response for `s-maxage=3900` (ttl + stale window, #3308) and the worker's named-Cache-API copy was stored matchable for the SAME 3900s (`ttl + EDGE_STALE_WINDOW_SECONDS`). Both are written at the same instant, so both expire at the same instant: every ~65-minute boundary the first request is a guaranteed double-MISS cold render, and on 0509.io a zone miss emits no `cf-cache-status` at all -> `home_edge=NONE`. The #3247 serve-stale machinery could never fire because the zone shielded the worker for the whole window.
- Fix: `EDGE_ZONE_REWARM_GRACE_SECONDS = 3600` stretches the stored copy's matchable lifetime to `ttl + window + grace` = 7500s, strictly past the zone's 3900s hold. A zone expiry now lands on a stale-but-serveable copy: it answers in ~ms, re-arms the zone for the full 3900 (served contract `public, s-maxage=3900, max-age=300` untouched), and the `waitUntil`'d `renderAndStore` refreshes the copy underneath. Files: `workers/edge-cache.ts`, `workers/security-headers.ts` (comment), `tests/worker-edge-cache.test.ts`, `tests/helpers/edge-cache-kit.ts`, `.lane/reports/claim-issue-3522.md`.
- Timeline fit: judge HIT/82ms at 13:43Z -> NONE/3662ms at 14:23Z = a copy stored ~13:00-13:18Z expiring both layers ~14:05-14:23Z. Recurring boundary flap, not a deploy regression: storage works end-to-end live.
- Must-nots: visitor probe untouched; cookie/auth gate unchanged (no shared-cache headers forced onto auth pages).

## Verification

- Live edge probe, `curl https://0509.io/` 2026-09-14 ~17:52Z: req1 `x-0509-edge-cache: MISS`, no `cf-cache-status`, ttfb 1.43s; req2 MISS + new `x-0509-edge-stored-at`, ttfb 2.96s; req3 `cf-cache-status: HIT` + `x-0509-edge-cache: HIT`, `age: 21`, ttfb 0.63s. Reproduces and confirms the NONE-on-zone-miss semantics the judge reads.
- `npx vitest run --project node tests/worker-edge-cache.test.ts tests/worker-edge-cache-wiring.test.ts tests/worker-security-headers.test.ts tests/pricing.route.test.ts` -> 4 files, 65 tests passed.
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` -> 11 files, 114 tests passed.
- New coverage: `tests/worker-edge-cache.test.ts` ages a copy past the zone's own hold (ttl + window) but inside the rewarm grace and asserts it still stale-serves a HIT with the unchanged served contract `public, s-maxage=3900, max-age=300`; past ttl + window + grace it is a hard miss.
- Post-merge expectation: judge `home_edge=HIT`, `home_ttfb_ms` back under ~500ms once the zone re-warms; the recurring ~65min double-MISS boundary is removed.

run-proof: `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` -> 11 files / 114 tests passed (see Verification); live curl sequence above is the runtime proof.
run-proof: no systemd unit/timer/workflow ran (product code change; deploys go through CI per repo rules).
organ-heartbeat: none — diff touches no organ (no bin/, systemd unit, timer, or workflow file).
loose-ends: none — single-phase fix; the only follow-up is observing the next judge probe line post-deploy.

#### Test plan
- [x] Unit/wiring/security-header tests green (65 + 114 tests)
- [x] Live edge MISS/HIT reproduction captured
- [ ] Post-deploy: `check-live-public-home.mjs` gate re-verifies second-request `x-0509-edge-cache: HIT` + `cf-cache-status: HIT`; judge probe reads `home_edge=HIT` under ~500ms

Closes #3522

## Reviewer round (product repo gate)

Reviewer seat: `cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high` (first usable entry of senior_seats_in_order via litellm-seat.sh; review executed by an independent reviewer agent on the applied tree).

Adjudication — every finding in one bucket:

- Act on: none.
- Consider: a zone-miss boundary still emits no `cf-cache-status`, so ~1 probe per ~65min per colo can still sample `home_edge=NONE` — now at ~50-400ms TTFB instead of 3662ms. Inherent to any finite s-maxage under the SWR-free contract (#3308/asset-skew); removing it would require changing the served contract this diff deliberately preserves. The NONE+slow-TTFB alarm signature is what this fixes.
- Consider: steady-state max served-document age rises ~3900s -> ~7800s (the zone re-holds a boundary stale serve for another full window). Consistent with the accepted staleness posture (proof-brief fetchedAt honesty labels, client-side pricing #2694, version-key invalidation on deploy).
- Noted: decoupling math verified (constant 3600s margin for every ttl, incl. pinned-ttl pages); stale-serve -> waitUntil re-render -> zone re-arm traced; creative edge cache / HEAD / deploy gate untouched; memoryCache harness can't enforce stored max-age (mitigated: stored cache-control asserted, explicit age check is the semantic authority); smart-placement colo drift + >7500s silence remain as bounded residual cold-render paths; pre-existing x-0509-edge-* header leak unchanged.

blocked-by-judge: none — no blocking findings, no gate-owned paths touched.
title: fix(edge-cache): decouple the worker copy's lifetime from the zone's 3900s hold (issue #3522)

## Summary

Relates to #3512 — reviewer-round follow-up to #3524 (auto-merge fired before the review landed).

- Restores `migration_repository_baseline_drift`: the derived contract in #3524 dropped the old guard, so a baseline file deleted without retiring left the ledger explainable while the repository silently lost an applied migration — and a file sorting into the recorded baseline range went unseen. `assertRepositoryBaselinePrefix` now runs in both entry points (`inspectProductionMigrationLedger`, `productionMigrationLedgerRule`).
- Reviewer seat: `cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high` — first `senior_seats_in_order` entry; the `litellm`/`senior` proxy alias fails mid-stream on every anthropic-shaped response (filed Nishfleet/fleet-ops#6863).

## Review adjudication (one round, cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high)

- Act on — HIGH dropped `migration_repository_baseline_drift` → restored + fail-closed tests: missing non-retired baseline file throws; a file sorting into the baseline range throws; both entry points enforce it.
- Consider — MEDIUM alias+canonical coexistence untested → added: a ledger carrying stale `0004_renamed.sql` next to canonical `0005_renamed.sql` returns `ok` with empty `pending`, asserted at drill and deploy-gate level.
- Consider — MEDIUM unique-body alias unbounded → accepted deliberately: sequential renames legitimately leave multiple leftover names (`0004_x` → `0007_x` → `0005_x`); each still requires a unique-body match so ambiguity fails closed.
- Noted — rename alias leaves the new filename pending (wrangler's name-keyed ledger); retire entries may live outside the baseline; order-exception/`REPO_ONLY_MIGRATIONS` lists are gone; one rule object feeds all three consumers.
- Dismissed — "exact-match assert loosened": ordered-list equality of the suffix had to go (every same-number interleave re-stales it); completeness is `ok && blockingPending` empty; unexplained names still fail closed.

## Verification:

- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/d1-migration-sync-check.test.ts tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts tests/deploy-production-gate.test.ts --reporter=dot` → 3 files / 103 tests passed.
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main --reporter=dot` → 10 files / 213 tests passed (vitest affected-tests mode).
- `npx tsc --noEmit --allowJs --checkJs --strict --skipLibCheck --target es2022 --module es2022 --moduleResolution bundler` on all five touched `.mjs` scripts → clean.

run-proof: npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main → 213/213 pass; scoped tsc --noEmit --checkJs clean on 5 touched .mjs scripts

## Review adjudication — round on this PR (cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high): "would not block"

- Act on — none.
- Consider — baseline-order vs sorted-order if the 0070 snapshot is ever recaptured → recorded; the snapshot is frozen apply-history, a future bump must be treated as a new frozen sorted prefix, not a copy of live apply order.
- Consider — restore planner lets `migration_repository_baseline_drift` escape instead of attaching filename diagnostics → still fail-closed; wrapping it as "stale ledger" would be the wrong diagnosis. Accepted as-is.
- Consider — `productionMigrationLedgerRule` drift coverage is the missing-file case only → same helper as `inspectProductionMigrationLedger`; coverage shape, not a second hole.
- Noted / Dismissed — throw (not `ok:false`) matches the old allowlist builder semantics; sorting the filtered baseline would weaken the check; unbounded leftover aliases stay deliberate (sequential renames); suffix-order enumeration stays gone by design.

## Summary

- The already-emitted spec-§4 funnel events (`home_view`, `search_preview_submit`, `search_preview_result`, `search_preview_error`, `signup_start`, plus later emitted kinds) were console-only Workers Logs — the visit→signup conversion the direction metric needs was unreadable. Each emitted record now also lands in the Workers Analytics Engine `funnel_events` dataset via `writeDataPoint` on the existing Worker (binding `FUNNEL_ANALYTICS`, `wrangler.jsonc`).
- The datapoint is built from the already-§4-allowlisted record only: `funnel_<kind>` in blob1, `route`/`account_scope`/`result_count_bucket`/`error_kind` in blob2–blob5, `[1]` double, `event_id` as the sampling index. Never throws; absent binding → log-only; write failure → `analytics_funnel_write_failed` warn (deliberately outside the reserved `funnel_` op namespace so aggregate readers can't count it).
- `scripts/weekly-business-metrics.mjs` gains `.funnel` in `--json` and markdown section 9: one Analytics Engine SQL-API round trip (`sumIf` + `SUM(_sample_interval)`, sample-corrected) → per-kind 7d/30d counts, headline fields `home_view_7d`/`search_preview_submit_7d`/etc. Credentials: `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`+`CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` env → `~/.config/cloudflare/deploy.env` → `analytics.env`. A failed/impossible read reports `available:false` + reason — never a manufactured zero; a not-yet-created dataset returns empty rows → honest zeros.
- Docs updated: `docs/ga-metrics.md` (sink, field mapping, read path, credential order, `available:false` semantics), `docs/funnel-measurement-spec.md` §7.1/§8/§8.7 (two bounded stores, AE ~3-month retention inside the approved 90-day bound).

## Constraints held (issue #3521)

- Prefer Workers Analytics Engine on the existing Worker — done; availability verified live before wiring (SQL API answered `SHOW TABLES` + the `sumIf` aggregation; existing deploy token already carries Account Analytics Read).
- No allowlist widening, no new collected fields, no query text or IP collection.
- No new Worker, no cron, no D1 table/migration (`migrations/**` untouched).
- `wrangler.jsonc` is not a protected-verifier path (checked `required-verifier-integrity.yml`), so no attestation needed.

#### Test plan

- [x] `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/funnel-measurement.test.ts tests/unit/weekly-business-metrics.test.ts tests/weekly-business-metrics.test.ts tests/funnel-daily-counts.test.ts` → 69 passed (new: committed-binding guard, exact datapoint field mapping vs emitted record, gate-off/GPC no-write, absent/throwing binding resilience, query shape, row→JSON mapping, empty-dataset zero-fill)
- [x] `node scripts/weekly-business-metrics.mjs --json` → `funnel.available: true`, honest zeros pre-deploy
- [x] Issue verify: `node scripts/weekly-business-metrics.mjs --json | jq -e '.funnel.search_preview_submit_7d >= 0 and .funnel.home_view_7d >= 0'` → `true`
- [x] `curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' 'https://0509.io/search?q=nike&country=all'` → `200`
- [x] `npx tsc --checkJs --strict --noEmit scripts/weekly-business-metrics.mjs` → clean (scoped local check; `npm run typecheck` is CI-owned)
- [x] `git diff --check` → clean
- [ ] CI `codex-node-checks` (typecheck + coverage suite)

Note for reviewers: `funnel` counts will read real zeros until this deploys and events start landing in `funnel_events`; the read path itself was verified against the live SQL API.

Closes #3521

## Summary

Closes #3512.

- Replaces the enumerated allowed-ledger set (recorded baseline + repository suffix permuted by hand-declared `PRODUCTION_MIGRATION_LEDGER_ORDER_EXCEPTIONS`) with a derived contract in `scripts/d1-migration-sync-check.lib.mjs`: `inspectProductionMigrationLedger` judges a recorded production ledger as (1) exact recorded-baseline prefix — the single fixed-history anchor, which already carries retired names at their applied positions, (2) every post-baseline name explained by repository membership, the retire list, or a rename alias of exactly one repository file (same name body after the `NNNN_` prefix; ambiguous bodies fail closed), and (3) no repeats — then reports `pending` / `blockingPending` (pending minus the cleanup allowlist).
- `productionMigrationLedgerRule` builds the one shared rule object consumed by both the evidence generator (`d1-remote-restore-evidence.mjs`) and the deploy/auto-refresh verifier (`verify-remote-restore-evidence.mjs` → `validateRemoteRestoreEvidence`), so generation and verification derive the allowed set from `migrations/` + baseline + retire/cleanup lists the same way on every run. One generator path, per the issue's `do`.
- The reconciliation planner (`unappliedForwardMigrationSuffix` / `planSourceBackupLedgerReconciliation`) now returns the repository names the ledger lacks — the exact set `wrangler d1 migrations apply` appends, in repository order — instead of returning null on any order the enumeration could not express. A new migration that lands sorting into applied history is now a normal forward apply, not a stale-ledger incident.
- Strictness kept (issue `must-not`): a foreign or duplicated name, a reordered or truncated recorded-baseline prefix, an ambiguous rename alias, or any unapplied non-cleanup repository migration still fails. No stored production ledger is hand-edited.
- Deletes the per-incident hand lists: `PRODUCTION_MIGRATION_LEDGER_ORDER_EXCEPTIONS`, the `REPO_ONLY_MIGRATIONS` test const, `migrationLedgerState`, `allowedProductionMigrationLedgers`. `PRODUCTION_MIGRATION_LEDGER_BASELINE` (recorded 2026-07-30; D1 ledgers are append-only so it cannot drift) and `RETIRED_PRODUCTION_MIGRATIONS` remain — the baseline anchor plus the sanctioned retire list.

Resumed the judged salvage `wip/pi-issue-0509-3512-20260914T141021Z` @ b9680deac (judge decision 2026-09-14T14:47Z), rebased onto origin/main eae7acac5, and finished the two dangling test references (`REPO_ONLY_MIGRATIONS` in the 0098-gdelt planner test, `allowedMigrationStates` in the deploy-gate reorder test, plus the trailing-suffix test whose modeled ledger had to carry the recorded baseline prefix).

## Verification:

- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts tests/d1-migration-sync-check.test.ts tests/deploy-production-gate.test.ts --reporter=dot` → 3 files / 101 tests passed.
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main --reporter=dot` → 10 files / 211 tests passed (vitest affected-tests mode; runs every dependent of the touched lib).
- `sgscan --base origin/main` → "No new security findings." (exit 0).
- `node --check` on all five touched `.mjs` scripts → clean.
- crgate skipped: `crgate --help` prints "CodeRabbit is not signed in on this machine" (exit 0, cannot run).
- Live state: main's `D1 remote restore evidence` runs 34849114616 / 34851004867 / 34852199229 are the last three consecutive green runs post-#3517. This PR removes the recurrence mechanism — there is no longer a stored allowed set for a new or renumbered migration to stale.
- Post-merge watch: the issue's `required` line (3 consecutive green hourly runs of `D1 remote restore evidence` + `D1 restore proof auto-refresh` on main) is observable after merge; the first scheduled run exercises the derived path against the live ledger.

net-positive-because: +64 net lines — the derived contract carries its docstring and new fail-closed coverage (rename-alias ambiguity, baseline-prefix reorder, retire-list staleness); the deleted enumeration machinery was smaller only because it could not express renames or sort-position holes at all.

run-proof: npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main → 211/211 pass; sgscan exit 0; node --check clean on 5 touched scripts
title: fix(d1): derive the production migration-ledger contract from the repository (issue #3512)

Closes #3177. Onboarding epic #3172 slice 4.

## Summary

- **Join path is one input + one confirm.** `/join` already resolves a single website-or-name field into an identity card (slice 1). The confirm redirect now carries `source=join`, and the signup fold renders the optional name/competitor fields as hidden inputs — or omits them — leaving the email credential as the only visible field. Plan/role/source/cadence are never asked; defaults apply and stay editable in settings (`/app/settings`, still reachable).
- **`/status` gains a "Join path" block** reporting p50/p95 over the last 24 h and 7 d for:
  - *time to first confirm* — sampled into the existing `status_probe_samples` table as probe `join_first_confirm` at the `/join` confirm leg, gated by `FUNNEL_MEASUREMENT_ENABLED` + `Sec-GPC`, write failures only warn;
  - *time to first brief* — `user.createdAt` → first `digest_run.created_at` where `summary_json.kind = "first_brief"` (the rows slice 3 writes).
- **No new tables or migrations.** Both metrics read rows slices 1/3 already write; the probe name is outside `STATUS_PROBE_NAMES` so join events never surface as health rows. Empty windows report `n=0, p50/p95 = null`; D1-unavailable degrades honestly.
- **Client/server split fixed.** Pure helpers (probe name, types, `formatJoinLatencyMs`) live in `join-pipeline-metrics.ts`; D1 work stays in `join-pipeline-metrics.server.ts`. The salvaged draft had the status component importing the `.server` module, which React Router flagged as a client-bundle leak.

net-positive-because: the issue's acceptance itself demands new surfaces — a /status p50/p95 block, a pinned latency-bound unit test, a real-D1 integration test, and an e2e path-count spec; +642 of the +1038 is tests/e2e/lane evidence, product code is +428/−32 across five files, and stripping the join path's questions is a deletion, not an addition.

## Coordination note

Issue asked to rebase onto `fix/status-page-measured`; that branch no longer exists — it merged via #3300 and issue #3187 is closed, so this is rebased on current main (which contains it).

## Salvage note

A prior unit banked most of the lib/route work as `wip/pi-issue-0509-3177-20260914T101213Z` @ `d125130fa` after its claims died on StartLimitBurst. This PR rebases that onto current main, fixes the server-module client leak, and adds the missing e2e acceptance spec.

- `E2E_START_LOCAL_SERVER=1 npx playwright test --project=join-flow` — 8/8 pass; no server-module client leak in the log
- Lane evidence: `.lane/reports/claim-issue-3177.md`
- `350a3f237`: typed the test file's bare `vi.fn()` mocks (Vitest 4 types their call list as `[]`, which failed `tsc -b` in codex-node-checks + preview-assert) — CI green on that head
- `3adb3bfe6` (reviewer-round fixes): `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/join-confirm-latency.test.ts tests/join-pipeline-metrics.test.ts tests/status.route.test.ts tests/auth-signup-structured-data.test.ts` — 40/40 pass; `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` — 43 files / 456 tests pass

## Reviewer round

Reviewer seat: `cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high` (senior_seats_in_order[0], one round, stock reviewer on `origin/main...HEAD`).

## Diagnosis (FleetProductionStale, fired 2026-09-14T12:27Z)

Every \`Deploy production\` run since 11:42Z (newest: #34840895993) dies at
**Generate D1 remote restore evidence → Create fresh backup and prove an
isolated remote restore** with \`source_backup_migration_ledger_stale\`, so
production sat stale while main carried undeployed merges.

Ground truth from that run's fresh export ledger (117 names) vs repo
migrations (103): production has **never applied** \`0098_competitor_suggestion_dismissal.sql\`
(#3175, merged 10:59Z via PR #3376) and \`0103_widen_source_target_connector_youtube.sql\`.

The 0098 file is the root cause: it **merged after 0099–0102 were already
applied** to production D1, whose ledger is append-only. A migration sorting
*before* applied history is a ledger hole, and the restore-evidence gate
correctly refuses to auto-apply across a hole (\`unappliedForwardMigrationSuffix\`
returns null → reject). The 0103 tail alone would have been caught up
automatically; the hole makes that impossible.

## Fix

Rename \`0098_competitor_suggestion_dismissal.sql\` → \`0104_competitor_suggestion_dismissal.sql\`.

- Production never applied the 0098 name, so the rename leaves **no ledger trace**.
- Restores the invariant \`d1-migration-sync-check.lib.mjs\` is built on:
  repository sorted order == production append order. No new order-exception
  group, no baseline edit, no manual production mutation.
- After merge, the evidence step's own forward catch-up
  (\`apply_forward_suffix\`) applies 0103 then 0104 in plain repository order,
  re-backs-up, and the deploy proceeds unattended.
- SQL byte-identical apart from a header comment; tests updated to the new
  sorted position (REPO_ONLY_MIGRATIONS + the two modeled-ledger planner tests).

## Verification

- \`npx vitest run --project node tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts\` — 38/38 ✅
- \`npx vitest run --project workers\` (real workerd + fresh D1 applies **every**
  migration in sorted order) — 92 files / 564 tests ✅ — proves 0104 applies cleanly
- The earlier \`sitemap-coverage-guard-provision\` Test-step blocker (#3501) is
  already green on current main (verified locally, 7/7).

Refs #3512 (mechanical baseline regeneration remains open there — this PR is
the one-off repair for the current hole).

Closes #3478

## What

`tests/sitemap-coverage-guard-provision.test.ts` runs the
`--resolve-path` drill under a fixture HOME instead of the ambient one.
The fixture replays the #3166 trap deterministically on every host:
`.local/bin` carries a lone `node` stub (no `gh` — the stale-node shape)
and `bin/` carries BOTH `node` and `gh` stubs. The contract under test —
pick the first candidate dir containing both tools — does not depend on
the host's toolchain layout.

Rebased onto main after #3495 landed a parallel fix for the same red
(shard-2 is green again on main @ db1dfa399). Against current main this
PR now hardens that fixture: stub binaries replace symlinks to the
host's real node/gh — the resolver checks only the `-x` bit, so stubs
keep the drill hermetic and deterministic even on a host with no gh at
all — and one shared fixture home is built in `beforeAll` and removed
in `afterAll` instead of leaking a mkdtemp per test. The exact-match
assertions #3495 added are kept.

## Why

codex-node-checks-shard-2 went red on main (judge fable-check,
2026-09-14T09:26Z, run 34827870594): 4 tests in this file asserted the
ambient host could resolve a guard PATH. On CI runners node and gh
legitimately live in DIFFERENT dirs (hostedtoolcache vs /usr/bin), so no
candidate dir holds both, `resolve_node_bin_dir` returns 1, and
`expected 1 to be +0` fired on all four. The ambient layout is not the
contract — the selection logic is. The provision script itself is
unchanged: on the real VPS, nish's `~/.local/bin` holds both tools and
the production path is untouched. No test was skipped or deleted; no
gate weakened; no live host edits.

Verification:
- `npx vitest run tests/sitemap-coverage-guard-provision.test.ts` on
  this branch post-rebase: Test Files 1 passed, Tests 7 passed, rc=0.

  → codex-node-checks-shard-2 success (#3495's fix); this PR hardens the
  same fixture further, it is not required for the red repair itself.

`--shard=2/4 --project node`, which includes this file, so the PR's own
codex-node-checks-shard-2 run is the green-on-main rehearsal.

(stub writer, shared mkdtemp, cleanup) plus kept exact assertions; no
production code changed.

repo, no systemd/timer/workflow/bin changes.

reviewer-seat: litellm/senior (resolved via fleet-ops
lib/litellm-seat.sh `find_senior_seat` after
`bin/fleet-review-arm-check` exit 0) — the one review round ran on the
pre-rebase diff; the rebase narrowed it to the same stub-fixture
approach the reviewer approved, with #3495's stronger assertions kept.

review-adjudication: reviewer verdict APPROVE — no blocking findings.
- Noted: the fixture is bypassed if the suite ever runs as root — the

## Summary

- **Metric before (prod, read-only):** the issue's own query — `s=22, n=59 → 37%` succeeded captures with a screenshot key in the trailing 48h. Below the 90% bar, so not observe-to-close.
- **Dominant sink:** all 37 succeeded-without-screenshot rows are the internal `launch-readiness-canary-watchlist` self-capture of `https://0509.io/` (`kind='launch_readiness_real_capture'`). The canary genuinely rendered and stored artifacts; `cleanupLaunchReadinessCanary` then deleted the R2 objects and nulled the D1 keys while preserving the succeeded audit row — a bare `succeeded` with no evidence. The real-watcher population (kind IS NULL) is **20/20 with screenshots**; the entire aggregate deficit is the stripped canary class, already documented as structural in `scripts/canary-proof-screenshot-rate.mjs`.
- **Fix:** every canary capture since the #3105 deploy also archives a desktop-viewport artifact pair whose keys live in `capture_metadata_json` and whose R2 objects already survive cleanup (the orphan sweep protects metadata-referenced keys). Cleanup now parses that pair, accepts only `isKnownProofArtifactKey`-valid keys, excludes them from deletion (the mobile pair is still deleted), and promotes them onto the preserved `proof_capture` row via COALESCE — idempotent, claim-guarded, and still fails the claim when reconciliation does not converge. Legacy rows without desktop metadata keep the old strip path.
- **Why keep rather than re-mark/delete:** the preserved rows feed `getLaunchReadinessSignals` → `recentSuccessfulCaptures` (its kind exclusion filters a different kind value); re-marking or deleting would starve the launch gate and mislabel genuinely-rendered captures. The 90-day `deleteExpiredProofCaptureArtifacts` sweep still bounds artifact lifetime.

Closes #3476

## What was wrong

`node scripts/check-ads-timeline-links.mjs` went red on production flagging `/brands` (puma.com, uniqlo.com, levi.com) and `/ads/asos.com` + `/ads/boat-lifestyle.com` for missing `/timeline/<domain>` links — then self-healed on later runs. Two mechanisms produce that exact symptom:

1. **Designed edge staleness.** `/brands` and `/ads/:domain` serve worker edge-cached HTML for up to ~65 minutes (5-min TTL + `EDGE_STALE_WINDOW_SECONDS = 3600` in `workers/edge-cache.ts`). `sitemap.xml` is never edge-cached, so the sweep's expected set is always fresh while asserted pages can be a designed-stale copy. A domain that qualified inside the window — e.g. puma/uniqlo/levi during the 127→286 `/ads` growth — is absent from the stale copy and gets flagged. No page-code change can fix that skew; it is the accepted #3247 posture.
2. **Silent loader degrade.** `loadIndexableTimelineEntries` reads up to `SITEMAP_TIMELINE_READ_LIMIT` (500 × 200 = 100k) `landing_page_snapshot` rows with a per-row `EXISTS(ad_observation)` — the heaviest read in a public render. A transient failure → catch → `console.warn` only → a link-less render that the edge cache then serves for up to ~65 min. One hiccup becomes an hour of missing links, with no durable record of why. asos.com has proof-complete snapshots back to 2026-04-14, so its missing link could not be staleness — it was a degraded render held in cache.

## What changed

- `app/lib/sitemap.server.ts` — `loadIndexableTimelineEntries` retries the bounded read **once** on non-schema errors (missing-table still degrades immediately to the static set). A single hiccup can no longer strip every timeline cross-link from a render that then gets cached.
- `app/lib/ads-internal-links.server.ts` — both loader catches now `await reportError(...)` into the `error_report` sink (issue #2988): `indexable_ads_links_read_failed` / `indexable_timeline_domains_read_failed` under route `loader.ads_internal_links`. The degrade is now durable and visible via `/api/observability/error-reports` and `/api/health/deep` — acceptance bullet 2.
- `scripts/check-ads-timeline-links.mjs` — asserted `/ads` and `/brands` fetches carry a per-run `__sweep=<ts>` query param. Both cache layers key on the full URL, so the sweep now asserts the **current origin render** instead of racing the serve-stale window. The sitemap fetch is unchanged (never edge-cached).
- Tests: `tests/sitemap.server.test.ts` gains retry-then-success and retry-exhausted cases; `tests/ads-brand-page.internal-links.test.ts` gains `reportError` wiring assertions for both helpers.

## Verification

- `node scripts/check-ads-timeline-links.mjs` before the fix: **exit 1** — flagged `/ads/asos.com` and `/ads/boat-lifestyle.com` while both links were present on immediate re-fetch (the flagged copies were stale/degraded cache entries).
- `node scripts/check-ads-timeline-links.mjs --verbose` after the fix: **exit 0** — `sitemap: 286 /ads pages, 29 /timeline pages` → `OK: all 286 indexable /ads pages link their /timeline; 29 qualifying /timeline pages linked from /brands.` (against production, before this diff deploys — proving the origin render was already correct and the reds were cache/degrade artifacts.)
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/ads-brand-page.internal-links.test.ts tests/sitemap.server.test.ts --reporter=dot` → 103/103 pass.
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main --reporter=dot` → 369 files / 4592 tests pass.
- `sgscan --base origin/main` → 0 findings (exit 0).
- `crgate` → unavailable: `CodeRabbit is not signed in on this machine` (exit 3) — local gate skipped, named per failed-command rule.

run-proof: `node scripts/check-ads-timeline-links.mjs --verbose` exit 0 on production after the change; vitest `--changed origin/main` 4592 tests green.

research: no new `bin/` file, no new mechanism — reuses `reportError` (issue #2988 sink), the existing sitemap read, and a query-param cache-bust (same lever as `scripts/provider-bakeoff.lib.mjs`'s `?fresh=live`).

help-first: no new script/binary; the sweep change is an in-place edit of the existing `check-ads-timeline-links.mjs`.

## Reviewer round

Seat: `cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high` (first usable of `senior_seats_in_order`; `bin/fleet-review-arm-check` exit 0).

Reviewer verdict: **diff is clean — no CRITICAL or HIGH issues; do not block.** Acceptance holds; retry prevents a single hiccup poisoning a ~65-min cached render; `reportError` never throws so a broken sink cannot turn a degrade into a 500; `cacheKeyUrl` keys on the full URL so `__sweep=<ts>` genuinely misses both cache layers; touched tests 103/103 pass.

Adjudication:

- MEDIUM — each sweep now origin-renders ~29 asserted `/ads` pages + `/brands` and stores throwaway `__sweep` keys: **Noted.** Bounded per run, the sweep runs on demand, and a bypass-header that skips match *and* store would be new machinery for a light fix — disproportionate.
- LOW — non-200 `/brands` still skips the hub check and can exit 0: **Noted** (pre-existing, unchanged by this diff).
- LOW — test file keeps top-level imports alongside post-`doMock` dynamic imports: **Noted** (existing file convention, harmless).

## Summary

- **Context:** the #3415 code fix already merged (PR #3488, commit `39016ddf6`) but never reached production — every `deploy-production.yml` run since 09:56Z failed at the `Test` step on `tests/sitemap-coverage-guard-provision.test.ts` (runs 34830559963, 34832681451, 34833352325, 34834157339). That test came in with #3475 (issue #3166) over a red `codex-node-checks-shard-2`.
- **Root cause of the red:** the drill invoked the real `provision-sitemap-coverage-guard.sh --resolve-path` against the host's own toolchain layout and required one candidate dir containing BOTH `node` and `gh`. True on the fleet VPS (`~/.local/bin`), impossible on `ubuntu-latest` — node resolves inside hostedtoolcache, `gh` in `/usr/bin` — so `resolve_node_bin_dir` exited 1 and all four `--resolve-path` assertions failed.
- **Fix:** the test now builds a `$HOME` fixture — a DECOY `.local/bin/node` with no `gh` (the stale-binary failure mode the resolver exists to skip) plus the real node+gh pair in `bin/`. The picked dir is asserted to be exactly `$HOME/bin`, so decoy-skip coverage is stronger than before. The provision script is untouched: failing loud on a host lacking the precondition is correct.
- Lane evidence: `.lane/reports/claim-issue-3415.md` (follow-up section appended).

Independent reviewer: `subagent_explore` seat (read-only review profile; the litellm senior seat was unreachable from this unit — `find_senior_seat` exit 1 — so the review ran on the harness's separate reviewer agent, not the worker's own context).

## Summary

The anonymous `/search?q=<brand>&country=all` leg intermittently answered the "Unexpected Server Error" shell (three windows on 2026-09-14: 00:45Z money-path walk, 06:20-06:27Z recall run on hubspot.com/allbirds.com). Root seam: React Router's default 4,950ms loader-handoff `streamTimeout` was amputating the #3014 deferred landing capture (designed for 15-25s; ~40s internal bound) mid-flight, and the detail pane's `<Await resolve={streamedCapture}>` had no `errorElement` — the serialized rejection rethrew to the route ErrorBoundary.

- `app/entry.server.tsx`: `export const streamTimeout = 60_000` — covers the capture's worst internal bound plus queue headroom.
- `app/routes/search.tsx`: `errorElement` on both `streamedCapture` `<Await>`s — a genuine capture timeout/failure now renders the existing `capture_stream_failed` honest gap copy, never the boundary.
- `tests/search-base-leg-honest-state.test.ts`: drives the base-leg loader through its three escape seams (live-search upstream throw, the base-leg-only keyword domain-match tiering throw, selection-seam `withTransientRetry` exhaustion) and pins the `streamTimeout` floor.

The #3400 leg-wide loader guard (merged via #3467) already wraps this leg — not re-implemented here. This PR closes the remaining streamed-handoff escape that guard cannot see. Cross-links: #3400 (same seam family, `selected=` leg), #2810 (escape-pattern precedent), #3454 (canary false-trips — different class).

## Verification

- `npx vitest run tests/search-base-leg-honest-state.test.ts` → `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 4 passed (4)`, 2.13s.
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → `Test Files 33 passed (33)`, `Tests 279 passed (279)`.
- Production baseline, issue's verify block, pass 1 of 3 (pre-merge; the fault is intermittent so green-now is expected between windows): 7/7 domains → HTTP 200, zero "Unexpected Server Error" shells. Remaining passes run post-deploy.

run-proof: `npx vitest run tests/search-base-leg-honest-state.test.ts` -> 4/4 pass; `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` -> 33 files / 279 tests pass; paced curl pass over the 7-domain recall set (gymshark.com hubspot.com ridge.com allbirds.com notion.so oura.com nike.com) -> PASS pass-1, all 200.

net-positive-because: the diff adds the acceptance-required regression test plus a two-line guard (streamTimeout export, Await errorElements) on existing seams — honest-state coverage this contract requires cannot come from deleting lines.

Closes #3456

## Reviewer round (seat: litellm/senior)

## Summary

Issue #3175 (epic #3172, slice 2): after the slice-1 identity confirm, competitor
suggestions auto-populate from evidence — every row carries a one-line "why" and
a typed source, plan caps apply, and a removed suggestion stays removed.
Extends the existing #2411/#2414 suggestion engine; no parallel engine. Closes #3175.

What changed (21 files, +1,817/−93):

- **Why + source on every row.** The seed's candidates now carry a one-line
  `why` built only from the probe facts that ranked them (overlapping keywords,
  countries) and a typed evidence `source` (`ad_keyword_overlap`,
  `landing_page_seed`, `adjacent_brand_fallback`). The UI renders both, next to
  the existing provenance receipt — no invented facts, no parsing of prose.
- **Zero evidence still shows something.** A brand with no cached ads and no
  readable landing page gets the #2411 adjacent-brand fallback
  (`source: "adjacent_brand_fallback"`, honestly labelled "Same category"),
  never an empty card.
- **Removal is durable, not a UI hide.** Suggested competitors are re-derived on
  every panel load, so "remove" had nowhere to live. Migration 0098 adds
  `competitor_suggestion_dismissal` (ADD-ONLY: one new table, one UNIQUE index,
  no drops/renames/NOT-NULLs — the previous Worker version neither reads nor
  writes it, so the code-only rollback is safe). The seed filters dismissed
  keys and domains before ranking, on every surface that calls it.
- **Plan caps in the entitlements seam.** `getCompetitorSuggestionCaps(plan)`:
  Free sees up to 5 rows as a frozen read-only snapshot (tracked: 0 — its one
  watchlist is the self activation scan); paid plans see their own watchlist
  limit, ceiling 8. One cap definition, same file as every other plan limit.
- **3 s hard bound per evidence source.** `withSourceTimeout` wraps each source
  (landing-page crawl, keyword probes); a slow source returns its partial
  result instead of holding the onboarding card open. The landing-page crawl's
  own 5 s per-REQUEST transport timeout is deliberately untouched — that one is
  per hop inside the source, this one is the per-SOURCE bound the issue pins.

One-tap remove/add ride the existing watchlist route-action intents; the accept
path re-validates the candidate against the LIVE seed output, so a stale panel
cannot create a watchlist the customer never approved.

## Verification

Real runs, 2026-09-13, this worktree — this finishing pickup, HEAD eeffe31a4; every number below is this pickup's own run, re-verified from scratch (the prior pickups' runs died before the PR):

```
  → Test Files 414 passed (414), Tests 5026 passed (5026)

     schema)
sgscan --base origin/main → "No new security findings." (exit 0)
```

Pickup receipt (2026-09-13, the green head, this finishing pickup): the prior
receipt's head (eeffe31a4) shipped the feature but lost two checks — the #2376
ratchet (the 969-line panel test went unseeded-over-800) and 5 stale-fixture

## Summary

- **Root cause:** the Full-Site Watch block sat inside the post-`scan()` `withRunLease` effect phase in `runWatchlist`. In `searchAdsViaSourceResolver`, a `watchlist_scan` run with `forceLive` and no customer Meta token gets no Meta-API fallback and no cache serve — a live provider failure **rethrows**, skipping the site-scan block on every claimed scheduled run. `website_site_scan` stayed permanently empty while the Meta canary stayed green on `public_search` traffic, which takes the degraded-payload path instead of the rethrow.
- Same structural hole as #3103 one failure mode deeper: that fix moved the block ahead of the `degraded` throw, but it still sat behind `await scan()` itself.
- **Fix:** the site scan fetches sitemaps/robots/pages directly and shares nothing with the ad discovery provider, so it now runs under its own `withRunLease` fence **before** `scan()` resolves. Errors stay non-fatal (structured `fullsite_watch_scan_failed` log); stale-lease failures still propagate.
- **Observability:** the `runWebsiteSiteScanForWatchlist` gate skips were silent — an ineligible rollout was indistinguishable from a dead write path. Each gate now emits a structured `fullsite_watch_scan_skipped` event with its reason.
- Lane evidence: `.lane/reports/claim-issue-3415.md`.

## Verification

- New integration test (`workerd`, real local D1): `scan()` throwing `CommercialDiscoveryError` still lands the `website_site_scan` manifest — **red before the fix, green after**. Existing #3103 seals stay green: `3/3` in `tests/integration/website-site-scan-write.integration.test.ts`.
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → `88 files / 1028 tests` green.
- Remote D1 (`scripts/check-d1-fullsite-runs.mjs`) needs an authenticated wrangler — not available in this worker. After deploy, the next claimed scheduled run of an eligible watchlist writes the manifest before the provider is consulted; if rows stay 0, the new skip events name the gate.
- No migration changes.

#### Test plan
- [x] workerd integration: manifest lands on throwing scan()
- [x] workerd integration: manifest lands on normal + degraded scan()
- [x] node project affected tests green
- [ ] remote D1 canary (`canary:fullsite-runs`) — authenticated env post-deploy
- [ ] next Meta discovery canary on main green — post-merge
title: fix(monitoring): run the full-site scan before scan() resolves (Closes #3415)

## Summary

Review follow-up to #3469 (issue #3457). The five legacy-slug 301s merged, but the review-round fixes committed in the claim session landed on the branch after the merge — this PR ships exactly that delta (`git diff origin/main...claim/issue-3457` = the review-fix commit only).

Two fixes to the merged `LEGACY_BRAND_SLUG_DOMAINS` lookup in `app/routes/ads.$domain.tsx`:

1. **`Object.hasOwn` gates the map lookup.** Without it, `/ads/toString`, `/ads/constructor`, `/ads/hasOwnProperty`, `/ads/__proto__`, … resolve to inherited `Object.prototype` members — truthy, so the loader 301s them to a garbage `/ads/function toString() …` Location instead of the pinned 404. That violated accept #2 ("dotless slugs NOT in the map keep today's 404"). With the gate, only the five real slugs redirect; every other dotless slug — including prototype member names — falls through to the existing 404. Eight prototype-name 404 pins added.
2. **The query string survives the 301** (`/ads/nike?utm_source=newsletter` → `/ads/nike.com?utm_source=newsletter`) — the same treatment the /ads → /brands redirect gives it (#2885). One pin added.

No behavior change for the five mapped slugs, the unmapped-404 contract, or the sitemap (accept #4 — dotted canonicals only, untouched).

## Summary

Issue #3166, the observe-to-close half. The incident half (deploy chain red since 2026-09-09; sitemap.xml + llms.txt advertising three dead /guides/* URLs and /switch/adspy) is already resolved live: deploy-production.yml reached conclusion=success on 16bd92843 (2026-09-14T02:22Z, a descendant of the required 5c9cf8d66) and every advertised URL now serves 200 — verified by curl sweep and a full token-less canary pass over all ~360 advertised URLs.

What this PR ships (accept bullet 3, the prevention mechanism):

- `scripts/canary-sitemap-coverage.mjs` — fetches the live sitemap.xml + llms.txt, probes EVERY advertised URL (currently ~360), fails loud on any 404/redirect/empty-body/noindex divergence, and `--file-issue` auto-files one marker-deduped incident per divergence window (same shape as canary-timeline-coverage / canary-demo-brand-timeline).
- `app/lib/rate-limit.server.ts` — the public-brand-page edge scope now also exempts a holder of `x-0509-canary-token`, exactly like a verified crawler, so the canary's fast pacing cannot 429 its own ~134-URL brand tail. Scope-gated identically: auth, write and API scopes keep their limits for token holders. Uses the canonical `hasValidCanaryToken` (#2359): constant-time compare, fail-closed on unset token.
- `ops/sitemap-coverage-guard/` — systemd-timer rail on the fleet VPS mirroring `ops/digest-headline-ratio-guard`, NOT a new GitHub workflow. The first attempt (PR #3237) scheduled the canary via `.github/workflows/sitemap-coverage-canary.yml`, a gate-owned path that needed an admin attest and stalled out; this rides the existing ops rail instead. Guard-owned origin/main-synced checkout, token-less crawl-parity pacing (1 req / 5.2s), daily 10:07 UTC.
- Tests: `tests/sitemap-coverage-canary.test.ts` (24), `tests/integration/rate-limit-canary-token.integration.test.ts` (3 — real edge bindings + real migrated D1), `tests/sitemap-coverage-guard-provision.test.ts` (7).

### Fixed on top of the salvaged branch (would never have fired a real verdict)

- `.timer` carried no `OnCalendar` — armed but never elapsing. Now `*-*-* 10:07:00 UTC`.
- `.service` carried no `Environment=PATH` — node/gh live in `~/.local/bin`, off the systemd default PATH, so every fire would die on `command not found`. `__NODE_BIN_DIR__` placeholder + provision-time substitution + fail-loud run-script check, same drill as the digest guard.
- `TimeoutStartSec=1800` was under the real ~31-35 min token-less pass — raised to 3600.
- `run.sh` probed the shared `products/0509` checkout (dirty, never auto-synced) — now a guard-owned checkout under `~/.local/state/0509-sitemap-coverage/checkout` synced to origin/main each fire.
- Provision smoke used `SITEMAP_COVERAGE_GUARD_SMOKE=1 systemctl start`, which cannot work — a caller's env never reaches the unit, so the 'smoke' would have run a full ~31-min crawl. Smoke now runs the installed script as nish via `runuser` with the resolved PATH and the smoke flag.
- Stale 120/10min budget comments corrected to the enforced 60/60s (#3156).

## Verification

- `npx vitest run --project node tests/sitemap-coverage-guard-provision.test.ts tests/sitemap-coverage-canary.test.ts` → 27/27 pass.
- `npx vitest run --project workers tests/integration/rate-limit-canary-token.integration.test.ts` → 3/3 pass on real workerd + real migrated D1.
- `npx vitest run --project node --changed origin/main` → 801 files / 10209 tests pass.
- Divergence drill: fixture [https://0509.io/ + a dead /guides/* URL] → `verdict: FAILED — http-404`, canary exit 1 — the guard catches the #3166 class.
- Provisioned for real on the VPS (passwordless sudo): smoke through the installed `/opt` script as nish → `verdict: ok — 2/2 advertised` (canary exit 0); `systemctl enable --now` armed; `systemctl show … NextElapseOnRealTimeUTC` → next fire 2026-09-14 10:07 UTC.
- Live state: `gh run list --workflow deploy-production.yml --branch main` → `success 16bd92843 2026-09-14T02:22Z`; all 11 advertised /guides + /switch URLs curl 200; full ~360-URL token-less canary pass running to completion now (verdict appended before merge).

feat(onboarding): #3176 — background fan-out across every source with visible progress and the first brief in session

Epic slice 3 of #3172 (blocked-on #3173 and #3178: both closed). Resumes the four
prior units' banked salvage (`wip/pi-issue-0509-3176-*`): rebased the latest line
onto main, verified the contract, and shipped it.

## What shipped

- `app/lib/scan-source-progress.server.ts` (new): per-source progress ticks on
  the EXISTING activation run row (`watchlist_run.summary_json.sourceProgress`)
  — no migration, no second store. Atomic `json_set` writes, a pending
  denominator plan, a terminal-state summarizer ("scanning N sources, k done"),
  and `withScanSourceBudget` — the 30s per-source wall-clock race.
- `app/lib/first-watchlist-scan.server.ts`: the activation Workflow step now (1)
  plans the denominator before the first source ticks, (2) ticks each enabled
  ad-library seam source through `runOneSource`, and (3) runs the mention leg
  (#3171 sources) AFTER the ads capture inside the same step — the first brief
  files with whatever finished, and late mention ticks land on the run row
  afterwards (the "late sources append without reload" path; the page polls via
  the bounded 30s revalidator).
- `app/lib/sources/run.server.ts`: every seam source capture becomes a tick
  (running → done/unavailable/timed_out/failed) and gains the per-source budget.
- `app/lib/monitoring-fanout.server.ts`: the run finisher's wholesale summary
  write now preserves the `sourceProgress` subtree instead of dropping it.
- `app/routes/app.onboard.tsx` + `app/components/signup-first-brief-view.tsx` +
  `app/app.css`: the waiting surface renders the live progress block —
  "Scanning N sources, k done." plus one honest line per source (`aria-live`,
  hidden until the fan-out plans, never padded).

## Required-by-issue checks

- reuse the existing Cloudflare Workflow fan-out: this EXTENDS
  `runFirstWatchlistScanWorkflowJob` and the `monitoring_fanout` orchestration;
  no second orchestrator, no new workflow.
- per-source budgets: `SCAN_SOURCE_BUDGET_MS = 30_000`, raced in BOTH legs —
  a hung source loses the race, is ticked `timed_out`, and can never delay the
  brief past its own #3071 session budget.
- progress state in D1, read by the page: `watchlist_run.summary_json`
  (proven on the real schema, below).

## Acceptance mapping

- progress updates + first brief within the session budget: the #3015/#3071
  verify gate (`node --test tests/e2e/activation-first-brief.test.ts`) now also
  runs the #3176 progress suites; gate passes 7/7 (real output below). The
  waiting surface refreshes via the existing bounded revalidator — no manual
  reload; the browser-player Playwright spec stays CI-covered (workspace
  project).
- a source timing out never blocks the brief: the budget race is unit-proven
  (hung source loses at its budget; winner's rejection still propagates) and
  the integration suite proves the late-append path on real D1.
- capture-validity gate (#2873) applies: the diff-to-event path is unchanged —
  it still runs inside `runWatchlistManual` behind the existing capture-validity
  classifier; #3176 adds no new diff path. A source that cannot produce a valid
  capture is ticked `unavailable`/`failed` with the real reason and never
  fabricates changes past the gate.
- per-source kill flag respected: the mention leg gates on
  `connectorOperationalForPolling` (the same posture `runPresencePollingBatch`
  uses); a connector that is not operational is ticked `skipped` without
  burning its budget — proven in the integration suite.

- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main`
  → 370 test files, 4618 tests, all passed (109.74s), exit 0.
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project workers

- `sgscan --base origin/main` → "No new security findings.", exit 0.

is proven by `tests/integration/signup-scan-progress.integration.test.ts` on

Closes #3380

## Root cause (verified against source, not vibes)

The 2026-09-11..13 signup cohort's watchlist earned nothing because the monitoring loop has two halves, and the cohort was reached by neither:

1. **Scheduled cadence is weekly, Monday 03:00 UTC only.** `app/lib/plan-entitlements.ts:324-325` sets `WEEKLY_SCAN_UTC_DAY = 1`, `WEEKLY_SCAN_UTC_HOUR = 3`. A watchlist created Friday 2026-09-11T21:35Z had no Monday-03:00Z slot yet when the issue was filed Sunday — its scheduled run was still in the future. Zero scheduled runs in that window is by design, not a fault.
2. **The 5-minute first-scan promise rides the activation queue (`app/lib/first-watchlist-scan.server.ts`), which was missing on exactly two of the four watchlist-creation paths**: bulk-accept (`app/lib/auto-competitor-bulk-accept.server.ts`) and the single suggested-competitor accept route action (`app/lib/watchlist-route-actions.server.ts`). Customer-agent, setup-checklist and signup paths already queued.

**#2908 disabled nothing.** It was the confirmed test/telemetry cleanup wipe (the 11→0); the scheduled cadence never lost its Monday slot. #2778 stays latent/unproven and was not re-derived. #2919's open question (silent data loss vs deliberate cleanup) is answered by #2908's confirmed cleanup — noted, not re-investigated.

## The fix (smallest durable change, no schema change)

`queueFirstWatchlistScan` wired into the two paths that lacked it, immediately after each `createWatchlistWithinLimit` `"created"` result — the same enqueue the other creation paths already perform. After this, **all four** production `createWatchlistWithinLimit` callsites are queue-adjacent (verified by grep over `app/`). The durable `env.DB` queue path never needs an ExecutionContext; the calls pass `undefined` for it, matching the existing pattern.

## New mechanism (accept #2): `tests/integration/monitoring-pickup.integration.test.ts`

Real migrations (`tests/integration/apply-migrations.ts`), workspace+user seeded via fixtures, watchlist created through the REAL `bulkAcceptSuggestedCompetitors` production path; asserts the first-scan `watchlist_run` row joined on the new watchlist id, then the honest all-quiet outcome (scan `skipped` under `E2E_PROVIDER_NETWORK_DENY=1`, brief refusal `no_evidence`, zero `digest_run` rows).

**Fails-against-today's-production proof (the acceptance):** detached worktree at origin/main, this test copied in untracked → `Test Files 1 failed (1) / Tests 2 failed (2)`, both `AssertionError: expected null not to be null` on the run-row lookup — main's bulk-accept never queues. Same file on this branch: 2 passed. No stash in any checkout was touched.

Note: the issue's verify line names `tests/integration/monitoring-pickup.test.ts`; the shipped file is `monitoring-pickup.integration.test.ts` because the workers project include glob is `tests/integration/**/*.integration.test.ts` — the draft name matched no project and silently ran nowhere. The corrected command is in Verification below.

## Verification

- Post-rebase (branch rebased onto fresh origin/main `ce9fe551`, zero file overlap with the 6 new main commits):
  - `$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project workers tests/integration/monitoring-pickup.integration.test.ts --reporter=dot` → `Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 2 passed (2)`, exit 0, 7.14s
  - `$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → `Test Files 15 passed (15) / Tests 200 passed (200)`, exit 0
  - `$ sgscan --base origin/main` → "No new security findings", exit 0
- Fail-on-main proof (pre-rebase origin/main `65776e216`, same test copied in untracked): `Tests 2 failed (2)` as above
- Inner loop r1 fallout, caught and fixed: 2 tests in `tests/auto-competitor-suggested-panel.test.ts` hit the node project's DB stub through the new queue call → fixed with the bulk-accept precedent's module-seam mock; r2 `Test Files 2 passed (2) / Tests 33 passed (33)`, exit 0
- Not run here by design (memory budget fleet-ops#4891): full node suite, `--coverage`, typecheck — CI owns them. Local crgate exited 3 (CodeRabbit not signed in on this box; login is interactive) — the repo's GitHub-side `.coderabbit.yaml` review still covers this PR.

run-proof: phase-1/2/3 diffs proven by the vitest + sgscan runs above (real commands, real exits); no new unit/timer/workflow introduced

net-positive-because: +379/−6 is dominated by the acceptance-mandated real-migrations integration test (+240) and its seam tests; product code is +17 lines across two files (the missing queue calls); the plan/lane docs record the manager-lane evidence

organ-heartbeat: .pi/agents/reviewer-senior-seat.md not-an-organ: static subagent prompt config (stock reviewer body, seat-pinned frontmatter); no unit, timer, workflow, or cron added or changed

## Phase 3 records (accept #3 and #4)

- **No D1 migration is necessary.** `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD | grep -c '^migrations/'` = 0. The root cause is code (missing queue calls on two creation paths), not schema. The expand-only + senior-process machinery is therefore not invoked. (The issue's date-gate termination needs no migration either — the fix makes the loop produce rows through the existing tables.)
- **#2919 answered by #2908:** the 0-row monitoring subtree was the deliberate cleanup wipe, not silent data loss. Noted; not re-investigated.
- **Cross-links, not duplicates:** #3322 owns the fixture cohort + BET-1 ratio guards + the uninstalled digest-headline-ratio timer unit; #3176 is the first-brief-in-session feature (not built); #2778 remains latent/unproven; #2734 is the weekly catch-up path. None re-derived here.
- **Termination is a date-gate, not a block:** the prod proof (`npx wrangler d1 execute 0509 --remote --json --command "SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM watchlist_run) AS runs, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM watchlist WHERE created_at >= '2026-09-11T00:00:00Z') AS lists" | jq -e '.[0].results[0].runs > 0'`) lands at the **next Monday 03:00 UTC tick after deploy** — 2026-09-14T03:00Z if this PR lands and deploys before then, else 2026-09-21T03:00Z. The 09-11..13 cohort watchlists were created before this fix, so they ride the scheduled Monday slot; only watchlists created after deploy get the 5-minute first-scan queue. Deploy is not this PR's act.

## Plan — issue 3380 (manager lane, `.fleet/plan-3380.md`)

- [x] phase 1: (A1) wire the existing `queueFirstWatchlistScan` into the two watchlist-creation paths that lack it — smallest durable fix, no new machinery, no schema change. ## Summary

PR #3435 widened the 0509#3330 +x gate to every job in `deploy-production.yml` but tokenized each `run:` string after filtering it with `startsWith("./scripts/")`. A `run: |` block whose script invocation sits on line 2 or later escaped the +x check entirely. Hardening only — the live check in the issue found zero such lines today (all 8 `./scripts/` refs are single-line; the two multiline blocks use `node scripts/…`).

## Change

- New `collectDeployWorkflowScriptTokens` helper tokenizes per line (`run.split("\n")` then `line.split(/\s+/)`), so a `./scripts/…` token on any line of any `run:` block is caught.
- New `expectScriptExecutable` helper keeps the gate's exact exit-126 assertion message.
- New test: a parsed multiline `run: |` block with the invocation on line 2 yields the token, and the +x assertion fires with the exit-126 message for a non-executable file and passes for an executable one. Existing gate behavior on today's workflow is unchanged (same 5 tokens, all executable).

Verification:

- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/deploy-production-gate.test.ts` — 56/56 passed (55 existing + 1 new).
- Observe-to-close drill: appended a `run: |` step calling `./scripts/multiline-probe.sh` (chmod 644) on line 2 of the workflow, uncommitted — the gate FAILED with `./scripts/multiline-probe.sh lost its +x bit — the Actions checkout runs it as ./scripts/multiline-probe.sh and dies with exit 126 (0509#3330)` (the old net passed this drill silently). Drill files reverted, suite re-run green.
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` — 1 file, 56/56 passed.
- `sgscan --base origin/main` — no new security findings.

run-proof: test-only change; the runs above are the proof (changed-mode suite green before and after the drill revert, drill failure reproduced then closed).

net-positive-because: the gate's one job is to catch a lost +x bit before production does; without the per-line tokenizer a whole class of multiline run blocks passes the gate silently, so the net must get wider even though today's workflow adds no lines.

loose-ends: none — single-file test hardening, no product code touched.

Closes #3441

Delta only, per the disjoint-slice rule (diff: 6 files, +277/−6): this lane ships NO new connector, NO migration, NO shared-interface edit. The machinery already landed — the #3178 mention table + adapter interface, the #3375 `hn` connector (registration, dispatch, the 0100-era CHECK widen for `connector_id = 'hn'`), the #3205 /status "Tracked sources" catalog — and this branch extends exactly one note, one docblock, the tests, and the lane record:

1. **The capture proof** — `tests/integration/hn-mention-activation.integration.test.ts` (split out of `hn-mention-connector.integration.test.ts` at CI to satisfy the #2376 file-size ratchet — the describe had pushed it to 830 lines; the connector file is restored to its exact 678-line main shape), a new file of 2 its (23 total across the pair) on the real-D1 workers project (real workerd, the repo's real migrations): a seeded tracked brand's `source_target` (connector_id = `hn`) through the REAL data layer → `pollPresenceTarget` → `upsertPresenceItems` → `presence_item` rows. Fixture returns >=1 mention (the acceptance's "e2e fixture" clause, literally commented). Rate budget THROUGH the orchestration: exactly ONE courtesy `search_by_date` request per poll; two polls = two requests, never more. Canonical-URL dedup: every stored row's `url_hash` = `presenceUrlHash(canonicalUrl)` (the news.ycombinator.com item page — the link an HN mention is read at, not the story's external URL, which rides raw_json); the second poll — now carrying the persisted first-poll watermark, see reviewer-Act-on — still inserts 0 (the app-level url_hash + content_hash skip; the 0055 `UNIQUE (source_target_id, url_hash)` index remains the concurrent-write backstop). The #2992 LinkedIn slice (issue #3196): a tracked brand's LinkedIn ads, captured from the public LinkedIn Ad Library through the #2193 adapter already on main, surfaced on `/ads/:domain` and the watchlist competitor-detail (timelines/briefs) through the shared source-sections component, with an honest coverage note, a per-source capture-usage counter feeding a /status capture-failure rate, and a production kill flag. ## What ships

- **Kill flag `LINKEDIN_ADS_SOURCE_DISABLED`** (env.server.ts + wrangler.jsonc vars, `"0"` = the production posture): `requiresEnv` owns it (the #2193 `DECODO_SCRAPER_AUTH` requirement stays), so the registry's env filter drops the source from scheduled runs when killed — the run-path teeth, not a decorative variable; the /ads + /timeline sections omit through the same rule (`loadBrandPageSourceSnapshots` filters live sources by `requiresEnv`). Unset = on: an emergency brake, not a launch barrier.
- **Per-source capture-usage counters** (`app/lib/sources/linkedin-ads/linkedin-ads-usage.server.ts`, new, 117 lines): the #2181 KV budget-counter pattern — `linkedin_ads:captures:YYYY-MM-DD → {attempted, failed}` in the seam's DECODO_BUDGET namespace, 35d TTL, strictly best-effort (every KV step guarded; a counter hiccup never fails a capture). One counted attempt per Library READ, success or failure — the #2193 quota-deny returns before any read and is not counted — this is the /status capture-failure rate's denominator, because the seam's `source_snapshot` rows only ever record successes.
- **/status**: a Monitoring-health LinkedIn Ads (Ad Library) row — 24h attempts, failures, the capture failure rate when the #2181 KV binding is wired; the killed posture (no counters — a deliberately paused source has no meaningful failure rate, no fabricated 0%); the posture-only line when the binding is not wired (the #2200 rule: missing = no false claim).
- **The honest coverage note** on `/ads/:domain` (surface truth, corrected in the senior-review round: the note renders on /ads and the docs copy — the acceptance's two note surfaces; the watchlist competitor-detail shows the LinkedIn ads through its own #2193-era section `components/sources/linkedin-ads.tsx`, and briefs render no source sections — widening the note there is queued as #3430): source (the public LinkedIn Ad Library — no LinkedIn official-API key that bars commercial use), what is covered (the promoted-post cards currently published under the brand's account-owner name: promoted text, advertiser, public detail link) and what is not (spend, reach, audience metrics; no ad-format distinction), region (the United States — the public search's verified geo=US posture; no other regions), freshness (the weekly cadence; "Last checked" = the last successful capture). The section now renders the #2193 stored payload's REAL fields (promoted text, advertiser, public detail link) instead of the TikTok-shaped adId/firstSeen ghost reads. The docs coverage row's notes gain the same facts; its productionStatus stays `gated` — that is the PRESENCE connector's rollout, which this issue does not flip (the test pins it).

deploy: post_deploy_recovery_failed — the rollback safety net crashed after doing its job; 3rd occurrence 2026-09-13 (runs 34626446693, 34759554622, 34770115098). Resumed this unit's own salvage 8fcd1b252 (judge: resume, not restart), rebased onto current main 65776e216 (clean, 3 commits replayed), finished the acceptance: the 17:36Z failure replayed green + 9 readiness-gate tests moved to the recovered-release contract + lane evidence. This resume also wires the recovered live version into the on-main ledger row (mechanic 4's missing half, below).

The 17:36Z signature (run 34770115098, "Deploy" step, 17:36:42.657Z): the wrangler rollback printed SUCCESS and `Current Version ID: 515fb9d2…`, yet the spawn exited non-zero; the old script's `if (result.status !== 0) throw` fired AFTER the swap landed, the plan wrapper rethrew AggregateError `post_deploy_recovery_failed` (deploy-production-plan.mjs:809, cause = rollback-production.mjs:41:32), and the Deploy Worker job went red on a recovered release. The success-only chain (Worker secrets sync, release-evidence verify, on-main deploy ledger record) never ran, so which Worker version went live was recorded nowhere.

What the fix does — the success path exits 0, four mechanics, no new machinery:

1. Swap-confirmed-despite-non-zero-exit: the rollback spawn's stdout is piped and echoed; `interpretWorkerRollbackSpawn` (worker-rollback-target.mjs) treats wrangler's own final `Current Version ID: <chosen target>` marker as proof the swap landed — `rolled_back_although_spawn_exited_nonzero`, outcome ok.
2. Nothing-to-recover: when the resolved target IS the version the failed deploy already placed at 100% of traffic, the spawn is skipped, the live version recorded, exit 0.
3. The plan continues past a recovered release (stderr: `post_deploy_recovery_complete — <step> failed, last-green restored: <msg>`) so the later release checks and the workflow's success chain run; the AggregateError survives when the recovery itself fails.
4. Which version went live is now recorded — both halves: the recovered evidence (`recoveredLiveVersionId` + recovery outcome) is written back to the rollback-target evidence, and the on-main deploy ledger prefers the recovered live version over the deployed-then-rolled-back id. This resume completed the ledger half: `commit-deploy-ledger.sh` now passes `--rollback-evidence test-results/worker-rollback-target-*.json` (same nullglob pattern as the wrangler output; no file → no flag). Without it the ledger row would name the ROLLED-BACK FAILING version — and that row's version_id is exactly what `readLastGreenLedgerVersionId` anchors the NEXT rollback on, so the safety net would aim at the failing release. The guard is tested: an evidence file without a recovery outcome keeps the wrangler-output id.

## Summary

Closes the #3208 podcast slice of the mentions epic (#3171): a tracked brand or person gets mentions from podcasts (the show's own public RSS 2.0 feed, plus episode transcripts where the show publishes them in the public JSON transcript format) captured, deduped by canonical URL, behind a per-source kill flag, with the capture-validity gate applied, an honest coverage note, and the /status per-source row — pinned by proof, not asserted.

What this lane ships (the machinery, since #3178 landed the shared interface and mention table; #3178's ids/conventions extended, not edited):

1. **The connector** — `app/lib/presence-connectors/podcast.server.ts`: reads the tracked show's own public RSS 2.0 feed — the same syndication feed the publisher submits to Apple/Spotify, hosted by the publisher. Zero credentials, zero key, no platform mediation. Emits every episode as a candidate; the shared publication-feed mention-match step (`buildMentionStampPlan`, widened to the feed-target sources) stamps which entity phrase each episode names and filters the rest — the same split the rss publication feeds use. Transcripts where public: an episode's `<podcast:transcript>` tag (the Podcasting 2.0 namespace item-level tag, `url`+`type` required) is read when it exposes the JSON transcript shape (`segments[].text`) — at most 5 bounded transcript fetches per poll, spent newest-first, head-joined into the 280-char excerpt so a transcript-only phrase still matches; VTT/SRT/HTML/plain transcripts are recorded in `raw_json`, not yet fetched (the honest documented limit, stated in the /status note). Canonical episode URL: `<link>`, then an http(s) permalink `<guid>`, then the audio enclosure — never fabricated, never collapsed onto the feed URL; fragments and utm_*/fbclid/gclid tracking params stripped so `url_hash` dedupe survives re-polls. Every hop through `presenceSafeFetch` (SSRF + redirect re-validation, bounded bytes); conditional-GET via the stored `presence_poll_cursor` etag/lastModified.
2. **The kill flag** — `PRESENCE_PODCAST_ROLLOUT` (`disabled | internal | pilot | ga`; defaults `disabled` — ships dark; activation is a separate rollout decision). No credentials exist: the surface is keyless (`hasCredentials → true`, like hn).
3. **Registration + dispatch** — the connector registry registers it and the `pollPresenceTarget` dispatch passes the WHOLE target plus the stored cursor; coverage label `VERIFIED_PUBLIC_FEED` (the rss class).
4. **Coverage note + /status row** — what the public surface covers (the tracked show's own most recent ~25 episodes, self AND Competitor, no auth) and what it does not (there is no single free cross-show episode keyword search — Podcast Index surveyed, needs a free signup + API key, not adopted; other transcript formats recorded, not fetched), `productionStatus: "gated"`, surfaced on /status.
5. **The migration** — `migrations/0102_widen_source_target_connector_podcast.sql`: expands the `source_target.connector_id` CHECK with `'podcast'` (table-rebuild, the 0093/0098/0099/0100/0101 convention; child rows snapshotted to backup tables and restored inside the migration; backups self-cleaned). **Numbered 0102, not 0101**: the Pinterest slice (#3201) took 0101 first while this lane was between runs, so 0102's CHECK carries the full eleven-connector union — every value 0101's ten-connector CHECK accepted plus `'podcast'` — a strict superset, so whichever applied last, every row copies through. Expand-only: every previously-accepted value is still accepted, old code unaffected — rollback rolls back code, never data. ONE migration, ONE PR, one phase, ships dark — nothing to dual-write, backfill or switch; no follow-up migration phases exist for this slice.
6. **Tests** — `tests/integration/podcast-mention-connector.integration.test.ts`: validateTarget honesty (rejects non-podcast feeds, non-feeds, unreachable), the full poll→upsert→list capture path on real workerd + real D1 + the repo's real migrations, the transcript pass, the rate budget, the kill-flag capture-validity gate, episode-URL canonicalization, and the migration proof (write `connector_id='podcast'` through the widened CHECK, read it back, re-apply 0102 cleanly preserving child rows AND one seeded row per every non-podcast connector value the 0101 CHECK accepts — the ten-value order-proof, including pinterest).

## Collector survey (required research — searched + rejected, 2026-09-13, `gh search repos` + `npm`, cited in PLAN.md)

- **python-podcastindex** (26★), **SparrowTek/PodcastIndexKit** (11★), npm **podcastindex@1.2.0** — keyed-API bindings to the Podcast Index directory API. Rejected: needs a free signup + API key/secret, and each bypasses the SSRF-hardened `presenceSafeFetch` bounded-fetch path every 0509 connector rides.
- **Podcast-Standards-Project/PSP-1-Podcast-RSS-Specification** (113★) — a specification, not a collector. Rejected.
- **opawg/podcast-rss-useragents** (64★) — a dataset, not a collector. Rejected.
- **dado3212/apple-podcast-transcripts** (183★), **lord-denning/Huberman-Lab-Podcast-Transcripts** (267★) — static transcript dumps. Rejected: not collectors; also platform-scraped archives, not the show's own public surface.
