# Plan — issue #3385: two-way /compare/* route↔sitemap parity guard

Written by the manager from the stock planner's output (2026-09-13/14). One line per acceptance
bullet, grouped into 3 phases; each phase ends runnable and green. Manager ticks a box + commits
after each phase.

## Goal
Add a two-way, route-file-enumerated `/compare/*` ↔ sitemap parity guard to `tests/sitemap.server.test.ts`
(folding the #1878 hardcoded winners-list into the same enumeration), so the next compare page cannot
merge unlisted or unrouteable.

## Plan

**Phase 1 — derivation scaffolding + acceptance 1(a) leg (route → sitemap). Ends runnable and green.**

- [x] phase 1: acceptance 1(a) — every `compare.<slug>.tsx` / `$locale.compare.<slug>.tsx` under `app/routes/**` maps to a `ROOT_SITEMAP_STATIC_ENTRIES` path, except the 3 pinned #1481/#1548 losers, enumerated by walking the physical route files (never a second hand list)
  - Extend the existing import (line 2) to `import { readFileSync, readdirSync } from "node:fs";` — the file already imports `readFileSync`; do not add a second `node:fs` import.
  - Immediately after `collectRoutePatterns` and above `describe("SITEMAP_PATHS", ...)`, add:
    - `const COMPARE_SITEMAP_LOSERS: readonly string[] = ["/compare/visualping", "/compare/foreplay", "/compare/visualping-ad-library"];` — comment: the #1481/#1548 consolidation losers are live-200 route files deliberately ABSENT from the sitemap; this pinned exemption means a silent drop of a winner OR a silent re-add of a loser both fail. Plain `readonly string[]` (no `as const`) so `.includes(routePath)` typechecks against derived strings.
    - Two regex consts: `const EN_COMPARE_ROUTE_FILE = /^compare\..+\.tsx$/;` and `const LOCALE_COMPARE_ROUTE_FILE = /^\$locale\.compare\..+\.tsx$/;` (the precedent's shape — `.+` conveniently excludes the `compare.tsx` / `$locale.compare.tsx` index files).
    - `function compareRouteSlugsFromRouteFiles(filePattern: RegExp): string[]` — `readdirSync("app/routes")` → filter(filePattern) → for each name strip the trailing `.tsx` then the leading `compare.` / `$locale.compare.` → replace any remaining `.` in the captured slug with `/` (identity today; future-proof for dotted slugs) → `.sort()`. Comment: mirrors the house precedent in `tests/compare-structured-data.test.ts` (`compareRouteIds()`); Vitest runs from repo root so the relative `app/routes` path resolves. State the #3385 enumeration universe: `compare.<slug>.tsx` + `$locale.compare.<slug>.tsx` ONLY — `/compare/magicbrief` is NOT here: it is a 301 redirect (`app/routes/legacy-vendor-redirect.ts`, `LEGACY_VENDOR_COMPARE_PATH`, issue #2127) and stays out of the sitemap by design; do not "fix" it.
  - Inside `describe("SITEMAP_PATHS")`, immediately after the #2081 `it()` ("lists every live /switch/:slug page…", the pattern being mirrored), add ONE new `it()` for the (a) leg:
    - Derive inside the it: `const enSlugs = compareRouteSlugsFromRouteFiles(EN_COMPARE_ROUTE_FILE);` and `const localeSlugs = compareRouteSlugsFromRouteFiles(LOCALE_COMPARE_ROUTE_FILE);` (each it derives its own — no shared module state).
    - Non-vacuous guards (mandatory): `expect(enSlugs.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)`; `expect(enSlugs).toContain("sneakerping")` (acceptance 3's sentinel); `expect(localeSlugs).toEqual(enSlugs)` — pins the EN↔$locale families to the same slug set, so a #3302-style add of one family without the other fails.
    - Walk: `const xml = buildSitemapXml([]);` (the #2081 precedent — pin the rendered production XML, not just the list); `const rootPaths = ROOT_SITEMAP_STATIC_ENTRIES.map((e) => e.path);` for each slug, `const path = "/compare/" + slug;` if `COMPARE_SITEMAP_LOSERS.includes(path)` → `expect(rootPaths, "<path> (#1481/#1548 loser) unexpectedly registered").not.toContain(path)`; else → `expect(rootPaths, "<path> has a route file but no ROOT_SITEMAP_STATIC_ENTRIES path").toContain(path)` AND `expect(xml).toContain("<loc>https://0509.io" + path + "</loc>")`.
  - Run: `npx vitest run tests/sitemap.server.test.ts` — green, 1 new `it()`, expect-count net-positive, no existing expect touched.

**Phase 2 — acceptance 1(b) reverse leg + acceptance 3 pin. Ends runnable and green.**

- [x] phase 2: acceptance 1(b) + 3 — every registered `/compare/*` maps to a real route file (no #2866-style 404), and `/compare/sneakerping` passes both directions
  - Add ONE new `it()` for the (b) leg, directly after the (a) it:
    - `const filenames = new Set(readdirSync("app/routes"));`
    - `const compareEntries = ROOT_SITEMAP_STATIC_ENTRIES.filter((e) => e.path === "/compare" || e.path.startsWith("/compare/"));`
    - Guard: `expect(compareEntries.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` (kills the "all compare entries deleted → loop zero times" vacuousness; the >=10-loc #1878-termination it() independently floors the total).
    - Derivation-existence guard: `expect(filenames.has("compare.sneakerping.tsx"), "route walk found no compare.<slug>.tsx files — the walk, not the sitemap, is broken").toBe(true);`
    - For each entry: if `path === "/compare"` → expect BOTH `filenames.has("compare.tsx")` and `filenames.has("$locale.compare.tsx")`; else `const rest = path.slice("/compare/".length).replace(/\//g, ".")` → expect BOTH `filenames.has(`compare.${rest}.tsx`)` (message: "…is in the root sitemap but has no route file — the #2866 miss-class") AND `filenames.has(`$locale.compare.${rest}.tsx`)`.
  - Add ONE new `it()` for acceptance 3 — "/compare/sneakerping clears both parity directions (issue #3302 miss-class, #3385)":
    - expect `enSlugs` and `localeSlugs` (re-derived inside this it) each `.toContain("sneakerping")`; `expect(rootPaths).toContain("/compare/sneakerping")`; `expect(xml).toContain("<loc>https://0509.io/compare/sneakerping</loc>")`.
    - Comment: #3302 added `compare.sneakerping.tsx` + the `seo.ts` registration and touched NO test — this pins the repo-truth; the production 404 today is the #3166 deploy gap, NOT this defect — do not touch the deploy chain.
  - Run the ONE test command → green (3 new `it()`s total; still zero edits outside this file).

**Phase 3 — acceptance 2 (fold #1878) + acceptance 4 (contingency + verify). Ends runnable and green.**

- [x] phase 3: acceptance 2 + 4 — fold the #1878 winners-list into the shared enumeration; only if a leg failed, the one-line `seo.ts` fix; final verify
  - In the existing `it("keeps every indexable /compare/* winner in the sitemap (issue #1878)")` — title stays EXACTLY as-is:
    - Replace the hardcoded 9-path `compareWinners` literal with: `const compareWinners: readonly string[] = ["/compare", ...compareRouteSlugsFromRouteFiles(EN_COMPARE_ROUTE_FILE).filter((slug) => !COMPARE_SITEMAP_LOSERS.includes("/compare/" + slug)).map((slug) => "/compare/" + slug)];` — NO `as const` (a const-assertion on a computed `.map()` expression is a TS error). Update the it's leading comment: winners are now enumerated from the route files minus the pinned losers (issue #3385); the old hardcoded 9-path list stopped diverging silently as of #2866/#3092/#3302.
    - The loop body's two `expect()`s (`rootPaths` toContain + `ROOT_SITEMAP_STATIC_ENTRIES.find(...).toBeTruthy()`) survive verbatim — 9→15 iterations, strictly net-positive.
    - Keep both existing loser expects (`/compare/visualping`, `/compare/foreplay`) untouched, and ADD the third: `expect(rootPaths).not.toContain("/compare/visualping-ad-library");` with a #1548 comment (currently unasserted — this closes it, net-positive).
  - Acceptance 4 contingency (verified: parity already holds on bd41132f7, so expected no-op): only if a leg fails on current head, add the ONE missing `/compare/<slug>` line to `SITEMAP_PATHS` in `app/lib/seo.ts`, in this same PR, beside the other #2866/#3092/#3302 registrations — no route-file changes, no other `app/` behavior, no `.github/**`, no migrations, no new dependencies. Note: `app/lib/seo.ts` is not MANIFEST-managed, so no dated backup-sibling / actions.log duty. If any `it()`/`expect()` had to be removed or skipped (it should not be), add `test-removal-justified: <reason>` to the commit message.
  - Final verify, in order: `npx vitest run tests/sitemap.server.test.ts` (ONLY the touched file — no coverage, no typecheck, no `--maxWorkers`; respect the unit's `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS`; one heavy toolchain at a time) → paste the green summary. Then `curl -sSI https://0509.io/compare/sneakerping | head -1` — a 404 today is EXPECTED (the #3166 deploy gap; the test pins repo-truth so the next green deploy carries sneakerping). Do not touch the deploy chain.

## Files to Modify
- `tests/sitemap.server.test.ts` — extend the `node:fs` import with `readdirSync`; add `COMPARE_SITEMAP_LOSERS` + the two route-file regexes + `compareRouteSlugsFromRouteFiles()` (with the magicbrief-301 comment) at module scope above `describe("SITEMAP_PATHS")`; add 3 new `it()`s after the #2081 it ((a) route→sitemap, (b) sitemap→route, sneakerping both-directions); fold the #1878 `compareWinners` literal into the shared derivation and add the third loser expect.
- `app/lib/seo.ts` — contingency only (acceptance 4): at most ONE `/compare/<slug>` registration line in `SITEMAP_PATHS` if a parity leg fails on current head.

## Risks
- **Vacuous enumeration** — the mandated guard: the derivation must be asserted non-empty (sneakerping present in both slug sets, `compare.sneakerping.tsx` in the filename set, `compareEntries.length > 0`) or a broken `readdirSync`/regex walks nothing and the parity legs pass silently. A `readdirSync` ENOENT throws loudly, which is fine.
- **Non-recursive readdir** — the derivation reads `app/routes` only. If compare routes ever move into a subdirectory, the derivation under-counts and legs (b)+guards fail loudly; the fix is the derivation, not the routes.
- **#1878 it() edit fragility** — title must stay byte-identical; the 2 existing loser expects and the 2 loop-body expects must survive verbatim; no `as const` on the folded computed array. Expect-count lands strictly net-positive (gate-integrity counts assertions); any removal would need the `test-removal-justified` trailer.
- **TS const-assertion trap** — `as const` on the `.map()`-built winners array is a compile error; declare it `: readonly string[]`.
- **Loc casing** — `renderSitemapXml` lowercases `<loc>` paths; all compare slugs are already lowercase, so the `xml.toContain` assertions are case-safe today. If a future compare slug ever gains uppercase, that assertion (not the parity) is what catches it.
- **Test-run discipline** — only `npx vitest run tests/sitemap.server.test.ts`; never coverage/typecheck/`--maxWorkers`; respect `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS`; one heavy toolchain at a time (fleet-ops#4891). The `--reporter=dot` optional one-line form is allowed; note Vitest 4 removed the long `basic` spelling.
- **Scope creep** — the #1878-termination it(), the #2031 honesty it(), the #2081 it(), and `SITEMAP_PATHS` itself are adjacent; edit only what the phases name. Production 404 on `/compare/sneakerping` is the #3166 deploy gap — informational, not this defect.

## Manager ledger (fleet-ops#3274)

- 2026-09-14T03:35Z, phase 1: GREEN — `npx vitest run tests/sitemap.server.test.ts` = 90 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped at 4b149bea0 (salvage commit rebased onto origin/main cff30e908, zero conflicts; banked on origin claim/issue-3385). (a) leg + sneakerping sentinel + #1878-termination + #2081/#2031 it()s all pass → acceptance-4 contingency = no-op, parity already holds, no `app/lib/seo.ts` line needed.
- Amendment (one-line reason): phases 2+3 delegated to ONE fresh stock worker — same single file, adjacent hunks, and one senior review pass then covers both; their boxes tick together after the green run + review.
- 2026-09-14T03:46Z, phases 2+3: GREEN — worker run 92 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped (03:41:50 IST, 6.95s); manager re-run 92/92, VITEST-EXIT=0 (03:44:56 IST) at b0c9ad623. seo.ts untouched — acceptance-4 no-op confirmed live (production /compare/sneakerping = 200, #3166 gap closed; informational, deploy-side).
- Senior review (the ONE step-8 round; serves as the phase-2/3 review per the amendment above): litellm/senior (reviewer-3385) — 0 Critical, 0 Warnings. Adjudication: 2 Consider (223-char `compareWinners` chain line :1515; CWD-dependent `readdirSync("app/routes")` — both non-blocking, no CI gate, recorded here, NOT re-delegated), 2 Noted (commit-msg "+11 expect()" vs ~16 senior source-level count — substantive claim verified; non-recursive readdir if routes move subdir — pre-declared in Risks), 3 Dismissed-with-reason (loser-XML redundant via rootPaths; $locale walk twin closed three ways; regex over-match = the acceptance's intent). No Act-on → no fresh-worker retry.

Closes #3409

## Why

Both newest Deploy production runs died outside Gate C. Run 34779307565 passed deploy and health, then failed only the ledger step: `./scripts/commit-deploy-ledger.sh: Permission denied`, exit 126. Run 34780512552 died earlier, in the Test step: the #3215 no-time-bomb guard found a violating fixture file.

The exec bit is already fixed on main: `git ls-tree` shows 100644 at pin d0ddd3db and 100755 at c6adf8c11 — #3408 (issue #3330) landed the one-command mode fix at 21:24:04Z, #3410 (issue #3403) confirmed it. This PR carries the other fault: the fixtures.

## Scope

Two test files, eight added lines. No product code, no workflow, no migration.

- `tests/status.route.test.ts` — the #3394 (issue #3197) block added this file's only wall-clock read, `todayDayKey(now: Date = new Date())`. That one default parameter exposed all 56 pre-existing ISO echo fixtures to the guard: a file escapes only with no clock read, a pinned clock, or annotations on every literal. Fix: freeze the clock at test start — `vi.useFakeTimers({ now: new Date(Date.now()) })` in the existing beforeEach, `vi.useRealTimers()` in afterEach — the pinned-clock escape the guard's own failure message grants, and the same shape #3191 itself used (460802e1c, "pinned probe-test clock", where a file carried many fixtures). Test side and loader side then derive the same UTC day key, and the `Checked \d+ min ago` regex keeps its behavior, because the frozen now equals the real now at test start.
- `tests/integration/reddit-mention-connector.integration.test.ts` — one unannotated literal: `expect(first?.publishedAt).toBe("2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z")`. It is the serialization of `POST_A_CREATED_UTC` (epoch 1_767_225_600), asserted verbatim, never compared against the clock. It now carries `// fixed-date:`, the same precedent line 53 already sets for the epoch constant.

The guard test is untouched: no weakened assertion, no skip, no removal, no `|| true` (motive 1; Nish 2026-09-11).

## Blast Radius

Test-only. No runtime path changes, and the new hooks are file-scoped, so no other suite's timers move. At the rebase point (fabccdda8, post-#3410) the guard still reports both files, so the fix stays necessary. Main's Test step keeps failing on every push until this lands: that is the continuing cost.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/no-time-bomb-fixtures.test.ts tests/status.route.test.ts` — 2 files, 20 tests, all pass: guard green, full /status suite green under frozen timers (re-run after the final rebase onto cff30e908, whose +24 added test lines also pass under the freeze).
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project workers tests/integration/reddit-mention-connector.integration.test.ts` — 1 file, 17 tests, all pass on real workerd with the real D1 migrations.
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` — 19 tests, 1 file, pass.
- Before the fix, the same guard in the same worktree failed with exactly the two violations above: 1 literal in the integration test, 56 in status.route.test.ts.

Verification: guard test, full /status route suite, and the reddit-mention integration suite, each run to green locally after the fix.

## Review

One reviewer round, seat litellm/senior (agent reviewer-3397, the stock reviewer prompt with the senior model pinned). Findings: 0 Critical, 0 Warning, 1 Consider — adjudication: Consider — the frozen clock turns the 5s probe timeout in `app/lib/status-probes.server.ts:127-132` into a dead letter (the probe promise settles instantly today, so the race always resolves; recorded here, not acted on). The reviewer independently confirmed: both fixtures fixed the documented way, the guard untouched, the publishedAt/epoch serialization claim true, and no third violation on the moved main.

run-proof: Deploy production run 34780512552 (bd41132f7) failed its Test step with `expected [ Array(1) ] to deeply equal []`, and its successor 34783711074 (c6adf8c11, 21:36:18Z) failed the same step with `expected [ …(2) ] to deeply equal []` — the two violations this diff fixes, confirmed on the production runner. The same assertion passes against this branch's HEAD (20/20 node + 17/17 workers, outputs above). The next Deploy production run after this PR merges is the remaining proof: its Test step passes and deploy-ledger.jsonl gains a row — the ledger +x is already restored on main by #3408/#3410.

loose-ends: post-merge acceptance — a Deploy production run newer than 34780512552 must end success, deploy-ledger.jsonl gains a row, and https://0509.io/status shows that run's version. Not provable until the run exists; #3190 stays the green-run owner umbrella.

## Summary

Closes #3391 — the TTFB watch — by doing exactly what its second clause says: probe TTFB by route (cache HIT variance vs origin), then fix what the probe isolates. The watch FIRED (every post-18:01Z read stayed >1500ms: 1757→6269 at 20:43Z judge, and this lane's own 21:01Z probe reproduced 6268ms on the same VPS vantage), and the probe split the symptom into its two known halves:

1. **Origin side** — the #3319 placement bimodality (`local-` isolate 5.7-6.2s vs `remote-NRT` 1.8s), whose fix is already merged (#3394) and waiting on the 99h-no-green deploy (judge: `last_green_deploy=NONE-in-100`, 427 merges — #2897's jurisdiction, untouched here). Today's merges after 17:40Z are all mentions/coverage; nothing touched `/search`, and nothing could have: prod predates #3319.
2. **Cache-HIT side — the NEW half, and this PR** — `/search` was never in the #2950 anonymous public-HTML edge cache: not in `PUBLIC_CACHEABLE_HTML_PATHS`, and its document fails BOTH `isEdgeCacheableHtmlResponse` clauses (`no-store` stamp + the #1972 `set-cookie`). So while `/` answered 316-635ms from the edge, **100% of `/search` reads paid full origin, every time** — judge, measure, AEO crawler, first-touch human.

The fix: `/search` joins the existing #2950 edge cache — one allowlist path, one marker, one guard, zero new mechanisms.

- `"/search"` joins the Set that feeds BOTH the `public, s-maxage=3900, max-age=300` stamp and the edge-eligibility gate (the #3193 agreement rule stays true by construction); `cacheKeyUrl` already preserves the query, so `?q=`/`?website=` are distinct (path+query, country, version) keys — the nonce-free-variant machinery, HEAD handling and #3247 serve-stale + waitUntil refresh all apply unchanged. The #3308 arithmetic gives the judge's hourly probe a warm-or-stale-refresh read instead of another cold origin render.
- `EDGE_CACHE_ELIGIBLE_HEADER` (`x-0509-edge-cache-eligible`): the worker marks the renders the edge cache will own — ONE truth, the #2950 predicate; the loader reads a marker rather than re-deriving eligibility (no worker→app imports exist; the wiring test couples them).
- The #1972 fresh-anon mint is suppressed ONLY on marked renders, so the stored copy stays cookie-free. #1972's semantics survive: a cookieless read has no per-browser identity to persist, the IP backstop (`RL_SEARCH_IP`) still limits it, the BET-2 funnel polls `/search.data` (a different pathname — never edge-gated) and that poll still mints the cookie, and the first cold post-deploy read mints again. Signed-in/cookie-bearing reads keep today's behavior exactly.

Diff: `workers/edge-cache.ts` (+ the exported marker), `workers/app.ts` (mark the render), `workers/security-headers.ts` (+1 allowlist path), `app/routes/search.tsx` (guard the mint), 4 test files, the `.lane` evidence record, and this body. No `migrations/**` (nothing expand/contract, nothing follows), no wrangler/zone change, no placement change, no #3319 redo.

net-positive-because: every added line either implements one clause of the watch (probe receipts; the HIT side) or pins it — no mechanism, no wrapper, no abstraction; the machinery count is +0 organs, +0 units, +0 timers; this lane JOINS a shipped rail.

## Verification (final head, this lane)

- By-route probe (the watch's clause 1), 21:01-21:02Z, 6 spaced reads, judge's own vantage: `/` = cf-cache HIT ×3, 316-635ms; `/search?q=calendly.com` = NO cf-cache-status, `no-store`, TTFB 1856-6268ms, `cf-placement` `local-` on both slow reads vs `remote-NRT` on the fast one — my 6268ms total reproduces the judge's 20:43Z 6269. Inner loop: round 1 ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND (fresh worktree, no node_modules — `npm ci` fixed), round 2 the stale #2950 eligibility pin (`isEdgeCacheableHtmlRequest(/search)` expected `false`) updated to the new world with a personalised-`/status` exclusion guard, round 3 green.

- One suite at a time, `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2` respected, `--maxWorkers` never passed, no coverage, no typecheck locally (CI owns both; the PR's affected-tests round-trip is the typecheck).

The 20:43Z-21:02Z reads were re-measured live this hour rather than assumed.

## Summary

Closes the #3201 Pinterest slice of the mentions epic (#3171): a tracked brand or person gets mentions from Pinterest captured, deduped by canonical URL, behind a per-source kill flag, with the capture-validity gate applied, an honest coverage note, and the /status per-source row — pinned by proof, not asserted.

What this lane ships (the machinery, since #3178 landed the shared interface and mention table; #3178's ids/conventions extended, not edited):

1. **The connector** — `app/lib/presence-connectors/pinterest.server.ts`: reads the tracked profile's first-party public feed `https://www.pinterest.com/<handle>/feed.rss` (public RSS 2.0 — no key, no auth, undocumented; the same honesty posture as PLAN.md's Google News RSS row). Emits `presence_item` rows whose `canonicalUrl` is the public `pinterest.com/pin/<id>/` page (the feed `<guid>` doubles as `externalId`). ONE network hop through `presenceSafeFetch` (SSRF + redirect re-validation, `redirect: "manual"`); every URL re-validated via `normalizePublicHttpUrl` (the #3339 capture-validity precedent) — dropped, not compromised, on failure. Pinterest double-escapes its description HTML, so the connector re-strips after the shared parse (the shared `stripHtml` is idempotent on plain text — exported, not forked).
2. **The kill flag** — `PRESENCE_PINTEREST_ROLLOUT` (`disabled | internal | pilot | ga`; defaults `disabled` — ships dark; activation is a separate rollout decision). No credentials exist: the surface is keyless (`hasCredentials → true`, like hn).
3. **Registration + dispatch** — the connector registry registers it and the `pollPresenceTarget` dispatch passes the WHOLE target (the #3386 lesson), coverage label `VERIFIED_PUBLIC_FEED`.
4. **Coverage note** — what the public surface covers (the tracked profile's own most recent ~25 pins, self AND competitor, no auth) and what it does not (keyword-wide search, boards off-profile, repins/comments, engagement counts — those sit behind the approval-gated OAuth-per-user API v5, parked in PLAN.md at zero-spend), `productionStatus: "gated"`, surfaced on /status.

## Summary

Closes #2030. The 30 `$locale.*` buyer-surface routes have emitted their hreflang cluster for weeks, but it was one-way: every EN canonical — `/`, `/pricing`, `/search`, `/compare/*`, `/switch/*`, `/ads/:domain`, the guides — emitted ZERO hreflang, so per Google's localized-versions documentation ("annotations that are not reciprocal are ignored") the whole cluster was discarded, and `/sitemap.xml` carried no locale signal at all. This diff makes the EN side answer, and gives the sitemap the cluster.

- `app/lib/seo.ts` — `buyerSurfaceHreflangLinks(splat)` now opens with the `en` self leg (the canonical EN twin), so ONE call serves EN and `$locale` pages identically: `en` + de/ja/pt-br/fr/es + `x-default`→EN. The #2871 methodology quirk is preserved: for `splat="methodology"` the EN legs point at the deep `/methodology/ad-aggression-score` canonical, never the 301ing shallow path. New `sitemapHreflangAlternates(path)` maps any EN or locale path to its cluster — `undefined` when no live variant exists (the canonicalized-away compare losers, `/privacy`, the noindex `/ads` shells) — and `renderSitemapXml`, the SINGLE builder behind the root feed, every `/<locale>/sitemap.xml` and the no-D1 static fallback, now emits each cluster as `<xhtml:link rel="alternate">` children (`xmlns:xhtml` added to the urlset). Locale URLs ride as alternates, never as their own `<loc>`, so #1561's no-URL-listed-twice rule across the root and locale sitemaps survives untouched.
- `app/lib/locale-markets.ts` — `BUYER_SURFACE_GUIDE_PATHS`: the seven `/guides/*` paths as one source of truth for both the locale-sitemap set and the sitemap hreflang map; the #3122 triple-agreement test now reads both files, so the move cannot blind it. `app/lib/sitemap.server.ts` consumes it (the 7-entry literal it replaces is the same set).
- 34 route/component files — every EN route with `$locale` twins gained the same one-call spread in `links()`: `/` (via `marketing.tsx`), pricing, help, docs, api/docs, status, changelog, trust, compare, search, competitor-monitoring, capture-rules, methodology, all 13 canonical compare children (bigspy, minea, poweradspy joined via the salvage commits), the 7 guides, both switch surfaces via `switchPageLinks` (`app/components/switch-landing.tsx`), and `/ads/:domain` via its noindex-gated `meta()` which the `$locale` twin re-exports verbatim. The 40/40 `$locale.*` twins now meet their EN answers; the three canonicalized-away compare losers correctly stay silent, matching their twins' documented no-cluster rule.
- `tests/seo/hreflang-reciprocal-cluster.test.ts` (NEW, 272 lines) — EN route clusters across 9 surface families (incl. `/` and a representative of the five #2888/#3093/#3127 guides), pricing locale-twin parity, loser exclusion, /ads indexability gating, sitemap alternates on the root + locale feeds, the no-`<loc>`-for-locales guard, the sneaker 3-locale cluster (whose EN self already rode `SNEAKER_RESALE_MARKETS`'s `en` row), and the no-variant `undefined` paths.
- Existing pins aligned for the added `en` entry and the urlset `xmlns:xhtml`/alternates shape: locale-child-routes, locale-buyer-surface, locale-content-integrity, locale-first-value-routes, pricing, search, guides (incl. the #3122/#3167 source-of-truth reads), methodology/aggression, switch (incl. magicbrief), new-compare, compare-meta-ad-library, sitemap.server, search-qprefill-ssr, ad-aggression, the ads `loc`-scoped regex.

Branch note: the diff carries this issue's three salvage-`success/0` deaths as two `wip(salvage)` commits (the #2871 methodology EN legs, the bigspy/minea/poweradspy EN compare routes, the guides/switch-magicbrief pin alignments). The 2026-09-13T21:07Z unit completed the set: the five #2888/#3093/#3127 EN guides were the last one-way routes — fixed, pinned, and recorded with the full 40/40- twin verification in `.lane/reports/claim-issue-2030.md`.

Verification:
- Round 1 (salvaged state, pre-this-unit): `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → 392 files / 4724 tests, all passed.
- Round 2 (after the five-EN-guide fix): 391 passed / 1 failed — the 5 exact-equality `links()` pins in `tests/guides-routes.test.ts` went red; fixed by aligning them to the house pattern the two covered guides' own route tests already use (the `...buyerSurfaceHreflangLinks(...)` spread appended inside the expected array; the #3093 trio shares one loop, so one edit covered three failures).
- Round 3 (green): the same affected command → **392 files / 4725 tests, all passed**; scoped rerun `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/guides-routes.test.ts` → 38/38. Inner-loop rounds 1→3, cap 5, one fix round.
- `sgscan --base origin/main` → "No new security findings.", exit 0. `crgate --base origin/main` → exit 0 (the CLI's not-signed-in notice is informational; CI's CodeRabbit reviews this PR, and the judgement gate is the reviewer round below).
- Live baseline (pre-merge truth, not a production claim): `curl -sS https://0509.io/ | grep -c 'hreflang='` → 0 and `curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -c '/de/\|/ja/\|/pt-br/'` → 0 at 2026-09-13T21:07Z; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 8fab568f7 origin/main` → 1, i.e. the fix is NOT on origin/main — the issue's termination: counts (≥3 / ≥1) flip when this PR deploys.
- Suite scope: the node project affected-only, strictly sequential, `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2` respected, two test suites never in parallel. No `migrations/**` or `tests/integration/**` changes → no workers-project run. CI owns coverage + typecheck (fleet-ops#4891) — the PR CI round-trip is the typecheck.

run-proof: this PR adds no unit/timer/workflow; the proofs above are the run evidence — rounds 1–3 of the node `--changed` run (4724/4724 → 4720/4725 → **4725/4725**), the scoped guides 38/38, sgscan clean, crgate exit 0 — every command at final state exit 0, run in this unit on 0c02bdf62 = origin/main(522c79d4c) + this fix.

research: the official documentation this implementation mirrors (read before building, 2026-09-13): Google's localized-versions guidance — hreflang sets must be reciprocal and each URL self-references, or the annotations are ignored; the sitemaps.org 0.9 + Google sitemap-extensions pattern — `<xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="…">` inside each `<url>`, the mechanism the issue's "grouped with hreflang alternates" clause names. The one deliberate deviation — locale URLs as alternates instead of their own `<loc>` entries — is #1561's constraint (a URL must never be listed twice across the root and locale sitemaps), predates this issue, and is pinned by the reciprocal test's no-`<loc>`-for-locales guard.

help-first: no new bin/ file; existing organs — `buyerSurfaceHreflangLinks`/`sneakerResaleHreflangLinks` (app/lib/seo.ts), the single `renderSitemapXml` choke point, `BUYER_SURFACE_LOCALE_IDS`/`BUYER_SURFACE_PATHS`/`BUYER_SURFACE_CHILD_PATHS` plus the new `BUYER_SURFACE_GUIDE_PATHS` (a #2295-shaped constant the #3122 triple-agreement gate already reads), and the existing guides/switch/compare route shells around their `canonicalLinks()` calls. Nothing new was built.

net-positive-because: the mechanism is +1 leg in ONE function (the `en` self), +1 mapping function and one emitter loop in ONE builder (the sitemap alternates); 51 of the 56 changed files are the mechanical one-call route spreads (34) and their test/pin alignments (17). Zero new mechanisms, zero flags, zero scheduled units.

organ-heartbeat: no organ paths touched (56 files: 34 `app/routes/*`, 17 `tests/*`, `app/lib/seo.ts`, `app/lib/locale-markets.ts`, `app/lib/sitemap.server.ts`, `app/components/switch-landing.tsx`, `.lane/reports/claim-issue-2030.md`) — nothing scheduled added.

loose-ends: none — no flags, no gates, no rollout decisions; the only remaining state change is the deploy itself, after which the issue's termination: counts flip from the recorded 0/0 baseline to ≥3 / ≥1.

Closes #2030.

## Summary

Root cause (named, per the deliverable): two independent blockers, both proven.

1. **Gate C e2e — the 217-anchor reachability walk blows the 420s test budget.** #3396 (merged 18:44Z) raised the buttons/links budget 240s→420s, but the walk stayed *sequential*: 217+ unique anchors × 0.7–2.3s each ≈ 150–500s — over budget on the median under any load. Deploy run 34775660969 (sha 522c79d4, 18:46Z) died exactly there: `Test timeout of 420000ms exceeded` + `apiRequestContext.get: Request context disposed` (the mid-probe request disposed when the test timed out) + the /brands "Sport & footwear" 404, at `expectPublicGetTargetReachable` (spec:107-108). The .f9-wk-say 30s locator failure in the same run's "observed" block was flaky, not structural — it passed on the same run's retry and again in the 19:58Z production run and here.
2. **The deploy-ledger recorder lost its +x.** Every Deploy production run since #2975's bbccf182f (2026-09-12) exits 126 at "Record the deploy in the on-main ledger": `./scripts/commit-deploy-ledger.sh: Permission denied` — the script was created `100644` (all its workflow-called siblings are `100755`; verified via `git ls-files -s` across every recent deploy sha). Proven again on run 34779307565 (d0ddd3db, 19:58Z): that run's **Deploy, secrets, evidence AND the full e2e:prod:public leg PASSED (14 passed / 0 failed, 7.2m)**, then the ledger step 126'd. No Deploy production run on main can conclude success until the bit lands — this PR is that unblock.

## The fix (salvage-resume of unit pi-issue-0509-3403's proven work + one chmod; no assertion weakened, no test removed)

- `e2e/prod-public.spec.ts` (resumed salvaged work, prior unit died before shipping): (a) `settledProbeResponse` — a settled read giving propagation 3 attempts 1.5s/3s apart before the answer is trusted, absorbing version-flip 404s and disposed contexts; the final expectations are unchanged, so a really-gone target still fails exactly as before; (b) the 217-anchor walk runs in 6 lanes (just under the production `MONITORING_FANOUT_MAX_INFLIGHT=8` fanout guard) instead of sequentially — same targets, same assertions, ≈1/6 the phase.
- `scripts/commit-deploy-ledger.sh`: +x restored (100644→100755, `git update-index --chmod=+x`). One bit; nothing else.

## Verification

Real runs, this worktree @ 13bef7ac9 (the 24560c54f salvage, rebased zero-conflict onto main bd41132f7 — its last local prod-public run had already PASSED before the unit died) + the +x commit (`PLAYWRIGHT_WORKERS=1` respected — no `--maxWorkers` passed; one heavy toolchain at a time):

- `npm run e2e:prod:public` — the deploy's own failing command, exactly — → **EXIT 0, 14 passed / 3 skipped (pre-existing production skips by design) / 0 failed, 4.0m** against https://0509.io, including the previously-failing smoke (spec:360, its 217-anchor walk) and the flaky .f9-wk-say header-layout test (2.9s).
- Production A/B: the 19:58Z Deploy production run (34779307565, d0ddd3db — same spec, pre-fix) **passed the entire e2e:prod:public leg: 14 passed / 0 failed / 3 skipped, 7.2m, smoke 6.8m vs the 420s cap — 12s of margin**; it then 126'd at the ledger. The 20:21Z run (bd41132f) is the same story in flight (queued; its ledger step will 126 identically — bd41132f carries no fix).
- Coupling: `tests/search-display.test.ts` (readFileSync's the edited spec) → **37/37**.
- `sgscan` → "No new security findings" (exit 0).
- `crgate` → "CodeRabbit is not signed in on this machine" — the CLI said so, no local review ran (headless, no OAuth session; flagged, not explained away; the substantive review is the senior round below, as in #3396).
- Acceptance: the green Deploy production run on main = the run this merge triggers (deploy-gated, not claimed here — the +x is the last blocker on that leg: 19:58Z cleared Deploy+secrets+evidence+e2e and only the bitless ledger 126'd; this PR removes exactly that). The /brands "Sport & footwear" assertion is green, not retired — proven above against the same production target CI uses.

That is this issue's documented no-(free-)surface entry, the only exclusion the epic's termination allows: the flag stays off until the MONEY decision (#3255).

## Summary

The daily `ads-prog-seo-canary` went red on 2026-09-12 (run 34685896915): the sitemap grew to 127 `/ads/:domain` URLs and the test's back-to-back fetch burst outran the then-12/60s `RL_BRAND_PAGE` edge bucket, so the tail of the loop saw HTTP 429s. Fix, on the existing test and workflow only:

- Pace: 5s between /ads fetches (~11 req/min, under the smallest bucket this surface has ever had), no sleep before the first request. Today's limit is 60/60s (`app/lib/rate-limit.server.ts:80`), so the pace holds against any future tightening too.
- Retry: curl `--retry 4 --retry-delay 3` — curl >=7.71 treats 429/5xx as transient and honors the limiter's Retry-After, so a missed window waits exactly as long as the app asks.
- Redirects: `--location --max-redirs 4` + a printed note whenever the effective URL differs from the sitemap's. The issue's 301 investigation: the 9 listed URLs (zivame, snitch, kamaayurveda, dotandkey, thedermaco, newbalance, hoka, mailchimp, nykaa) were trailing-slash 301s onto the canonical non-trailing-slash forms and have all settled to 200 — the sitemap lists the right targets, so the canary asserts the FINAL landed page (what a search engine indexes) and prints, never fails, persistent-redirect drift.
- Workflow timeout 15 -> 30: the paced loop needs ~12-14 min, not the burst-era 15.

No assertion is weakened: every sampled URL is still fully fetched and noindex-asserted, the verdict lines are unchanged, and the note lines are additive. Acceptance bullet 2 resolved as "the redirects are intended and the canary follows them" (they were), plus the sitemap-side truth verified: it lists canonical non-redirecting URLs as of 2026-09-13.

Verification: `SEO_PARITY_SITE=https://0509.io SEO_PARITY_MAX_SAMPLE=300 bash tests/seo/sitemap-noindex-parity.test.sh` (the exact canary invocation) -> 127/127 `ok — ... is indexable (HTTP 200)`, final line `PASS — all sampled sitemap /ads URLs are indexable; the snapshot fixture matches the live cluster /ads set; /switch/magicbrief is a 200 MagicBrief page listed in the sitemap`, exit 0. Zero 429s and zero redirect notes in the run — all 9 issue-named URLs served 200 at their sitemap URLs. `sgscan` -> "No new security findings", exit 0. The diff touches one `.yml` and one `.sh`; no TS, no `migrations/**`.

run-proof: no new machinery — the touched workflow is the existing scheduled `ads-prog-seo-canary.yml` (M, not A; no new unit/timer/workflow). It triggers on workflow_dispatch + daily schedule only, so PR CI cannot run it; the proof of record is the local run above, which is byte-identical in command and env to the workflow's step (`SEO_PARITY_SITE=https://0509.io`, `SEO_PARITY_MAX_SAMPLE=300`, same script), exit 0.

organ-heartbeat: .github/workflows/ads-prog-seo-canary.yml — not-an-organ: existing 0509 product scheduled canary, not a fleet-ops organ; no new timers or schedules, only its step script and its own timeout.

net-positive-because: the issue's two acceptance bullets each need lines that did not exist — the 429 defenses (pace + Retry-After-honoring retry) and the redirect handling (follow + printed drift note); the +36 lines are those two defenses, their rationale comments, the 15->30 timeout, and the synced comment math. Nothing speculative.

loose-ends: ads-canary-3278 — (1) the workflow has no PR trigger, so the final green is the next scheduled daily run after this merges; the worker token has no Workflows scope and cannot dispatch it. (2) By design the redirect note prints but never fails: if a sitemap URL starts redirecting again, the canary stays green and the note surfaces the drift for a follow-up.

Closes #3278

Reviewer round (seat reviewer-senior = nebius/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash, resolved via the stock seat lookup `find_senior_seat` after `bin/fleet-review-arm-check` exit 0; senior ladder reported exhausted/walled, the lookup's documented capable-seat fallback; one round, verdict: merge as-is, nothing must change):
- Act on: none.
- Consider: (1) a persistent 301 from a sitemap `<loc>` only prints a note and passes green — the issue allows exactly this; failing on a sitemap-listed redirect would be a later policy tightening, already disclosed in loose-ends (2). (2) if the RL_BRAND_PAGE binding ever vanished, the limiter fails closed with 429 + Retry-After: 60, so retries would burn ~4-5 min/URL and the job dies slow-red on the 30-min timeout — correct (a canary must never go false-green), just slow; no action.
- Noted: the reviewer verified Retry-After honor by direct measurement (loopback server, curl waits the announced 10s over the shorter --retry-delay) and confirmed the sitemap lists canonical non-trailing-slash URLs (app/lib/sitemap.server.ts:407) and that pace ~11 req/min sits under both the 60/60s and the historical 12/60s bucket.
- Dismissed-with-reason: none — no finding failed to land in a bucket.


Salvage resume (unit pi-issue-0509-3278, 2026-09-13, next session of the same unit): the prior session opened this PR, posted this body, and died before the attest+arm. This session re-verified everything end-to-end: the exact canary invocation above -> 127/127 "ok — ... is indexable (HTTP 200)", 0 FAIL, 0 HTTP 429, 0 redirect notes, final PASS, exit 0. Lockfile-only Dependabot PRs failed `gate-integrity` ("weakens a quality gate without the required justification") while touching nothing test- or workflow-related. Dependency security updates could not land. This fixes the scan, narrowed — never relaxed, never disabled, no attest bypass for Dependabot.

Closes #1947

## What shipped

- `.github/scripts/gate-integrity.sh` (+25): a `LOCKFILE_PATH` rule (`package-lock.json` | `pnpm-lock.yaml` | `yarn.lock`) that `continue`s past the CONTENT scan only. Filename-level test/gate checks still run: a test renamed to a lockfile name is still caught (pinned by fixture), a gate path edited through one is still caught. Nothing else relaxed.
- `.github/scripts/test-gate-integrity.sh` (+52): 5 new fixtures pinning the exclusion.
- `.lane/reports/claim-issue-1947.md` (+27): lane-unique evidence record for this branch, per the repo lane convention.

Why exclusion instead of anchoring patterns: a Dependabot bump rewrites machine-generated version/integrity text; whether any given bump's bytes happen to resemble a skip marker or an assertion (`@babel/helper-skip-transparent-expression-wrappers`, `"integrity": "sha512-..."`) depends on the dependency graph, not on the PR. Excluding the three lockfile paths from the content scan up front makes the whole class structurally immune regardless of how the content patterns evolve — which is the narrowest possible statement of "machine-generated manifests are not gate-weakening signal".

## Verification

Real runs, this worktree, 2026-09-13. Base = origin/main 271a90d87 (the 2 gate files are byte-identical on it to this PR's parent).

- Fails before: today's main's `gate-integrity.sh` run against the new fixture suite — `83 passed, 1 failed`. The one failure is exactly the reported class:
  ```
  FAIL lockfile_pnpm_ci_softener: expected PASS, got rc=1
     | FAIL: this pull request weakens a quality gate without the required justification
     |   - CI step softened in pnpm-lock.yaml: || true
  ```
  A lockfile-only diff (a Dependabot `pnpm-lock.yaml` bump) fails today's gate because the CI_SOFTENER content rule scans every `.yml`/`.yaml` — lockfiles included. That is the one reproducible false positive, proven, not inferred.
- Passes after: the fixed script against the FULL suite (all pre-existing fixtures plus the 5 new) — `84 passed, 0 failed`, exit 0.
- #1579's exact 3-line diff is pinned as `lockfile_only_bump` — PASS after. Honest note: that exact diff also passes on today's main's script, because the 2026-09-08 failures the issue cites were actually the jq E2BIG context-step crash (0509#2516, fixed on main 2026-09-10, 310fa5c70). So no #1579-exact fixture can fail-before — the fails-before property of the lockfile-only class is proven by the pnpm fixture above, which is the live false positive. Both shapes are pinned.
- Negative fixture still blocks (required by the issue, pinned twice):
  - `lockfile_negative_control`: a real `it.skip(` in `tests/auth.test.ts` with no `test-removal-justified:` trailer → FAIL `test disabled in tests/auth.test.ts` — behaves as pinned in both the 83/1 and 84/0 runs.
  - `lockfile_rename_bypass`: a test renamed to `package-lock.json` → FAIL `test file renamed out of the suite: tests/auth.test.ts -> package-lock.json` — proves the exclusion did not weaken filename-level suite integrity.
- sgscan: `No new security findings.` rc=0.
- No attest posted by this PR and none needed by this change; attest discipline unchanged.

## The three Dependabot PRs (accept — no code change of their own)

Live truth via `gh pr view`, 2026-09-13:

| PR | State today | gate-integrity | Note |
|----|----|----|----|
| #1579 | MERGED 2026-09-11T17:25:32Z | (landed) | Went green once 0509#2516's crash fix landed; merged with no code change of its own. |
| #1543 | CLOSED (superseded) | SUCCESS (last verdict) | Dependabot closed it; the class it represents is now pinned by `lockfile_skip_like_text`, so a re-PR of the same bump passes by construction. |
| #1589 | OPEN | **SUCCESS** | Its remaining BLOCKED verdicts are `codex-node-checks` FAILURE and `preview-assert` FAILURE — different checks, outside this issue's scope. |

`gh pr checks` on this PR after merge: every future lockfile-only diff reads the 84/0 suite from base, so the class this issue reports cannot recur.

## Machinery accounting

net-positive-because: the issue's Required demands both the narrowed exclusion AND a fails-before/passes-after fixture AND a still-failing negative control — the +25 (exclusion), +52 (the pins that make the narrowing provable), +27 (lane-unique evidence record) are exactly those deliverables; there is no smaller shape that satisfies the Required section, and 79 pre-existing fixtures are untouched (zero renamed, zero skipped, zero deleted).

organ-heartbeat: .github/scripts/gate-integrity.sh not-an-organ: CI gate decision script, not a registered fleet organ (no systemd unit/timer, not in the organ registry)
organ-heartbeat: .github/scripts/test-gate-integrity.sh not-an-organ: fixture regression for a CI script, not a registered organ
organ-heartbeat: .lane/reports/claim-issue-1947.md not-an-organ: lane evidence record, not machinery

## Gate-owned paths

This diff touches gate-owned paths: `.github/scripts/gate-integrity.sh` and `.github/scripts/test-gate-integrity.sh`, both inside the workflow's `gate_globs` (`.github/scripts/**`). Per the handoff rule the admin attestation is the orchestrator's job, so this PR carries an `attest-requested: <head sha>` comment and no self-attestation.

loose-ends: #1589 stays BLOCKED on codex-node-checks + preview-assert failures — different checks with their own issues; this PR does not pretend to fix them
loose-ends: #1543 was CLOSED unmerged (browserslist 4.28.1 -> 4.28.8); its last gate-integrity read SUCCESS, so the bump can be re-PRd by Dependabot and will pass — noted here so the security bump is not silently lost

run-proof: fixture regression 84/0 exit 0, fails-before 83/1, negative controls still FAIL — bash .github/scripts/test-gate-integrity.sh (this worktree, 2026-09-13)


## Reviewer round (product repo; senior reviewer, one round, no loops)

Seat: nebius/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash — the 0509 repo's committed project-local reviewer (`.pi/agents/reviewer.md`), independent of the authoring seat (worker-class); senior-seat availability proven first (`find_senior_seat` → exit 0). Same convention as the #3360 precedent. Ran AFTER this head's predecessor, its 2 Consider fixes are the final commit 82dd9d1b2 (each 1 line, line-count neutral — the +25/+52/+27 and +104 counts above remain exact).

Findings: 0 Critical, 0 Warnings, 3 Suggestions. Adjudication, every finding in exactly one bucket:
- Act on: none.
- Consider, fixed (82dd9d1b2): (1) the fixture-suite comment overstated the fails-before scope — only `lockfile_pnpm_ci_softener` is fails-before (pnpm-lock.yaml is `.yml`, the only lockfile the pre-PR scan touched; package-lock.json/yarn.lock content was never scanned); (2) the lane evidence record's base hash was stale (f026d4248 → 271a90d87, the actual diff base).
- Noted: 21 of the 25 added gate-script lines are comment — left as-is, no defect; the density helps future gate readers.
- Dismissed-with-reason: none.

Reviewer's leak-analysis (Noted, no action): the early-continue sits AFTER every filename-level check (test deleted / renamed out / gate-owned changed / gate-owner renamed), so a test or workflow co-committed with a lockfile still gets its own full scan; `TEST_PATH` and `LOCKFILE_PATH` endings are mutually exclusive; the ratchet continues-skip is dead surface (ratchet globs can never match a lockfile); the +52 test diff is purely additive, all 84 `run_fixture` calls intact, both negative controls still FAIL.

Post-reviewer-round gates (true exit codes, this worktree @ 82dd9d1b2):
- fixture suite re-run: 84 passed, 0 failed, exit 0
- sgscan: exit 0, "No new security findings."
- crgate: true exit 3 — CodeRabbit not signed in on this box (named; 0509 repo-side CodeRabbit auto-review is disabled — the senior reviewer round above is the substantive review); same disclosure as #3371

fix(auto-revert): close-halts-on-green under GITHUB_TOKEN, GraphQL-assert, closes by label AND title (0509#2929)

Fixes the surviving half of #2929 after #3220 (bdd56cfca) deleted the filing half.

The 2026-09-11 red-main streak filed 104 AUTO-REVERT HALT issues with ZERO labels (root cause, 11:03Z run 34592177395: the fine-grained AUTO_REVERT_PAT cannot run the GraphQL calls gh's issue comment/label-resolution paths need). #3220 stopped the filing at the source — a halt is now a step-summary warning, and the FleetProductionStale alert (fleet-ops#5785) owns the condition — so the judge-endorsed label-ensure now guards a mechanism that no longer files. What survived #3220 is close-halts-on-green, and it still carried every #2929 class:

- it ran under AUTO_REVERT_PAT, and the workflow's permissions block grants only its listed permissions — without `issues: write` the GITHUB_TOKEN side cannot even list (the silent "closed 0" class).
- it closed ONLY by label, so an unlabelled halt survivor could never be found (#2929 consequence 2).
- a `for` over `$(gh issue list ...)` masks a failing query as an empty list: no GraphQL assert, "closed 0" forever.

## Changes (2 files, +149/−3)

- closer runs under GITHUB_TOKEN (`github.token`); `issues: write` granted explicitly in the permissions block — once any permission is granted, the rest default to none.
- GraphQL access asserted BEFORE listing; a dead token is a FATAL, never a masked empty list.
- close set = label list UNION title search. Every halt title begins "AUTO-REVERT HALT:", so the search candidates are narrowed by a startswith("AUTO-REVERT HALT:") filter — #3364 ("auto-revert: delete close-halts-on-green once the AUTO-REVERT HALT backlog is 0") is found by the search but correctly spared.
- EACH source is its own `v=$(gh …)` assignment BEFORE the loop (review round 1, Act on, 0509#2929): under bash 5.2 `inherit_errexit` is off, so a `{ gh; gh; } | sort -u` group's status is its LAST command — a failed label list beside a successful title search would report success and silently close a partial set (verified: `{ false; echo 42; } | sort -u` assigns 42 and survives). A bare assignment's exit status IS its substitution's, so any source failure dies at the assignment, before the loop closes anything. The union joins the two captures via `printf | sort -u` into `candidates`.

## Mechanics-read vs the issue's Do bullets

The judge endorsed the #3013 spec (2026-09-12); #3220 then superseded the mechanism it targeted.

- "after `gh issue create`, verify the label … same guard on the comment/dedupe path": #3220 removed the create — zero filings means zero labels to drop; the endorsed guard survives here as the closer's GraphQL-assert + label-AND-title close. Bullet satisfied by supersession plus this diff.
- "Collapse the duplicates: one open halt per red streak; the dedupe must key on the label AND fall back to a title search": the filing side is #3220 (no new floods, nothing to dedupe); the closer side is this PR (label AND title).
- "Test in tests/ … assert the create step is followed by the label verification": the create no longer exists; 4 new its (8 → 12) assert what does: GITHUB_TOKEN + issues:write, GraphQL-assert-before-listing, label+title+startswith+sort-union, and the freshness drill ("main moved after the red commit" records itself loud — step summary + ::warning — and exits 0 without filing an issue).

## Verification

- 12/12 tests in tests/auto-revert-workflow.test.ts on BOTH heads: 9082ea160 (277ms, 21:30:33Z) and fe8f2f97 post-Act-on (285ms, 21:57:51Z); targeted vitest run, no coverage, no typecheck — CI owns the full suite; VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2 respected.
- Review-round Act-on re-proven live, this unit 2026-09-13T21:52Z: the EXACT new capture trio (two assignments + printf|sort -u) against this repo → labelled 68, title-prefixed 67, union 68 — the sources genuinely differ by one issue TODAY (a labelled halt whose title lost the "AUTO-REVERT HALT:" prefix would have been missed by label-only OR title-only closing); #3364 correctly NOT in the set. bash -n on the extracted closer script: SYNTAX OK.
- 36 earlier halts were closed by this same closer on the 2026-09-12 08:04Z green (#2909/#2917/#2923, 2s-apart close stamps) — the mechanism this PR hardens, proven in production.
- Run 34761479156 (14:01:51Z, red deploy, head 9082ea160): close-halts-on-green correctly skipped; the halt recorded itself as step summary + ::warning, no issue filed (#3220 design, working as shipped).

run-proof: single unit pi-issue-0509-2929 on issue 0509#2929; targeted vitest 12/12 on final head fe8f2f97 (21:57:51Z, 285ms) and pre-fix 9082ea160 (21:30:33Z, 277ms); the live 68/67/68 union + #3364-exclusion + bash -n proof (21:52Z); the 2026-09-12 08:04Z green closer (36 closes) and skipped-closer run 34761479156; PR CI (preview-assert) is the workflow round-trip; no timers involved.

net-positive-because: the closer's four silent-failure classes (PAT token, missing issues:write, label-only close, masked substitution) each become machinery that fails loud or falls back — +149/−3 across exactly 2 files, no test removed (8 → 12 its; the round-1 Act-on strengthened 2 of them).

organ-heartbeat: .github/workflows/auto-revert.yml not-an-organ: gate verdict "SKIP: no fleet organ touched in the diff" — it is a repo workflow, not a registered fleet organ; no absent() owed.

loose-ends: auto-revert-halt-backlog — 68 halts still open; they drain on the next green Deploy production via the closer this PR hardens (needs a green-main trigger, machine-side). Plus the gate-integrity-attest for the head sha (gate-owned path: .github/workflows/auto-revert.yml) — attest-requested posted for fe8f2f976991336d0772a9261d140dadaa5395fa, judge queue.

## Review adjudication (one round, 0509#2929)

Reviewer: senior seat cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high — first usable of senior_seats_in_order (#3121; seat_usable re-verified this run) — via the reviewer-issue-2929 agent, so the worker's own seat was not used.

- Act on — the `{ gh; gh; } | sort -u` compound masks a failed label list (group's status is its LAST command, bash 5.2 `inherit_errexit` off; reviewer reproduced `{ false; echo 42; } | sort -u` → 42, step survives): FIXED in fe8f2f97 — two bare `v=$(gh …)` assignments, printf|sort -u union; any source failure now dies at the assignment.
- Act on — the test pinned `candidates="$({`, locking the masked shape: FIXED in the same commit — pins both captures + the printf-union and asserts the brace-group shape is gone.
- Dismissed-with-reason — scope `issues: write` to the closer job only: zero privilege delta (the workflow still grants contents/pull-requests/actions workflow-wide), one more permissions block, and the permission test pins the workflow level. Recorded, no code change.
- Dismissed-with-reason — replace the `viewer { login }` probe with a 1-item issue list: the observed 2026-09-11 failure WAS the GraphQL class (403 addComment), and the permission grant is pinned by the YAML test — the reviewer's own wording: "The YAML permission test is the real check". Recorded, no code change.
- Noted — the freshness drill asserts the #3220 loud-halt YAML contract (GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY + ::warning, exit 0, no filing), not an executed bash simulation; reviewer: "fine for this file".
- Noted — pre-existing stale "files an issue via gh issue create" phrasing in test names/comments (:48/:115); a later pass.

## Test plan

- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/auto-revert-workflow.test.ts` (12/12, 285ms, on final head)
- PR checks: preview-assert, semgrep, gitleaks, actionlint; gate-integrity covers the gate-owned workflow path (attest via the orchestrator, see loose-ends)

Closes #2929

- Issue termination: the four route greps (`og:image.*/social-card/`) and the `briefs/weekly.png → image/png` clause are locked by the sweep + alias assertions; the production half turns green after the next 0509 deploy (deploy-gated, not claimed here — the undeployed-#3371 receipts and the 404s are recorded in `.lane/reports/claim-issue-3383.md`).

Closes #3268

**Fault:** every merged-batch push to main fails 'Tighten design-system ratchet ceilings' at the 'Verify pinned main checkout' step — `gh run list --workflow 'Ratchet auto-tighten' --limit 5` reads 5/5 `completed/failure` (34741508247, 34741426531, 34740969267, 34740749015, 34738857809), each dying with `expected the main branch to be checked out, got: HEAD`.

**Why:** the checkout pins `ref: ${{ github.sha }}`, so HEAD is always detached and `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` prints `HEAD`. The guard's branch-name assert can never pass on any trigger — every merge batch and main look red, which masks real ratchet regressions.

**What:** the guard is now event-aware, the issue's "verify against github.sha instead of the branch name" option:

- Keeps `test "$HEAD_REF" = "refs/heads/main"` — the event's-ref assert for the schedule/dispatch path, as the issue requires.
- Replaces the branch probe with `git merge-base --is-ancestor "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" origin/main`. `origin/main` is guaranteed locally: the checkout runs `fetch-depth: 0`, which fetches all refs including `refs/remotes/origin/*`, and `persist-credentials: false` means a second network round-trip could not authenticate on this private repo — so the remote-tracking ref is the only witness. The property asserted is the event-aware one the issue asks for: the tightened tree belongs to main's history.

**Mechanism (fleet-ops#366):** `tests/ratchet-auto-tighten-guard.test.ts` is the detector — asserts the guard step never re-asserts a branch name, keeps the event-ref assert, resolves `origin/main` from the checkout's own history (no second `git fetch`).

**Verification:**

```
$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/ratchet-auto-tighten-guard.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Duration  176ms
```

- A/B at the runner's exact state (detached HEAD at main's tip b1e76ca06): old guard → `expected the main branch to be checked out, got: HEAD` (exit 1); new guard → PASS (`merge-base --is-ancestor` true); event-ref assert → PASS.
- Workflow YAML re-parsed; both guard lines present in the parsed step.

**run-proof:** workflow 'Ratchet auto-tighten' — run 34741508247 (and the four before it) is the failing end-to-end proof of the fault. Post-merge, the next push-to-main batch must show the job green: `gh run list --workflow 'Ratchet auto-tighten' --limit 3` no longer all-failure.

net-positive-because: +63/-8 — one fixed guard plus the regression detector that keeps it event-aware; every changed line is the assert itself or its detector.

organ-heartbeat: .github/workflows/ratchet-auto-tighten.yml not-an-organ: 0509 CI workflow, not a registered machine organ.

loose-ends: ratchet-3268-postmerge-green-check — after this lands, the next merge-queue batch's 'Tighten design-system ratchet ceilings' run must be green (or legitimately tightening).

Deploy-impact: none — CI-only (one workflow + one vitest guard); no production code touched.

Vitest 4.1.11 dropped the built-in `basic` reporter. Every issue verify/termination line written as `npx vitest run <file> --reporter=basic` now Startup-Errors before a single test runs — and each affected pickup burns a cycle rediscovering it (the fifth #3302 pickup documented the cause; the sixth re-hit it because the issue text still said `--reporter=basic`). This PR lands the deletion-first fix: the convention goes bare, a detector keeps it there, the two affected issues are swept, and the generator question is answered with a probe receipt.

## Convention (acceptance 1) — (a), no shim

Issue verify/termination vitest lines run bare — `npx vitest run <path>` — or with `--reporter=dot` for a one-line summary. Recorded once, in the instruction entrypoint every pickup reads: `AGENTS.md` → new "## Test conventions". Option (b), a vitest-config `basic` shim, would add a mechanism where a convention suffices; the issue itself calls (a) fewer mechanisms, and this diff ships zero lines of vitest config.

## What changed (3 files, +124)

- `AGENTS.md` — the 4-line "## Test conventions" section: the bare/`--reporter=dot` rule, why (vitest 4 dropped `basic`), the guard-test pointer. Written so the literal flag appears nowhere in the tracked convention surfaces — exactly what the detector asserts.
- `tests/vitest-reporter-convention.test.ts` (NEW) — the detector: `AGENTS.md` + every text file under `.github/` must contain zero `--reporter=basic`, failing with a message that names the bare form and this issue. `docs/**` deliberately not scanned (historical records, not the convention). Runs in CI's node project (`tests/**/*.test.ts`); does not leak into the workers project (integration glob only).
- `.lane/reports/claim-issue-3370.md` (NEW) — this unit's lane evidence record, lane-unique path per the standing convention.

Not changed: no vitest config (no shim — acceptance 1(a)), no `.github/**` workflow (no new organ), no `migrations/**`, no production file. Every hunk is additive; no test removed or weakened.

organ-heartbeat: (none) not-an-organ: this diff touches no registered organ — AGENTS.md, one vitest test, one lane record; `fleet-organ-heartbeat-check gate` exits 0 on this diff (receipt below).

## Sweep (acceptance 2) — fixed where the written commands live

The issue bodies were edited on GitHub (the issues are documents; the written commands live there, so that is where "the written command actually passes" is fixed):

- #2873 (OPEN): body now carries 0 occurrences of `--reporter=basic`; its termination line reads `npx vitest run tests/capture-validity` — witnessed passing, 5 files / 63 tests, exit 0, this run.
- #3302 (OPEN at claim time; CLOSED since by #3365's merge): body 0 occurrences; termination line `npx vitest run tests/compare-sneakerping.route.test.ts` — witnessed exit 0 this run.

## Generator (acceptance 3) — the conditional resolves to NO

`rg -F "reporter=basic"`, unpiped:

- 0509 tracked+untracked tree (`--hidden`, excl. node_modules/var/lock): matches ONLY the detector itself (it must name the literal to assert it) and the historical `.lane/reports/claim-issue-3302.md` record — neither is a generator.
- fleet-ops deploy clone (read-only, where the scout/intake machinery lives): no match, exit 1 (no-match probe).
- vault `_system` (read-only): no match, exit 1 (no-match probe).

No tracked mechanism stamps the flag into new issues today; the occurrences were scout-drafted issue text (#2873, #3302), both swept. New pickups learn the convention from AGENTS.md, which the detector pins. The reviewer independently strengthened this premise: `scripts/ci-vitest-run.sh` — the wrapper CI actually runs vitest through (`ci.yml:111-117`) — contains no `reporter` string at all.

## Verification

```
npx vitest run tests/compare-sneakerping.route.test.ts --reporter=basic --maxWorkers=2
  → exit 1, Startup Error: Failed to load custom Reporter from basic /
    [cause] Failed to load url basic — the issue's error, verbatim (the bug, expected)
npx vitest run tests/compare-sneakerping.route.test.ts --maxWorkers=2   # #3302's termination, as now written
  → exit 0
npx vitest run tests/capture-validity --maxWorkers=2                    # #2873's termination, as now written
  → 5 passed (5) files / 63 passed (63) tests, exit 0
npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main   # affected-tests, the blessed form
  → 1 passed (1) — the new detector, exit 0
sgscan (3 touched files) → No new security findings, exit 0
crgate → "Non-interactive environment detected. Use --api-key for authentication", exit 1 — the known
  signed-out state, named not papered over (coderabbit auth login is the one-time interactive step;
  GitHub-side CodeRabbit reviews this PR)
```

Coverage/typecheck were not run locally — CI owns them (fleet-ops#4891). `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=2` respected; no two suites in parallel. One inner-loop round, all green; the only exit-1s are the expected bug repro and the named crgate state.

run-proof: unit pi-issue-0509-3370 — vitest 4.1.11: flag repro exit 1 (Startup Error, the bug, verbatim), #3302's written termination exit 0, #2873's written termination 5 files / 63 tests exit 0, affected-tests (node, `--changed origin/main`) 1/1 exit 0, sgscan exit 0; witnessed 2026-09-13 on head 5c5f7e8cb.

net-positive-because: the convention is fewer mechanisms, not more — zero lines of vitest config (no shim), zero new workflows; the only machinery added is one detector test inside the existing vitest rail, and the sweep deletes flag occurrences from two issue bodies. Rollback (issue: "convention-note only, or a one-key vitest config shim; no data, no gates") is a single revert.

loose-ends: vitest-reporter-convention

- #2873 stays OPEN (blocked-on: orchestrator since its 09-11 verification) — this unit only fixed its verify/termination lines; its own scope was already satisfied on main.
- #3302 closed mid-task (by #3365's merge); its sweep still landed (body 0 occurrences) — closed-and-swept, better than open-and-lying.
- Two Consider findings from the reviewer round (below) are recorded, deliberately not churned: the reviewer judged both safe to defer to a future round.
- crgate stays unrun until Nish's one-time `coderabbit auth login`; GitHub-side CodeRabbit covers this PR meanwhile.

mechanism: detector + observe-to-close — `tests/vitest-reporter-convention.test.ts` is the gate (runs in CI's node project); the flag repro receipt above is the failing-observe; any future pickup that writes the dead flag fails it with a message naming the bare form and this issue. No new workflow, no new organ.

Closes #3370

- Seat: **litellm/senior** — `bin/fleet-review-arm-check` exit 0; `find_senior_seat` (fleet-ops `lib/litellm-seat.sh`) → `litellm<TAB>senior`, exit 0; passed explicitly via the repo's `.pi/agents/reviewer.md` `model: litellm/senior` binding (the extension would otherwise inherit the worker's own seat).
- Verdict: CLEAN — no blocking findings. The reviewer re-witnessed the bug, the `--reporter=dot` alternative, the detector (1 passed), both swept bodies (0 occurrences, #2873 OPEN / #3302 CLOSED), and confirmed the vitest pin (`^4.1.10` → 4.1.11) plus the detector's placement (node project only, no workers-project leak).
- Findings, one adjudication bucket each (review-adjudication):

  1. `tests/vitest-reporter-convention.test.ts:31-33` — the guard never asserts AGENTS.md itself is among the scanned surfaces; a rename would silently drop the primary surface while `.github/` keeps the list non-empty. → **Consider**: agreed; one-line close (`expect(surfaces).toContain("AGENTS.md")`); the reviewer judged it safe to defer and the diff the seat blessed is what ships — recorded for a future round, not churned post-review.
  2. `tests/vitest-reporter-convention.test.ts:35` — the regex catches only the `=basic` spelling; a future `--reporter basic` (space) or YAML `reporter: basic` would slip. No such occurrence exists today in the scanned set (grep no-match). → **Consider**: agreed; same one-line shape (`/--reporter[= ]basic/`); same deferral.
  3. `tests/vitest-reporter-convention.test.ts:12-15` — `scripts/ci-vitest-run.sh` (the one file that invokes vitest in CI) sits outside the scanned scope. → **Noted**: if the wrapper ever stamped a dead flag, CI's own shard goes red visibly, so the guard adds nothing there. Deliberate, documented in the test's comment.
  4. A tracked `.lane/reports/` record added directly above the pre-existing AGENTS.md sentence claiming the `.lane/` tree was retired by #2991. → **Noted**: pre-existing drift in that sentence (dozens of records are tracked on main); the lane-collision guard — the live convention — passes; not this diff's regression.
  5. The +42 lines of net machinery. → **Dismissed-with-reason**: one test inside the existing vitest rail, no new workflow or organ, and nothing else enforces this convention — satisfies READ-FIRST #1 and #4 (no checkers for conventions the existing canary already enforces, because none does).

- No Act-on items → nothing to fix; the PR does not touch gate-owned paths (none of the 3 files is gate-owned), so no attest duty arises.

## Summary

Delivers the HN fast-follow presence connector (#3253, epic #3171): a new `app/lib/presence-connectors/hn.server.ts` (`id: "hn"`, `supportedModes: ["self", "competitor"]`) that turns a tracked entity's match phrase into one serialized Algolia HN Search call (`GET https://hn.algolia.com/api/v1/search_by_date?query=<phrase>&tags=story,comment`) and emits normalized `presence_item` rows whose `canonicalUrl` is the public news.ycombinator.com item URL (the discussion page — where an HN mention is actually read); the story's external link, points and comment count ride in raw_json for ranking.

Frugality posture (the ~10k req/hour/IP Algolia figure is a community-observed courtesy budget, not an SLA): ONE awaited `presenceSafeFetch` per poll — no parallel page fan-out (zero `Promise.all` in the connector) — and no deep paging: the connector always reads page 0 of the date-ordered results and slides the window forward via `numericFilters=created_at_i>watermark`, so the ~1,000-result ceiling is never approached (time-window slicing is Algolia's documented pattern for this). Ships dark behind `PRESENCE_HN_ROLLOUT` (credentials gate always true — no key, no auth).

Migration `0100_widen_source_target_connector_hn.sql` follows the 0093/0098/0099 CHECK-widen table-rebuild convention: the nine-connector union CHECK (eight predecessors + `hn`), expand-only, child tables (presence_item, presence_poll_cursor, presence_item_revision) snapshotted into plain backup tables before the rebuild and restored after, all inside D1's single-transaction migration. No drop of data tables, no renames, no NOT NULL without DEFAULT — rollback of the PR removes code, never data.

Phase shipped: this issue is ONE expand/contract phase (a CHECK widen; the column already exists, so no add-column/backfill/read-switch/drop chain). Nothing follows.

Modified beyond the issue's EXACT FILES, all consequence-of-landing (each asserts the widened/extended surface): `presence-display.ts` (docs copy "Hacker News"), `tests/customer-claim-surface-registry.test.ts` (presenceSources catalog gains `hn`), `tests/presence-source-coverage.test.ts` (coverage fixture), `tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts` (migration-list pins gain 0100), `app/lib/env.server.ts` (the `PRESENCE_HN_ROLLOUT` binding the issue's MODIFY-list gate file reads). No gate-owned path touched (no .github/**, no scripts/ci-*, no existing migration edited, no plan/entitlements, no competitor-site-monitor, no existing connector).

Review-adjudication buckets (senior reviewer round, ONE round per fleet-ops#3709; reviewer seat: cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high, resolved via find_senior_seat after `bin/fleet-review-arm-check` exited 0): VERDICT: BLOCKING — both Act-on items fixed in 0783ee458 and everything re-run to green.
- Act on (1): `tags=story,comment` — Algolia ANDs bare tags, and no item is both a story and a comment, so live polls would honestly return empty mention sets while the mocked fixture hid it. FIXED: the connector now sends the documented parenthesized OR form `tags=(story,comment)` and both test pins were updated to it.
- Act on (2): `safeIsoDate(hit.created_at)` — `created_at` is `string | null` in the Algolia hit, a strict-TS type error at CI, and at runtime `new Date(null)` is the 1970 epoch, not a missing-date null. FIXED: rss:552 house pattern — `typeof hit.created_at === "string" ? safeIsoDate(hit.created_at) : null`.
- Consider (recorded, not fixed): `comment_text`/`story_text` are HTML and excerpts are not stripped (not XSS — rendered as a text node — but tags would show); `hitsPerPage=50` is lossy for >50-mention bursts (the watermark jumps to the newest hit; 1,000 in one request would still be one serialized fetch); `itemType` discriminates via `comment_text || story_id` where `_tags` would be stronger. All three are judgment calls the reviewer explicitly did not block on.
- Noted (recorded): the coverage-label ternary grew another `hn` arm; healthCheck treats any 2xx as healthy (same as Threads); the integration test mocks the network, so it could not catch the tags-AND bug — noted, matches the gdelt/threads precedent.
- Dismissed-with-reason: the 0100 rebuild's `DROP TABLE source_target` (0093/0098/0099 convention, child snapshots, CHECK is a strict superset, tested read+write); cursor wrapping via pollPresenceSourceTarget (service keeps priorCursor on failure); SSRF/fetch posture (presenceSafeFetch public-IP + redirect re-validate + 750k cap, digits-only objectID); constraints and stale-API checks (no gate-owned paths, no package.json change, no vitest-pool-workers/SELF.fetch).

Verification (final head 0783ee458, after the reviewer's two Act-on fixes):
- Termination command, literal, as written in the issue: `npx vitest run tests/integration/hn-mention-connector.integration.test.ts` → exit 0, 21/21 passed on real workerd (`Test Files 1 passed (1) / Tests 21 passed (21)`); same after the reviewer's fixes (post-fix run: 21/21, Duration 17.95s; the pre-fix run was 21/21, Duration 5.91s — the fixes changed the asserted URL, which is why the suite's pins were updated with it)
- Affected node-project tests at final head (`npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main`) → exit 0, 373 files / 4663 tests passed, Duration 206.01s (presence-types/coverage/registry/display changes ripple, so --changed pulls the affected set; CI owns coverage and typecheck, none run here)
- `sgscan` at final head → "No new security findings.", exit 0
- Integration test asserts, against fixture Algolia responses over real workerd + real migrations: registry registration; `presenceSourceCoverageForDocs()` surfaces hn as gated; validateTarget shape + metadata; gated while `PRESENCE_HN_ROLLOUT` unset (refuses to poll without fetching); story+comment items with public news.ycombinator.com canonicalUrl carrying contentHash/publishedAt/author and points/commentCount in raw_json; honest empty (`ok: true, items: []`); page-0-only even when Algolia reports 25 result pages (~1,000-result ceiling never walked); next-poll time-window via `numericFilters=created_at_i>watermark`; persisted watermark read back the way the poll orchestrator does; HTTP errors → honest degraded, never fabricated items; healthCheck pending/healthy(degraded) tri-state; documented search_by_date URL; `connector_id='hn'` written via the widened CHECK and read back; 0100 re-applies cleanly preserving child rows and every predecessor connector's rows

net-positive-because: the issue's whole purpose is a NEW connector — a new file, a new migration and its integration test (+1280 net-new lines, 12 files, 6 modified lines) are the deliverable, not bloat; the only subtraction is one blank line in presence-display.ts

run-proof: prove-one-run-check OK ("net-positive diff (+1280 lines) carries net-positive-because:") — this PR adds no unit, timer or workflow; its proof of work is one proven end-to-end termination run: the literal command `npx vitest run tests/integration/hn-mention-connector.integration.test.ts` exits 0 (21/21 tests, real workerd), plus the affected node-project --changed run (373 files / 4663 tests, exit 0) and sgscan ("No new security findings.", exit 0), all at final head 0783ee458

research: Algolia HN Search API docs (https://hn.algolia.com/api — search_by_date, tags, numericFilters, page-0-only 1,000-result ceiling, time-window slicing as the documented deep-paging alternative); the official Firebase HN API has no search, so Algolia is the only free search surface (issue evidence agrees); the ~10k req/hour/IP figure is community-observed, not in Algolia's docs, so it is treated as a courtesy budget (serialized, low-cadence, page-0-only), not an SLA. Peer shapes read before writing: `app/lib/presence-connectors/rss.server.ts` (connector interface), migrations 0093/0098/0099 (CHECK-widen convention), existing presence-hash / public-url / presence-robots / bounded-response reused read-only per the issue.

help-first: no new bin/ file in this PR; nothing hand-built that already exists — the connector conforms to the existing `presence-types` interface, the migration reuses the 0093/0099 table-rebuild convention, and networking/dedup/SSRF reuse presenceSafeFetch, presenceContentHash and normalizePublicHttpUrl.

organ-heartbeat: none — this PR touches no organ (no scheduled unit/timer/heartbeat file; the only scheduled behavior, the poll orchestrator, already exists and merely gains a registered connector).

token: fleet-token-efficiency-check OK ("no token-efficiency anti-patterns in changed prompt assemblers")

loose-ends: activation (flipping `PRESENCE_HN_ROLLOUT` and adding hn targets in production) is a deliberate rollout step, not part of this PR; the issue's UNKNOWNS (one-target-vs-two, relevance-vs-date ordering) are pinned by the test as ONE target with date ordering + numericFilters watermark, and relevance-vs-date is eval-covered per the issue.

Closes #3253

Relates to #3171
title: feat(presence): Hacker News presence connector — Algolia HN Search, free, no key, no auth (issue #3253)
