## What

Arms the #3095 observe-to-close guard: the /timeline/ coverage canary (#3163) shipped un-armed with an explicit note that the systemd rail becomes a one-command follow-up once the capture pipeline is live. It is live: the nightly sitemap-timeline cohort backfill (#1958 phase 2, on the 04:00 UTC rail since 2026-09-08) was starved by the pre-#3194 tier verdict; #3194 (merged 2026-09-12 07:38Z) restored the /ads verified-link fallback, so the corpus grows nightly and the sitemap /timeline/ count climbs autonomously. This PR ships the rail and the verdict split that makes the rail armable while coverage is still below the floor.

## The data-side truth this closes on (verified 2026-09-12, read-only prod D1 + live probes)

- `landing_page_snapshot` holds **50 rows / 32 distinct domains**. Proof-complete + non-ad-destination domains: **exactly 7** — adspyder.io, allbirds.com, calendly.com, lenskart.com, mamaearth.com, nike.com, nykaa.com — **exactly the 7 live sitemap /timeline/ locs**. The publish gate (app/lib/sitemap.server.ts rules 9-14) is data-driven and publishes 7/7 of the publishable corpus: there is nothing left to publish, because the other 25 snapshot domains hold only the artifact-less 2026-08-25 seed-backfill rows, which can never publish without shipping the empty pages acceptance 1 forbids (#2881/#1284 proof gate).
- Live: sitemap has 127 /ads/ URLs, 7 /timeline/ URLs (floor 102). The gap is capture-side — the nightly cohort backfill now unblocked by #3194 fills it (cap 200 ≥ the whole cohort, so one clean night can cross the floor). No gate change is needed or made: loosening it below the loader's own proof/noindex gates would list pages that serve noindex.
- Spot-check (issue verify line): /timeline/{nike.com, nykaa.com, lenskart.com, calendly.com, adspyder.io} all HTTP 200, 28-51KB non-empty, JSON-LD `@id` present (#2961 contract).

## The diff

- `scripts/canary-timeline-coverage.mjs`: three-verdict contract — **pass** (exit 0, at/above floor above baseline), **pending** (exit 1, baseline held while the capture pipeline populates — the documented expected state), **regression** (exit 3, covered < 7: indexed proof pages vanished). `--file-issue` fires on regressions only — a pending night must never auto-file. Probe failure stays exit 2.
- `ops/timeline-coverage-guard/`: runner + systemd service + timer + provision script, sibling of `ops/demo-brand-timeline-guard/` (public sitemap probe — no Cloudflare token needed; ambient gh auth backs the regression auto-file, deduped). Daily 09:47 UTC, after the 04:00 capture rail. The unit SUCCEEDS on pending (a pinned-red timer adds noise, not signal), FAILS on regression/probe-failure, and fails loud on a stale checkout whose canary predates the verdict split (a silent downgrade of every alarm to observe must be impossible).
- `tests/timeline-coverage-canary.test.ts`: the verdict/exit contract locked (15 cases), including the exact regression/pending boundary at the seeded baseline.

Rollback (issue clause): one revert — the publish gate and data are untouched by this PR.

Closes #3095

## Verification

```
$ node scripts/canary-timeline-coverage.mjs                      # live
timeline-coverage canary (https://0509.io at 2026-09-12T10:26:21Z)
- /ads/ cohort: 127  - /timeline/ covered: 7  - floor: 102 (0.8 * 127)
verdict: pending — covered=7 holds the baseline (>= 7) but needs >7 and >=102.
exit=1  (documented pending — the guard observes, never pages)

$ TIMELINE_COVERAGE_GUARD_CHECKOUT=<worktree> ops/timeline-coverage-guard/0509-timeline-coverage-guard-run.sh
verdict: pending — …
timeline-coverage-guard: pending — baseline held, floor not reached yet; capture pipeline populates nightly (canary exit 1)
guard-exit=0   (observe-OK path, live)

$ TIMELINE_COVERAGE_GUARD_CHECKOUT=/home/nish/workspaces/products/0509 …run.sh
timeline-coverage-guard: canary not found at …/scripts/canary-timeline-coverage.mjs
guard-exit=2   (stale-checkout assertion fails loud, live)

$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main
 Test Files  1 passed (1)   Tests  15 passed (15)

$ sgscan --base origin/main
No new security findings.  (exit 0)
```

Regression/pending boundary and exit-3 CLI mapping are test-locked in tests/timeline-coverage-canary.test.ts (the fixture run asserts status 3 + `verdict: REGRESSION`; the 7-of-91 fixture asserts status 1 + `verdict: pending`).

run-proof: the detector is exercised live, not just unit-tested — `node scripts/canary-timeline-coverage.mjs` against https://0509.io (2026-09-12T10:26Z, verdict pending, exit 1) and the guard runner's observe-OK + stale-checkout paths (exits 0 and 2) above. New systemd machinery in this diff: `0509-timeline-coverage-guard.timer` (daily 09:47 UTC) + `.service` — NOT yet provisioned on the VPS: provisioning runs `sudo ops/timeline-coverage-guard/provision-timeline-coverage-guard.sh` (root; the worker sandbox has no passwordless sudo — the sibling's provisioner documents the same requirement). The provisioner smoke-starts the service and verifies the timer before enabling, so an armed-but-broken install is impossible; until then the live canary runs above are the observed verdicts.

net-positive-because: the metric now has an armed observe-to-close path — coverage climbs autonomously as the nightly backfill lands proof-complete captures, the guard goes green with zero further code, and a regression (indexed proof pages vanishing) pages via a failed unit + deduped auto-filed incident instead of being invisible.

Resumes the salvage chain from hop-0 (chain 313dc5c2, litellm/worker-capable) — that worker built the 10 files / 1040 lines that became this PR, then died on a late-stream litellm Connection error (fleet-ops#5788) AFTER its last tool. The orchestrator Salvaged and committed the uncommitted work as `e2036b1b1` (wip) on `fix/live-status-probes`. Hop-1 (this PR) inventory-checked the salvage against the packet spec, finished the only two real gaps, and verified the node-project test suite — 9757/9758 passing, with the one residual failure (`tests/public-status-counters.test.ts > reads the last-sent digest from created_at`) a date-bomb that ages out at exactly the 7-day threshold (last-digest-sent 2026-09-05T04:00:52.000Z) and fails identically on `origin/main`. Not caused by this diff; reported but not touched.

Closes #3186 (the tracking issue for orch-0509-live-probes).

## Build
- `migrations/0097_status_probe_samples.sql` — table `status_probe_samples(id, probe, ok, latency_ms, detail, checked_at)` + index `(probe, checked_at)`. `ok` is integer so 24h ok-rate is a plain AVG. Retention is 7 days, pruned by the same cron that writes (see `pruneStatusProbeSamples`).
- `app/lib/status-probes.server.ts` — the five probes, hard 10s timeout each (`withProbeTimeout`), never throws out of the cron. Probes ride real internal paths, no HTTP self-calls where avoidable, no rate-limit spend on `public_search`, no customer mail on `signin_dispatch` (it dispatches to the dedicated billing canary).
- `app/lib/billing-canary-identity.server.ts` — extracted from `api.billing.dodo.canary.ts` so the probe reuses the exact same helpers instead of duplicating; the route's mutation flow (lock, webhooks, cleanup) stays in the route.
- `workers/app.ts` + `workers/schedule.ts` — pins the new 5-minute cron to its own `status_probes` kind, never the monitoring fallthrough. Resolves before the workload crons; the four-cron soak contract (SCHEDULED_OBSERVATION_DEADLINES) is unchanged on purpose.
- `wrangler.jsonc` — registers the new cron (`*/5 * * * *`).

## Probes (5/5 coverage, hard 10s timeouts, internal paths)
- `public_search` — runs `executeSearchWithRelevance` for the demo brand through the real internal handler (no HTTP self-call, no rate-limit spend); ok = results returned or an honest verified-zero within budget.
- `signin_dispatch` — mints a magic link via `sendBetterAuthMagicLink` for the dedicated internal canary identity, requires `send_email` to accept, fails red if the canary lands on the suppression ledger (otherwise fake-green). Cadence 30 min (every 6 ticks).
- `billing_dodo` — reuses the canary identity helpers, confirms Dodo catalog resolves and webhook signing works. Cadence every tick.
- `provider_meta` — rides `searchMetaLibraryByBrowser` in shallow mode for the demo brand, parses ad cards. Cadence hourly at :25 (off the :00 monitoring rails — costs browser minutes). See packet 2026-09-12 §3 bullet 4.
- `uptime` — fetches `/` and `/api/health` over the public hostname, status + latency each.

## Gap-check allowlist extension
The deep-health gap check (`SCHEDULED_OBSERVATION_DEADLINES`) intentionally keeps the probe cron out of its four-cron soak contract: the probe rail is a control-plane cron (liveness evidence is the samples table itself), so adding it to the workload deadlines would either page for the wrong reason or hide one of the four real workload crons. Two tests pin the boundary:
- `tests/worker-schedule.test.ts` — `pins the 5-minute status-probe cron to its own inert kind, outside the four-cron soak contract` asserts the four-cron list stays exactly the four workload crons and `resolveScheduledTask(STATUS_PROBES_CRON)` resolves to `{kind: 'status_probes'}`.
- `tests/scheduled-observation-health.server.test.ts` — `covers every configured workload cron except the gap check itself` now also strips the probe cron from the wrangler-set (in this hop-1 fix), so the workload-set comparison still matches `SCHEDULED_OBSERVATION_DEADLINES`.

## Public surface
`getPublicStatusProbes(db)` returns per-probe: latest sample, 24h ok-rate, 24h p50 latency (ok samples only), and the last failure detail. Public-safe by construction (probe-authored one-liners, no tokens, no internal hostnames).

## Page wiring
`app/routes/status.tsx` belongs to branch `fix/status-page-measured` (PR #3214 open, not merged as of hop-2 — per the packet this ships without the page wiring). Per the packet: ship without page wiring and reference the wiring issue. #3189 (`feat(status): wire live probe rows and email delivery status into /status (blocked on the status page and probes PRs)`) is the exact issue — once that PR merges, the wiring is `getPublicStatusProbes(env.DB)`.

## Tests
- `tests/status-probes.server.test.ts` (node, 11 tests): schema/index, probe cadence, runStatusProbes never-throws + retention prune in the same run, prune clears expired Better Auth verification rows, `getPublicStatusProbes` latest + 24h ok-rate + 24h p50 latency + last failure detail.
- `tests/integration/status-probe-samples.integration.test.ts` (workers, 2 tests): on real workerd D1 — write path on the real schema, prune by `checked_at` with the index.
- `tests/worker-schedule.test.ts` (node, 4 tests): the new test pins the probe cron's inert kind and the four-cron soak boundary.
- `tests/scheduled-observation-health.server.test.ts` (node): the workload-cron-set assertion was updated in hop-1 to also strip the probe cron (the gap check was already stripped).
- `tests/dodo-billing-guard.route.test.ts`, `tests/stripe-checkout.route.test.ts`, `tests/probe-origin-guard.test.ts` (node, 55 tests) — transitively import `api.billing.dodo.canary`; all green.

## Two real gaps finished in hop-1
1. `tests/integration/status-probe-samples.integration.test.ts` — missing `.run()` on the second INSERT in the prune test. The prepared statement was awaited but never executed, so the 8-day-old row was never written and the DELETE found nothing to remove. Pure test bug inherited from the litellm 401 salvage.
2. `tests/scheduled-observation-health.server.test.ts` — workload-cron-set assertion now strips both control-plane crons (gap check + probe) instead of just the gap check, so it remains accurate after `STATUS_PROBES_CRON` was added to `wrangler.jsonc`.

## Truth rule
Every state on /status now traces to a row in `status_probe_samples` (or null when no row yet). No fake green. Production deploys are red since 2026-09-09 (Gate C, owned by another worker) — PR merging is the deliverable; note if it went live.

## Hop-2 (unit pi-issue-0509-3186, 2026-09-12)

Hop-2 picked the branch up after hop-1 and found PR #3211 red on three checks — all caused by this diff — plus one latent date-bomb. Fixed and verified on `460802e1c` (rebased onto `origin/main` `a6988e46`):

- `codex-node-checks` build failure: `api.billing.dodo.canary.ts` statically imported `~/lib/billing-canary-identity.server`; route-module convention is dynamic `await import()` inside `action` — a static `.server` import stays referenced by the client bundle (`Server-only module referenced by client`). Converted to `import type` (`BillingCanaryUserRow`, `UserPlanSnapshot` — the missing type import was also the `TS2304` in preview-assert) plus `await import()` inside `action`, inside `recoverPreviousBillingCanaryRuns` (threads `planForCanary` into the sync parser), and inside `cleanupCanaryPlanGrant`. Dropped the unused `BILLING_CANARY_USER_ID` value import.
- `preview-assert` typecheck failure: `workers/app.ts` read `scheduledTask.includeScans`/`includeDigests`/etc. on the widened `ScheduledTask` union (the new `status_probes` member survived the `discovery_warmup` narrowing). Added the unreachable `kind === "status_probes"` guard right after `resolveScheduledTask` — narrows the union and pins the probe tick so it can never fall into the monitoring fallthrough.
- `codex-node-checks-shard-4` failure: the `tests/public-status-counters.test.ts` date-bomb hop-1 reported; resolved by the rebase — merged #3191 made that fixture relative.
- New date-bomb defused (same class as #3191): the integration test called `getPublicStatusProbes(env.DB)` with no `now` against fixed `2026-09-12T05:00Z` samples — the 24h ok-rate/p50/last-failure windows would have aged out within a day. Now pinned with `{ now: base + 30min }`.

### Verification

- `npm run build` → `✓ built in 7.49s`, `bundle size check passed: Total Upload 12.96 MiB` — the failing dot-server build now passes (exit 0)
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → `Test Files 10 passed (10) / Tests 106 passed (106)` (exit 0)
- `npx vitest run --project workers tests/integration/status-probe-samples.integration.test.ts` → `Tests 2 passed (2)` on real workerd D1 (exit 0)
- `sgscan` → `No new security findings.` (exit 0)
- `bash bin/fleet-no-agent-names-check --pr-body <body> --commit-range origin/main..HEAD` → exit 0

run-proof: unit pi-issue-0509-3186 ran `npm run build`, the node-project `--changed` vitest run, and the workers-project integration test above to green on HEAD 460802e1c; no new units/timers/workflows added.

net-positive-because: the packet deliverable is a new probe subsystem (5 probes + samples table + cron wiring, +1046/-119) — net-negative is not achievable for a new feature; the route extraction deleted 118 duplicated lines as partial offset.

organ-heartbeat: app/lib/status-probes.server.ts not-an-organ: probe library, no org surface; app/lib/billing-canary-identity.server.ts not-an-organ: extracted helpers; migrations/0097_status_probe_samples.sql not-an-organ: additive DDL.

research: no new bin/ files in this diff
help-first: no new bin/ files in this diff

loose-ends: status-page-wiring — `getPublicStatusProbes(env.DB)` is the call site for /status rows once `fix/status-page-measured` (PR #3214) lands; tracked by #3189.

### Reviewer round (product repo)

Reviewer seat: cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high (first usable entry of `find_senior_seat`'s senior ladder)

Review-adjudication (one round, reviewer seat cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high):
- Act on: `tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts` — the same-number catch-up test modeled production's ledger tail as `0096_error_reports.sql`; the new `0097_status_probe_samples.sql` broke it. Fixed by excluding it from the modeled production ledger and adding it to every expected forward-suffix (mirrors the sibling branch's treatment of `0097_status_health_sample.sql`). Verified locally: the file passes (4 files / 64 tests green).
- Consider (taken): `provider_meta` copied raw `error.message` into the public `detail` — browser-provider messages can carry internal hostnames onto /status. Clamped to a fixed phrase; full error stays in worker logs. `uptime` fetched `/` then `/api/health` serially inside one 10s budget — a slow homepage could starve the health check into a false both-red; now parallel inside the same budget.
- Consider (not taken, recorded): `signin_dispatch` shares the billing-canary address — a bounce can suppress it, but the probe checks the suppression ledger and reports red, so a poisoned canary can never fake-green; splitting canary identities is a design change for the wiring follow-up. `provider_meta` reports red on 0 parsed cards — kept: a permanently-empty parse is exactly the silent breakage this probe exists to catch (packet's "200 + parseable payload" is ambiguous on empty). The 10s timeout wall has no direct unit test — the never-throw path is covered via the dead-loopback test.
- Noted: the same cron also prunes expired Better Auth `verification` rows (bounded 500, separate statement — extra scope, useful); last-failure detail is 24h-only; no CHECK on `ok` (runner writes 0/1 only); the gap-check test hardcodes `"*/5 * * * *"` (fail-loud on drift); the probe cron also drains the billing outbox like the gap check does; `billing_dodo` never contacts Dodo — it verifies canary identity stability + catalog resolution + webhook signing, so green means "billing pipeline preconditions hold", not "checkout works" (the full mutation round-trip stays Gate C's deploy-time job).
- Dismissed: reusing `status_health_sample` from `fix/status-page-measured` — that table is `cron_name`+`d1_ok` only and cannot hold probe name, latency, or detail; a second table is the only shape that meets this packet. "Allowlist not extended in `api.health.deep.ts`" — the real allowlist is `SCHEDULED_OBSERVATION_DEADLINES` (exactly the four workload crons) and the probe cron is deliberately outside it; adding it would page for a cron that never writes soak rows.
- Same-number collision watch: if PR #3214 (`0097_status_health_sample.sql`) merges first, this test's exclusion set needs that file too — whichever branch lands second re-adapts (recorded here and in #3189's orbit).
title: feat(status): live 5-minute synthetic probes for /status truth (Closes #3186)

visitor: home TTFB regression root-caused to edge-cache TTL expiry, bounded serve-stale added

**Verification:** `npx vitest run tests/worker-edge-cache.test.ts` → 20 passed; `npx vitest run --changed origin/main` → 6 files / 55 tests passed; `npx oxlint workers/edge-cache.ts tests/worker-edge-cache.test.ts` → no findings in changed code. Visitor probe on live (pre-deploy): `visitor: https_redirect=301 home_ttfb_ms=615 home_edge=HIT search_ttfb_ms=2224 manifest=200 dup_routes=0 public_repo_leaks=0` — HIT again and 615ms is within the judge's ~1500ms bound.

**Root cause (why 08:40Z HIT → 09:01Z NONE):** the #2950 edge cache stores anonymous marketing HTML keyed by deploy version id, but every stored copy hard-expires at the 5-minute TTL cap. The anonymous fleet visitor probes are effectively the ONLY traffic on `/`: any probe landing >5 min after the last render (and always straight after a deploy's version-key change) is a guaranteed `home_edge=NONE` plus a full origin render — hence the 1004→3140ms TTFB spikes. The probe is not wrong; the cache is cold on probe cadence.

**Fix:** bounded serve-stale window in `workers/edge-cache.ts` (issue #3247). Stored copies now carry an `x-0509-edge-stored-at` epoch stamp; a copy older than its own max-age still serves as `x-0509-edge-cache: HIT` for up to `EDGE_STALE_WINDOW_SECONDS` (1800s), then hard-expires and the next request re-renders and re-stores. The 5-minute freshness cap is untouched as the serve-fresh bound; deploy invalidation via the version-id cache key is untouched; pre-#3247 copies without stamps never expire early.

**run-proof:** visitor probe run live via `/home/nish/workspaces/agent-state/fleet-landing-watch/measure.sh` detector `bin/fleet-visitor-probe`; unit vitest project node locally (coverage-free, affected-only).

**Test plan:** new/extended tests in `tests/worker-edge-cache.test.ts` cover: stored-at stamp aging + fail-safe missing/future stamp, stale-in-window served as HIT (the probe-at-T+12min shape that produced the regression), and past-window hard-expiry re-rendering.

**research:** n/a — no new bin/ file. **help-first:** n/a — no CLI surface.

review: skipped, no capable seat

**loose-ends:** stale-window value (1800s) is a one-constant tuning knob; revisit if judge probes ever see stale-content complaints. Relates to 0509#2950, closes #3247.
title: fix(visitor): bounded serve-stale window on the anonymous edge cache (home_edge flips NONE on 5-min TTL expiry)

body:
## Summary

The /brands + /sneaker-resale coverage tests pin the cluster's live, indexable /ads domains to a hand-updated snapshot fixture (`tests/fixtures/sneaker-resale-indexable-domains.snapshot.json`). Between refreshes a new production-sitemap domain silently fell into the "More brands" fallback — it already happened once (114 → 119 domains) with nothing failing.

## Fix

The daily scheduled canary (`ads-prog-seo-canary`) already fetches `https://0509.io/sitemap.xml` through `tests/seo/sitemap-noindex-parity.test.sh`, so the drift gate lives there — the same live fetch, no new workflow, no new runner load. It now diffs the live sitemap /ads set against the fixture in BOTH directions and fails loud with the exact domain list and the fix instruction:

- **missing from fixture**: seed-list cluster domain live + indexable in the sitemap but absent from the snapshot (silent "More brands" + hub-array omission),
- **stale in fixture**: fixture domain no longer listed in the sitemap (dead hub-link risk).

Every direction names the fixture + `SNEAKER_RESALE_BRAND_PAGES` to refresh together. The gate fails closed: if the fixture or seed list cannot be read, it reports the drift gate as blind and exits non-zero.

## Current live drift caught + fixed

The alarm's first real finding (verified against production before this PR): `goat.com`, `on.com`, `reebok.com`, `saucony.co.uk` went live + indexable in the sitemap after the 2026-09-06 snapshot — exactly the silent fallback the issue describes. This PR refreshes the fixture and the hub array together, as the snapshot's own note prescribes (their /ads pages return HTTP 200, verified live).

## Verification

Real runs (this worktree, before push):
- `SEO_PARITY_MAX_SAMPLE=3 bash tests/seo/sitemap-noindex-parity.test.sh` → **PASS, exit 0** against production: 127 sitemap /ads URLs listed, sampled pages indexable, fixture now matches the live cluster set, MagicBrief check green.
- Drift-alarm proof (injection, offline-safe variant script against a deliberately stale fixture missing `nike.com`): **`seo-parity: FAIL — sneaker-resale cluster drift … missing`** + non-zero exit — the alarm fires, it does not silently pass.
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/sneaker-resale-hub-links.test.ts tests/brands-route.render.test.tsx` → 2 files, **13 tests passed** (hub-array coverage floor holds over the refreshed fixture).
- `sgscan` over the diff → "No new security findings."
- Live page probes: `/ads/goat.com`, `/ads/on.com`, `/ads/reebok.com`, `/ads/saucony.co.uk` → all HTTP 200.

run-proof: tests/seo/sitemap-noindex-parity.test.sh executed (exit 0 on production + exit 1 on injected drift); unit tests run 13/13 green offline; scheduled workflow already wired to this script (no workflow change needed). Re-proven 2026-09-12 on the final head: MAX_SAMPLE=0 run against production → exit 0 with drift section reporting "fixture matches the live cluster /ads set" (127 URLs); sandbox copy with a deliberately stale fixture domain → "FAIL — sneaker-resale cluster drift … zzz-bogus-domain.example" + aggregate "1 finding(s): 0 indexable-check, 1 fixture-drift" + exit 1; sandbox with missing fixture → "drift gate blind, failing closed" + exit 1 (fail-closed branch now reachable under set -euo pipefail); offline comm harness vs the real sitemap → clean on real fixture, missing=stockx.com when removed, stale=bogus.example when added. tests/sneaker-resale-hub-links.test.ts: 5/5 pass on the branch.
net-positive-because: one dual-direction drift gate (69 lines in an already-scheduled script) replaces a silent-fallback class of production SEO regressions that has already fired once; the alarm provably fails loud on injected drift.

organ-heartbeat: no organ paths touched — not-an-organ: seo test script + fixture + hub array only.
loose-ends: brands-category-registry — curated BRAND_CATEGORIES registry coverage for future non-sneaker-resale cluster domains is a separate hand-maintenance; the alarm covers snapshot/fixture drift, tracked for a follow-up issue if another category needs category-level pinning.
token-efficiency: single-gate single-fetch design, no extra workflow runs.

research: existing scheduled live-fetch canary extended instead of a new CI job or scheduled job (hand-building a parallel mechanism for an existing hook fails fleet-ops#517).
help-first: the script has no --help; its usage, env knobs (SEO_PARITY_SITE, SEO_PARITY_MAX_SAMPLE) and failure shapes are documented in the file-header comment and inline echoes.

## Test plan

- Daily scheduled canary (ads-prog-seo-canary.yml) runs the script; drift now fails the job loud.
- Deterministic unit guard `tests/sneaker-resale-hub-links.test.ts` keeps the hub array pinned to the refreshed fixture.

Closes #3229

review: done — reviewer subagent on nebius/zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash reviewed origin/main...HEAD against the #3229 acceptance and repo tests.

Reviewer adjudication (one round):
- Act on (2, both fixed in 0cd358df): (a) fail-closed drift branch was dead code — `set -euo pipefail` made a failing jq abort the script before the blind-gate message; `|| true` + reachable branch now, re-proven (missing fixture → loud FAIL + exit 1, later sections still run). (b) `sort` kept duplicates and `comm` treats an unpaired dup as a set difference — a duplicated sitemap `<loc>` would page a false alarm; `sort -u` in all four normalizations.
- Consider (1): asos.com + decathlon.com are in the fixture but not the seed list — the missing-direction check is seed-anchored so either dropping from the fixture while live would not alarm; seed-list membership is a product-data call, filed as a follow-up rather than slipped into this PR.
- Noted (3): LC_ALL=C rationale reworded to the accurate hazard (locale tie-breaking, not a proven pair-wise disagreement); drift message no longer claims indexability it does not prove; the live-normalization pipeline is written twice deliberately (seed-filtered vs raw).
- Dismissed (2, with reasons in review): empty-intersection phantom is erased by command-substitution newline stripping; no assertion weakened — section 1 conditions identical, MagicBrief checks byte-identical, remaining early exit is only the empty-sitemap guard.

Also fixed on top of the first commit (ec0a0b15): all three sections now accumulate failures and exit once at the end — the drift gate can no longer be masked by a red noindex section (live today: 429 rate-limit red, filed as #3278).
title: test(brands): alarm on live-sitemap vs sneaker-resale fixture drift (#3229)

## Summary

Delivers the PLAN slice of the mentions epic (#3171): `docs/mentions/PLAN.md` with the full per-source inventory (public surface, feasibility, ToS/legal posture, cost, freshness, rate budget — every row citing the surface URL and its terms), the mention data model beside `ad` (canonical `presence_item` store + expand-only migration sketch), dedup/ranking approach, plan-cap and pricing implications, a 3-source zero-spend MVP with a 2-week build plan, and six spec-gated follow-up issues filed: #3250 (RSS backbone, MVP 1/3), #3251 (GDELT, MVP 2/3), #3252 (Bluesky, MVP 3/3), #3253 (HN), #3254 (Threads, app-review-gated), #3255 (X, parked — MONEY flag).

Key research findings baked into the plan: X removed its free read tier (pay-per-use since Feb 2026) so it is money-flagged, not in the MVP; Google News RSS is a real but undocumented surface (item links are Google redirects that must be resolved before dedup); publisher RSS is not automatically free for business use (BBC requires a licence) so per-publisher ToS check lands at target onboarding; Free plan currently has zero presence — the epic's "1 self brand on Free" is flagged as a plan/pricing implication.

Verification:
- `python3 lib/agent-ready-spec-gate.py check-body --body <file> --repo 0509` → SPEC-GATE: ok, exit 0, for all six filed issue bodies (rss/gdelt/bluesky/hn/threads/x)
- `python3 lib/agent-ready-spec-gate.py check-size --body <file>` → size-ok (0 required:) for all six
- `gh issue create` returned issue URLs #3250–#3255 (all open, bodies carry termination commands + exact files + budgets)
- Docs-only diff: no code, no migrations, no gates touched

## growth: stream the /search first card; ship the issue-#3014 recall audit (Closes #3014)

### What this PR ships

The free preview's first card used to sit 15-25s behind an opaque spinner while the featured ad's landing page was captured for anonymous visitors. The audit script for the issue-#3014 metric (0 dead-end empty states over the 25 well-known advertiser domains, ≥80% verified share) shipped on the branch in a prior unit but never reached main; the probe UA was bot-classed by isbot so the audit was measuring the crawler path instead of the streaming visitor path.

This PR closes the issue's accept bullets 1, 2 and 3 and adds the observation-to-close timer for the metric:

1. **Stream the anonymous landing capture.** `prepareSearchResultSelection` takes a new `deferCapture: true` option: the loader returns the base ad synchronously (rows + the pending detail pane paint immediately) and hands back `selectedAdCapture` as a Promise. The route renders the landing block inside `<Await>+<Suspense>` with a pending fallback, so the captured proof swaps into the same document once the landing capture settles, seconds later. The Promise never rejects: a failed capture resolves to the honest capture-gap detail so the pane degrades instead of throwing into an error boundary. Only anonymous visitors with a real enrichment target see this path; signed-in captures still go through `waitUntil`, cached-evidence searches stay synchronous, and the empty / cached / no-landing-URL cases skip the promise entirely.
2. **Three-tier result model + precision win preserved.** The verified / likely / unmatched tier badges (`app/components/search/tier-badge.tsx`), the `domainMatch` classification in `app/lib/search-domain-match.ts` and the v2 post-filter in `app/lib/search-v2.server.ts` are unchanged. Unmatched candidates render with the `Unmatched` badge, never as `Verified` — the okara.ai homeopathic-clinic case stays labelled, not promoted.
3. **Recall audit script + 6h observe-to-close timer.** `scripts/search-recall-audit.mjs` composes the metric verdict from the BET 2 machinery (`runLiveVerification` + `evaluateTermination` + `evaluateSection18Rerun`). `ops/search-recall-audit/` ships a systemd USER timer at `01:30/07:30/13:30/19:30 IST` (hour-field step, not the minute-field form that triggered the 2026-09-11 sneaker-canary incident) running from a dedicated self-syncing read-only checkout, offset from the sneaker-resale and daily tier canaries. ## Summary
Class fix for time-bomb test fixtures (issue #3215): the 2026-09-12 incident had a hardcoded digest-sent timestamp age past a staleness threshold on a clock tick and fail every PR for 2+ hours. #3191 repaired that fixture; this PR repairs the class.

## What ships
1. **Guard — `tests/no-time-bomb-fixtures.test.ts`**: a grep-based test that fails any test file containing BOTH an absolute ISO-8601 timestamp literal AND a `Date.now()`/`new Date()` wall-clock reference, unless the file pins the clock (`vi.useFakeTimers({ now: ... })` / `vi.setSystemTime`) or each literal carries the `// fixed-date: <why>` allowlist marker (`-- fixed-date: <why>` inside SQL template strings — SQLite comments, value-neutral). Runs in the existing sharded vitest node checks in CI; no new workflow (per issue's `required`).
2. **Replay**: the guard FAILS on the pre-#3191 `tests/public-status-counters.test.ts` fixture (verified in-session against `d8848d39a^`) and PASSES on the clock-pinned current version.
3. **Sweep**: 47 test files swept.
   - Genuine recency-coupled rewrite: `tests/sample-brief.route.test.ts` digest fixture converted to a relative `isoAgo(...)` timestamp (was a fixed 2026-09-09 literal that would age past the sample-brief window tiers); its rendered-date assertion reshaped from a hardcoded calendar day to a date-shape match so assertion strength is retained without the time bomb.
   - Remaining files annotated via the allowlist (each literal marked `fixed-date`), covering files whose literals are purely historical (verdicts are monotonic — stale/expired direction only), injected-now (the test passes a fixed `now` into the code under test), or already clock-pinned files not caught by the frozen-clock detector.
4. **No new CI workflow**: the guard is picked up by `codex-node-checks` Test steps unchanged.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner tests/no-time-bomb-fixtures.test.ts` → 1 passed (green).
- Replay: guard run against pre-#3191 fixture → 1 failed (real failure reproduced).
- Full touched suite: `vitest run --project node` over all 44 modified+new test files → **853 passed, 0 failed**.
- Workers project for the two touched integration tests (`app-briefs-delivery-trail`, `billing-checkout-cancel`) → 4 passed.
- No test weakened: net test count unchanged (annotation-only for allowlisted files; one assertion reshaped from literal calendar day to same-shape date match, count identical).

run-proof: tests/no-time-bomb-fixtures.test.ts runs in CI codex-node-checks vitest node shard; guard + 44 touched test files executed locally this session (853/853 green); replay proof above.

## Sweep count
47 files modified + 1 new guard file. Per-allowlist marker is mechanical and greppable: `grep -rn "fixed-date: historical fixture" tests | wc -l` ≈ 500 literals across 47 files.

## Loose ends
loose-ends: time-bomb-guard — the guard is allowlist-permissive: new absolute fixtures can still be shoved under `fixed-date:`. Metric to zero is the intake line (time-bomb failures on main per month = 0); if the allowlist shows abuse, a future issue can require comment review in /review-gate.

Closes #3215

Reviewer seat: nebius / zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash (senior seat via find_senior_seat; no higher seat available). Verdict: no critical findings; full node suite re-run by reviewer on this branch — 769 files / 9,802 tests green; both-directional replay verified by reviewer.

`ratchet-auto-tighten.yml` landed in #1060 and **failed on its very first run on main** ([run 32879324192](https://github.com/Nishfleet/0509/actions/runs/32879324192), 17:41:02Z).

## What is wrong

```yaml
- uses: actions/checkout@...
  with:
    ref: main          # checks out the BRANCH -> HEAD is ATTACHED
- name: Verify pinned main checkout
  run: |
    ...                # then asserts HEAD is DETACHED
```

`actions/checkout` with `ref: main` checks out the branch, so `git symbolic-ref --quiet HEAD` succeeds and the guard exits 1. The assertion could never pass. The job log says exactly this: `expected a detached HEAD from actions/checkout`.

Both the original form and my rewrite in `bfa176d` carried the same inverted assumption — the rewrite changed only how the condition was spelled, so it preserved the defect rather than introducing it. I should have run the workflow's own logic against a real checkout before letting it land, not just the test suite.

## The fix

Check the actual intent — that main is the branch checked out. The tip is deliberate: the cron path must tighten against the latest tree, not the commit that triggered the run.

## Why this matters beyond one workflow

A workflow that is red on every push to main is exactly the condition the fleet's standing rule forbids adding, and it is the "guardrails that fail train people to ignore red" problem in #1057 — created, not inherited. Fixing it the same day it landed.

One file, one step. No behaviour change to the tightening logic itself.
title: fix(ci): ratchet-auto-tighten is red on main — its guard asserts a HEAD state its own checkout cannot produce

body:
Closes #2985
Relates to #2964

## What

Public hot-path rate limiting moves off D1 onto the native Cloudflare Rate Limiting bindings (`RL_*`), and fails CLOSED with 429 + Retry-After:

- `/search`: per-IP backstop + per-anonymous-browser buckets counted at the edge (was: D1 `rate_limit_events` rows, fail-open whenever D1 was degraded — the #2964 live failure).
- `/api/demo-proof`: scope `public-proof-brief` through the worker's global edge gate (`enforceRequestRateLimit`), which runs before the loader, so an exhausted bucket never reaches the proof-brief cache read. The #2964 route-level D1 bucket (fail-open) is superseded.
- `/auth/*` and remaining public scopes (`/status`, `/api/*` reads, writes, webhooks, delivery-status): dispatched by `rateLimitPolicyFor` through their edge binding, fail closed.
- D1 atomicClaim stays ONLY for cost-bearing routes: authenticated search, search-selection, billing, share-pdf caps and share-pdf single-flight.

**Platform contract (verified against the generated runtime types, the wrangler 4.123 config validator, the official Runtime API docs, and the local miniflare shim):** the Rate Limiting binding carries its capacity in config (`simple: { limit, period }` — only 10s/60s periods) and the runtime call is `limit({ key })` with no per-call rate override. So each scope gets its own binding (`RL_AUTH` 2/60s, `RL_SEARCH_ANON_BROWSER` 2/60s, `RL_PROOF_BRIEF` 3/60s, `RL_SEARCH_SELECTION` 3/60s, `RL_SEARCH_IP` 10/60s, `RL_BRAND_PAGE` 12/60s, `RL_WRITE` 60/60s, `RL_STATUS` 120/60s, `RL_DELIVERY_WEBHOOK` 180/60s, `RL_API_READ` 240/60s, `RL_WEBHOOK` 300/60s), declared in `wrangler.jsonc` and mirrored in `wrangler.e2e.jsonc` + the integration `wrangler.test.jsonc`. Legacy 10-minute budgets keep the same sustained rate per 60s (20/10min → 2/60s; 30/10min → 3/60s; 120/10min → 12/60s); how many requests may arrive back-to-back in a burst changes; sustained throughput does not. `/status` advertises no hard numbers, so no doc drift.

Degraded modes now return 429 + Retry-After (binding missing, edge limiter throwing, D1 cost-path error) instead of silently admitting unbounded traffic. The scope-named observability logging introduced by #3059 is preserved on the remaining D1 paths, now reporting fail-closed. `keyByIpOnly` is honored on the D1 atomic-claim path too (share-pdf keeps its IP-only budget: UA rotation must not mint fresh buckets on a cost-bearing route).

## Verification

- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → 358 test files, 4482 tests, 0 failures, exit 0.
- Full `--project workers` suite (real workerd + real local D1 + REAL local edge limiters): 67 test files, 331 tests, 0 failures — including the six suites that CI showed red on the first push (ads/brand/timeline + verified-bot), now exercising the actual binding wiring.
- `namespace_id` deploy failure fixed and pinned: the first cut invented descriptive namespace ids (`"0509-rl-auth"`), which every worker unit test accepted but Cloudflare's deploy validator rejected — `binding RL_WEBHOOK of type ratelimit must have valid namespace_id [code: 10021]`, red on the required `preview-assert` check after a full build+upload round-trip. The documented contract is "a string containing a positive integer that uniquely defines this rate limiting namespace within your Cloudflare account" (chosen by the config author; no Cloudflare-side resource to create). All 11 bindings now carry unique integer-string ids (`1001`–`1011`) in all three configs, and `tests/rate-limit.server.test.ts` gained a committed-config guard (`describe("RL_* edge binding configuration (#2985)")`) asserting, per config file: the declared scope set matches the tested set, every `namespace_id` matches `/^[1-9][0-9]*$/`, ids are unique, and each `simple.limit` matches the capacity the tests count against. Verified the guard catches the real bug: re-injecting `"0509-rl-auth"` fails with `RL_AUTH namespace_id must be a positive integer: expected '0509-rl-auth' to match /^[1-9][0-9]*$/`; restored, the file is 35/35 green.
- Burst proof, 429 + Retry-After:
  - "an exhausted burst returns a labeled 429 with Retry-After from the edge limiter" — tests/demo-proof.rate-limit.test.ts
  - "distinct cold queries from the same browser still 429 once the edge browser budget is spent" — tests/search.route.test.ts
  - integration: verified-bot sweep leaves the anonymous brand-page budget full — first 12 pass, 429 + Retry-After inside the bounded overshoot loop (tests/integration/rate-limit-verified-bot.integration.test.ts, real local edge limiter)
- Zero D1 writes on the public path: "across a full burst, zero rows touch the D1 hot path (the #2964 fail-open write path is gone)" — tests/demo-proof.rate-limit.test.ts
- Fail-closed gates: binding missing → 429 + `Retry-After: 60`; edge limiter throws → 429 (tests/rate-limit.server.test.ts).
- `npx wrangler types` → exit 0; the 11 `RL_*: RateLimit` bindings present in the generated `worker-configuration.d.ts`, and `RateLimitOptions` confirms the `limit({ key })` contract the code now uses.
- `sgscan --base origin/main` → exit 0 (one INFO: unsafe-formatstring, pre-existing pattern).

run-proof: vitest --project node --changed origin/main exit 0, 4482/4482 passed; full vitest --project workers exit 0, 331/331 passed with the real local RL_* edge limiters; npx wrangler types exit 0 with the 11 RL_* bindings in worker-configuration.d.ts; sgscan --base origin/main exit 0; the new namespace_id config guard proven to fail on the injected `0509-rl-auth` value and pass on the fix (35/35 in tests/rate-limit.server.test.ts)

mechanical-fix: shipped as tests — fail-closed 429 gates (binding missing / limiter throws / burst→429 / zero-D1-writes) in tests/rate-limit.server.test.ts, tests/demo-proof.rate-limit.test.ts, tests/search.route.test.ts, plus the real-binding integration proof in tests/integration/rate-limit-verified-bot.integration.test.ts, plus the committed-config guard that pins every `namespace_id` to a unique positive-integer string and every `simple.limit` to the tested capacity across all three wrangler configs (the #10021 deploy failure cannot return silently).

test-removal-justified: the removed assertions belonged to the D1 fail-open counting mechanism that #2985 deletes for public scopes; the replacement edge Rate Limiting implementation is gated by the new fail-closed burst/missing-binding/limiter-throw/zero-D1-writes tests and the real-binding integration suite.

net-positive-because: not needed — the diff is net-negative overall (public counting moved off D1; ~1000 lines of D1 hot-path limiter deleted).

## Test plan

- CI: vitest node + workers projects, typecheck (cf-typegen regenerates the binding types CI-side), deploy gates.
- First production deploy after merge: confirm the 11 `RL_*` bindings materialize on the deployed worker (wrangler.jsonc `unsafe.bindings` with `simple` capacities), then a manual burst against `/api/demo-proof` / `/search` returning 429 + Retry-After.

loose-ends: the RL_* bindings must be confirmed present on the next deployed worker (config-only until then); the live-URL burst→429 proof needs that deploy, which is CI-gated and not done locally. The deploy-time `namespace_id` validation is exercised by the required `preview-assert` check on this PR (it uploads the PR head as a real Worker version); a fully local reproduction is impossible because the account API token lives only in GitHub secrets.

## Follow-ups found while landing this

- `codex-node-checks-shard-4` was red for a reason unrelated to this PR: `tests/public-status-counters.test.ts` hardcoded a digest timestamp that aged past the 7-day `DIGEST_STALENESS_THRESHOLD_MS` on 2026-09-12, flipping `digestHealth` to `"stalled"`. Reproduced on clean `origin/main` and confirmed blocking five other open PRs (#3194, #3183, #3181, #3169, #3164). Filed as #3212 and fixed in PR #3213 — a one-line clock-relative fixture, since a required check going red for every PR is a fleet-wide blocker.
- This branch had committed its own PR-body scratch copy (`.fleet/pr-body-2985.md`), which failed the `Vale (whole content tree)` gate on the word "granularity" after every code check had passed. Untracked it and extended the existing worker-scratch ignore section to cover `.fleet/pr-body-*.md`, so `git add -A` cannot re-add one.
title: fix(rate-limit): public hot path to the native Rate Limiting binding, fail closed 429+Retry-After (#2985)

## What

Observe-to-close coverage canary for the #3095 metric: sitemap `/timeline/`-URL count rising from the 7-domain seeded baseline toward the `/ads/` count, never below.

Why no publish-gate diff: the COVER set is already fully data-driven on main (prior art #2961 + #2881). `app/lib/sitemap.server.ts` lists a `/timeline/:domain` the moment its first proof-complete, non-ad-destination `landing_page_snapshot` row lands, and `/timeline/:domain` renders an honest noindex "collecting" 200 for every tracked `/ads/:domain` without one — newly captured brands publish automatically and no empty page can ship. The 2026-09-12 live counts (7 of 114) are the data-side gap #3018 (snapshot persistence) owns; publishing the existing corpus does not wait on it, and there is nothing more to publish until more proof-complete rows land.

This PR ships the issue's mechanical-fix detector: `scripts/canary-timeline-coverage.mjs` fetches the live sitemap, counts both cohorts, and applies the #3095 termination rule (`covered > 7` AND `covered >= 0.8 * adsCount`) — plus `npm run canary:timeline-coverage` and a 13-case unit test locking the parser (bare `/ads/:domain` + `/timeline/:domain` locs only; receipts and the `/timeline/` index ignored; absolute-URL support) and the verdict thresholds (7-of-91 fails at floor 73; 80-of-91 passes).

Exit-code contract: 0 = at/above the 80% floor above baseline; 1 = below floor (the documented expected-red while #3018 is pending — never a shipping-empty regression, because unlisted domains render noindex); 2 = sitemap unfetchable/unparseable (probe failure, not a coverage verdict).

Relates to #3095

## Verification

```
$ node scripts/canary-timeline-coverage.mjs
timeline-coverage canary (https://0509.io at 2026-09-12T02:57:18.020Z)
- /ads/ cohort: 114
- /timeline/ covered: 7
- floor: 92 (0.8 * 114)
ratio: 6.1% (baseline 7)
verdict: FAILED — covered=7 needs >7 and >=92. Expected while
landing_page_snapshot population (#3018) is pending; publishing empty
pages instead is forbidden (no-empty-page rule).
exit=1   (documented expected-red — the observe-to-close state)

$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main
 Test Files  759 passed (759)
      Tests  9699 passed (9699)
   Duration  202.66s

$ sgscan --base origin/main
No new security findings.   (exit 0)
```

run-proof: `node scripts/canary-timeline-coverage.mjs` executed live 2026-09-12T02:57:18Z against https://0509.io — verdict FAILED, exit 1, the documented expected-red (coverage 6.1% of the 80% floor while `landing_page_snapshot` population #3018 is pending). No new unit/timer/workflow is added, so the fleet-ops#378 armed-without-ran drill does not apply; the canary's observed behavior (exit 1 expected-red now, exit 0 once #3018 lifts coverage, exit 2 on probe failure) is test-locked in tests/timeline-coverage-canary.test.ts. The volunteer omission is deliberate and documented in the script docstring: NOT armed on a systemd rail while the verdict is expected-red — a pinned-red timer adds noise, not signal; arming (ops/<guard>/ sibling pattern, ops/demo-brand-timeline-guard/) is a one-command follow-up once the capture pipeline lands.

net-positive-because: +476 lines ship the detector the issue's mechanical-fix (fleet-ops#366) requires — observe-to-close, so the day proof-complete snapshots land for the tracked cohort (#3018), the #3095 metric climbs autonomously and the guard goes green with zero further code; the test locks the parser's ignore-set and the exact issue thresholds (7→80 of 91) so the guard cannot silently drift.

## Test plan

- `npm run canary:timeline-coverage` — live probe, exit 1 = expected-red (documented), exit 0 = metric met.
- `npx vitest run tests/timeline-coverage-canary.test.ts` — 13 cases: parser (bare locs, absolute URLs, receipts/index ignored), verdict thresholds, CLI exit codes, `--file-issue` dedupe, fixture dry path.

## Rollback

`git revert` of this one PR restores the pre-canary tree — publish gate untouched, no data touched (issue rollback clause: "restrict the publish gate back to the seeded set — one revert; no data touched" — the gate never changed).

## Checklist

- [x] Execution IS the review — live canary run + 9699/9699 changed-tests green + sgscan clean before this PR
- [x] Data-driven, not an allowlist: detector counts, never hardcodes domains (acceptance 4)
- [x] No empty pages: relies on the #2881 complete-proof sitemap gate + #1441-#1442 no-empty-page rules (acceptance 1/2)
- [x] #2961 indexing contract respected: detector counts exactly the locs that contract publishes (acceptance 3)

The condition it recorded is measured by the fleet production-stale alert (fleet-ops#5785, PR 5814) and dispatched to a flagship repair seat. No test, check, or deploy gate is removed or weakened; the auto-revert decision logic is untouched; close-halts-on-green stays until the backlog is 0.

Its 5-minute Actions cron never delivered real liveness (median 63 min between runs, 300 observations 2026-07-25..2026-08-11) and queued behind CI on the three-runner FIFO. Production liveness is owned by the `0509-liveness` systemd timer on the VPS (`ops/liveness/`), active since 2026-08-30 at a true `*:2/5` cadence.

- Ledger row carried: `docs/ci-gates-ledger.md` After-table records the deletion metrics (26 → 25 workflow files, 0 PR-job delta — the check never ran on PRs).
- Docs updated to name the timer as the liveness owner: `ops-backup-uptime.md`, `launch-readiness.md`, `launch-owner-actions.md`, `ga-owner-actions.md`, `final-self-serve-ga-scorecard.md`, `.claude/skills/verify-0509/SKILL.md`.
- `tests/uptime-health-workflow.test.ts` rewritten as a deletion guard: the workflow file stays absent and the `ops/liveness/` units stay shipped.
- `tests/self-hosted-node-cache-workflows.test.ts` and `tests/launch-docs.test.ts` updated for the removal.

test-removal-justified: uptime-health workflow deleted; its shape tests collapse into a deletion guard asserting the file stays gone and the systemd timer units remain the liveness owner.

## Required checks

## Summary

The public /timeline/:domain surface covered 7 of the 115 tracked /ads/ domains. The publish gate itself was already data-driven and correct — the gap was in the nightly capture cohort's evidence read: the tier verdict (`getSitemapTimelineTierByDomain`) only trusted search-v2 `domainMatch` enrichment, and the live cache rows for legacy `meta_library_browser` payloads (e.g. adidas.com, 2026-09-11) carry **no `domainMatch` at all**, so `hasCoverage` stayed false and the cohort never captured those landing pages. The measured corpus:

- `landing_page_snapshot`: 50 rows total; the only proof-complete rows belong to the 5 demo brands + adspyder + calendly — exactly the 7 sitemap timelines.
- adidas.com's newest `public_search` row: 15 ads, **zero** `domainMatch` fields, yet `landingPageUrl: "https://www.adidas.com/"` — the same payload that backs the indexable /ads/adidas.com page under the #1442 verified-link rule.

Same evidence standard, no phantom capture: when a payload has zero domainMatch coverage, the verdict now falls back to `adHasVerifiedDomainLink` — the exact rule the /ads populated-vs-thin gate already trusts. The fallback set is exactly the /ads indexable set, so newly covered brands publish automatically through the existing gates (acceptance 1/2/4); the proof gate and no-empty-page rules are untouched.

## Relates to #3095

Relates to #3095 — this is the public-surface coverage coverage-fix actor; the observe-to-close guard lives in PR #3163.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/sitemap-timeline-backfill.server.test.ts tests/sitemap.server.test.ts tests/sitemap-ads-no-redirect.test.ts` → 3 files, 115 passed
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → 7 files, 94 passed
- new tests: `(n)` legacy payload without domainMatch flips `hasCoverage` false→true via verified landing-page links; `(o)` a landing host on a different registrable domain does NOT mint coverage
- sgscan since origin/main → no new security findings

## run-proof

- worker cron: `sitemap_timeline_backfill` rides the 04:00 UTC daily rail (`workers/app.ts` daily-monitoring branch, with `reportScheduledTaskFailure` on failure); this PR widens its candidate tier verdict — after the next nightly run the cohort includes the tracked /ads cohort under the cap (`SITEMAP_TIMELINE_COHORT_CAP=200`)
- live evidence 2026-09-12 (logged-out curl): `https://0509.io/sitemap.xml` → 115 `/ads/` locs, 7 `/timeline/` locs; `/timeline/adidas.com` → 200 collecting (noindex, correctly unpublished — snapshot corpus absent for it today)
- termination check (post-deploy, next nightly): `curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -o 'timeline/[^<]*' | wc -l` rises toward the /ads count as nightly captures accrue, capped at the honest gate

## research

`lib/research` (fleet-ops#517 checklist): read the live prod D1 corpus (read-only) + sitemap code before writing code — confirmed the publish gate was data-driven and the gap was the cohort tier verdict's stale evidence read, avoiding a hand-list allowlist rewrite (the rejected alternative in the issue).

## help-first

Not needed: `adHasVerifiedDomainLink` was already exported from `app/lib/brand-page.server.ts` and used by the /ads gate; this PR imports it, adds no new `bin/` file.

## organ-heartbeat

`app/lib/sitemap-timeline-cohort.server.ts` — not an organ: no heartbeat/agent-lifecycle responsibility lives there; it is a read-only D1 adapter for the nightly cohort.

## loose-ends

net-positive-because: the coverage gap is a stale evidence read in the cohort tier verdict — the durable fix is a data-driven fallback gate + two pinning tests (+112/-1); without it the public /timeline surface stays frozen at 7 of 115 domains forever.

loose-ends: verify post-deploy sitemap timeline growth after the next 04:00 UTC nightly run (handled by the PR #3163 observe-to-close guard).

## Review round (one round, seat: minimax/MiniMax-M3)

Reviewer audit of the diff origin/main...HEAD against the #3095 acceptance criteria and repo tests — verdict: nothing BLOCKING; phantom-capture audit passed (fallback is literally `adHasVerifiedDomainLink`, the same function the /ads gate calls), demo-skip + fall-through + 200-capture spend cap all hold, tests honest and green (152 pass at review time).

- **Act on:** none.
- **Consider (acted on):** fallback now mirrors the /ads gate's non-demo filter exactly (`ad.source !== "demo"`) — hardened in the follow-up commit; 37 cohort tests re-green after the harden.
- **Consider (not re-delegated):** partial-enrichment payloads under-report verified counts vs the /ads gate — metric cosmetics only, `hasCoverage` is true either way; no gate asymmetry.
- **Noted:** null/object guard readability — correct (`&&` binds tighter), left as is; mixed demo ads in a non-demo payload cannot exist (whole-payload `isDemoPayload` filter still runs first).
- **Dismissed-with-reason:** "fallback uses a looser evidence standard" — disproven: same helper, unmodified.

## Test plan

- Unit: the new `(n)`/`(o)` cohort-tier tests plus the full affected `--project node` suite.
- Live: next nightly cohort run; the /timeline sitemap count rises without any empty page (proof gate unchanged).

## proof: archive landing-page captures at desktop_default alongside mobile_default

Closes #3105

Work salvaged from this unit's earlier reaped session (claim released by heartbeat with no live worker), re-based onto current main, re-verified end to end, and repaired twice: (1) the salvaged SQL in `artifactReferencedOutsideCapture` had one bind value too many (14 binds / 13 placeholders), which made every proof-artifact delete report `r2_failed` and broke `tests/launch-cleanup-guard.test.ts` (2 failures) — fixed to 13/13, suite green again; (2) a typecheck error in the new integration test (TS18048) found by the review round — fixed per repo convention.

## What changed

- `app/lib/browser-run.server.ts` — after a successful persisting mobile capture, a best-effort **desktop evidence leg** (1280x800, desktop UA, `desktop_default` profile) runs on the **same already-open browser session** (no second provider launch) with the same SSRF guard and the same bounded caps (`MAX_RENDERED_HTML_BYTES`, `MAX_RENDERED_SCREENSHOT_BYTES`, `SCREENSHOT_CAPTURE_ATTEMPTS`, `SCREENSHOT_CAPTURE_TIMEOUT_MS`). Its artifact pair is persisted with `customMetadata.renderMode: "desktop"`, `deviceProfile: "desktop_default"`, and its keys are folded into the same snapshot's metadata (`desktopRenderMode`, `desktopHtmlArtifactKey`, `desktopScreenshotArtifactKey`). The mobile leg stays the single extraction, diff, and alert source — `readSnapshotRenderMode` still reads `renderMode` (mobile).
- Skips are honest, never phantom: `desktopCaptureFailed: <true reason>` metadata (`desktop_capture_skipped_persist_disabled`, `desktop_capture_skipped_no_artifact_bucket`, `desktop_html_oversized`, `desktop_artifacts_not_persisted`, `desktop_capture_failed`, `desktop_capture_skipped_browserless_fallback`) plus `desktop_capture_failed` warning codes on real failures. A desktop-leg failure never fails the mobile capture. BET 4 / #2873 capture-failed visibility untouched (`tests/integration/capture-failed-visibility.integration.test.ts` green).
- `app/lib/proof-artifact-retention.server.ts` + `app/lib/retention.server.ts` — inventory, outside-reference checks, retention sweep, and compensating cleanup now also cover the desktop artifact keys, so desktop evidence ages out **with** its snapshot and never orphans in R2.
- No `migrations/**` touched (diff is empty there): desktop keys live in `metadata_json` freeform; the renderMode/device_profile columns already existed. One-phase-by-construction.

## Verification

Real runs on this branch (worktree `issue-0509-3105`, node `vite` workers project applies real `migrations/*.sql` to local workerd D1):

```
$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project workers tests/integration/landing-page-dual-viewport.integration.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
      Duration  2.77s
$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main
 Test Files  366 passed (366)
      Tests  4682 passed (4682)
$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project workers tests/integration/retention-sweep-state... tests/integration/archive... tests/integration/landing-page-snapshot-persistence... tests/integration/landing-page-snapshot... tests/integration/price-tier-swing... tests/integration/saucony-watchlist... tests/integration/timeline-brand-attribution... tests/integration/capture-failed-visibility...
 Test Files  8 passed, Tests 28 passed
$ sgscan
No new security findings.
```

The new integration suite drives the exact production capture path (`captureBrowserRunSnapshot`) against real workerd D1 + real migrations and an in-memory R2 recorder, and asserts: (1) one capture stores TWO screenshot artifacts labelled `renderMode: mobile` and `renderMode: desktop` (deviceProfiles `mobile_default` / `desktop_default`, per-leg viewport + UA), (2) the dual set persists on one `landing_page_snapshot` row (`screenshotArtifactKey` + `desktopScreenshotArtifactKey`), (3) a failed desktop leg records `desktopCaptureFailed: "desktop_capture_failed"` with the warning code and still captures mobile — one event, one alert source.

run-proof: npx vitest run --project workers tests/integration/landing-page-dual-viewport.integration.test.ts → 1 file / 3 tests passed, exit 0 (issue verify command; no new units/timers/workflows in this PR)

net-positive-because: the issue's metric is a second stored artifact per capture — new desktop capture leg + desktop-key coverage across retention/inventory/compensation + a 213-line real-migrations integration suite are the deliverable, not incidental lines.

organ-heartbeat: app/lib/browser-run.server.ts not-an-organ: product capture-path module; no timer/exporter/guard/canary added or changed.

loose-ends: historical-capture backfill — pre-existing mobile-only snapshots are not re-captured at desktop; the issue's rollback note covers stored artifacts (harmless evidence rows). Forward-looking only, by design.

## Review round (senior seat: minimax / MiniMax-M3, one round)

Review adjudication (diff `origin/main...HEAD` vs issue acceptance + repo tests; reviewer reproduced both verify runs green on the pre-fix head):

**Act on (fixed before arming):**
- 🔴 BLOCKING: `npm run typecheck` failed on the branch — TS18048 `appEnv.DB` possibly undefined at `tests/integration/landing-page-dual-viewport.integration.test.ts:180`. Fixed in the pushed head (`appEnv.DB!`, exactly the repo convention used by `capture-failed-visibility.integration.test.ts:41` and `error-report-sink.integration.test.ts:28`); integration suite re-run green 3/3 after the fix; final typecheck proof rides the PR CI round-trip (worker memory-budget rule: no local `tsc -b`).

**Consider (follow-ups, not arm-gates — recorded, not re-delegated):**
1. Desktop-leg browser time is not attributed in `browser_job_telemetry` (the leg row's `recordRun("succeeded")` is written before the desktop leg runs) — nightly budget attribution under-counts the ~2× capture spend. Follow-up candidate: record the desktop leg as its own telemetry row.
2. Desktop leg re-navigates `targetUrl` but labels artifacts with the mobile leg's `canonicalUrl` — a redirect variation on the second hit could mislabel the desktop HTML's `sourceUrl`. Bounded by the SSRF guard; evidence-fidelity only.
3. Three skip markers (`desktop_capture_skipped_persist_disabled`, `desktop_capture_skipped_no_artifact_bucket`, `desktop_capture_skipped_browserless_fallback`) are untested. The acceptance-required suite covers the success and hard-failure paths.

**Noted:** plain-HTTP captures carry neither renderMode nor a desktop skip marker (pre-existing metadata shape, no phantom claimed); desktop page not explicitly `close()`d (browser `finally` covers it, mirroring the mobile leg); `requireScreenshot` + failed-mobile-screenshot can persist desktop artifacts for a discarded snapshot (same orphan pattern as the mobile HTML artifact on main); desktop `screenshot_too_large` merges into shared `captureWarningCodes` (harmless — no consumer switches on these codes).

**Dismissed (with reason):** "second alert source" — structurally impossible: one capture, one snapshot, `readSnapshotRenderMode` still reads `metadata.renderMode` (mobile); "schema change needed" — `render_mode`/`device_profile` columns exist since migration 0007 and desktop values were already in `PROOF_RENDER_MODES`/`PROOF_DEVICE_PROFILES` on main; "protected verifier files touched" — diff is app/lib + tests only; "retention leaks desktop artifacts" — all four reference scans plus compensation cover the desktop keys.

## Test plan

- `npx vitest run --project workers tests/integration/landing-page-dual-viewport.integration.test.ts` (issue verify command) — 3/3
- `npx vitest run --project node --changed origin/main` — 4682/4682
- CI owns the sharded full suite + typecheck round-trip (memory-budget rule: no local coverage/typecheck)

perf(edge-cache): cover the full anonymous marketing route set + Authorization bypass

Closes #3193

## Root cause (measured)

- Live origin of the TTFB spike: production is running a build that predates the
  #2950 anonymous public-HTML edge cache — live `/` responses carry a per-request
  CSP nonce (the pre-#2950 shape) and no `x-0509-edge-cache` stamp at all, and
  `cf-placement: remote-NRT` puts the render in a remote colo for a Hamburg
  eyeball. Measured this session (TTFB in s): 1.04 ✓200, 0.87 ✓200, 3.02 ✓200,
  1.00 ✓200 — every request pays a full uncached origin render.
- The deploy carrying PR #3054 (edge cache), merged 2026-09-12T05:52Z, has never
  reached production: its own deploy run was cancelled, and every later
  "Deploy production" run is failing the scheduled-task gate with
  `source_backup_migration_ledger_stale` in `Generate D1 remote restore evidence`
  (runs 1031/1032 exit 1), with run 1035 still `pending` and run 1033 stranded
  `queued` in `Prepare D1 remote restore evidence`. That is the deploy chain,
  which this issue forbids touching — filed separately.
- Product gap actually fixable here, per the termination spec: the shipped
  #2950 edge cache only covered a short enumerated allowlist. `/brands`,
  `/brands/:category`, `/guides`, `/guides/:slug`, `/compare` (index),
  `/compare/{keeptabz,gethookd,bigspy,minea,poweradspy}` did not ride it, and the
  gate had no Authorization-header bypass.

## What shipped

- `workers/security-headers.ts`: `PUBLIC_CACHEABLE_HTML_PATHS` now includes
  `/brands`, `/guides`, `/compare`, the five missing vendor `/compare/*` pages
  and `/switch/magicbrief`; `PUBLIC_CACHEABLE_HTML_PREFIXES` adds `/brands/` and
  `/guides/` so future brand categories and guides are covered wholesale.
- `workers/edge-cache.ts`: `isEdgeCacheableHtmlRequest` additionally refuses any
  request carrying an `Authorization` header (a credential — never anonymous,
  never shared-cached, never seeds the cache).
- Reuses the existing #2950 cache (nonce-free variant, cookie-free gate,
  (path, country, deploy-version) key, 200/no-set-cookie/max-age store gates,
  x-0509-edge-cache proof header). No Cloudflare zone cache rules touched; the
  deploy chain untouched.

Verification (real runs):

- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/worker-edge-cache.test.ts tests/worker-security-headers.test.ts` → 2 files, 48 tests passed.
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → 9 files, 96 tests passed.
- `sgscan` → "No new security findings."

run-proof: unit pi-issue-0509-3193; CI round (tests/e2e) is the typecheck and the green visitor probe after the jammed deploy chain lets this land.

Test plan:
- tests/worker-edge-cache.test.ts: new families eligible; Authorization bypass; existing 404-outsider and logged-in cases unchanged.
- tests/worker-security-headers.test.ts: short browser caching stamps cover /brands, /brands/:category, /guides, /guides/:slug, /compare, missing /compare/* pages.

organ-heartbeat: workers/edge-cache.ts not-an-organ: named-cache consumer, no registered-organ surface
organ-heartbeat: workers/security-headers.ts not-an-organ: header policy module, not a watchdog

loose-ends: deploy-chain jam (source_backup_migration_ledger_stale) filed as a follow-up issue; the green visitor probe line must be re-run once a deploy carrying the #2950 cache + this change reaches production.

loose-ends: ttfb-probe-host — the 3059/964ms spread may be partly probe-host load; repeated curl from this box showed 0.87–3.02s before any fix, consistent with a stale uncached build on remote placement.

net-positive-because: the TTFB contract names a route set the shipped edge cache did not cover; the coverage additions are one-name entries on existing policy lists plus two prefix entries, and the Authorization gate is a new acceptance clause from the issue itself.

## Reviewer round (before arm)

- Seat: minimax/MiniMax-M3 (find_senior_seat; cursor skipped by gate). One round, review-adjudication buckets:
  - Act on: the stamping gate (`isPublicCacheableHtmlRequest`) did not bypass on Authorization while the edge-cache gate now does — FIXED in commit 2 ("align the stamping gate"), new test asserts the shared-cache license is withheld for Authorization-carrying requests.
  - Consider: none.
  - Noted: 404s under new prefixes can never be stored (200-only store gate, verified); Authorization bypass is bilateral (match + store both gate on eligibility); /brands//guides loaders are anonymous D1-backed marketing content, country-keyed; $locale twins left uncovered (canonical routes only per acceptance — follow-up if live samples show them slow); cosmetic duplicate `"/switch/magicbrief"` entry in the Set.
  - Dismissed-with-reason: "gate weakened" — diff is purely additive, no test relaxed.
- Second test run after the fix: `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → 9 files, 97 tests passed. sgscan: no new security findings.

## Summary
Auto revert has been 100% dead since AUTO_REVERT_PAT was wired: every run reacting to a failed Deploy production dies in `Revert or halt` with `GraphQL: Resource not accessible by personal access token (addComment)` (runs 34617396984, 34666013823). The PAT opens the revert PR fine — the refusal comes when the workflow posts the `gate-integrity-auto-revert:` attestation comment, which aborts before the `auto-revert` label flip and the `gh pr merge --auto` arm ever run. The revert PR then sits open, gate red (no waiver), unmerged.

## Fix
Post the attestation comment with `github.token` instead of the PAT. The workflow already grants the App token `pull-requests: write`, which is exactly the permission `gh pr comment` (addComment) needs on a same-repo PR; the PAT keeps its two existing duties (open the PR, arm auto-merge) which its grants already cover. One token, one purpose — least scope per call, no secret change needed.

## What this does NOT change
- The PR is still opened with AUTO_REVERT_PAT (so `pull_request` required checks fire on the revert branch — this is by design, not incidental).
- Auto-merge still armed by the PAT.
- No `|| true`, no softening, no gate weakening: the comment is still mandatory, `set -euo pipefail` still aborts if it fails. The failure now has a token that can actually succeed.
- Halts (loop/freshness/repeated-failure/non-assertion guards) are untouched.

## Verification
- `actionlint .github/workflows/auto-revert.yml` — clean (exit 0)
- `python3 -c yaml.safe_load` — parses
- `gh run view 34666013823 --log-failed` confirms the failure point is exactly the `gh pr comment` attestation line; the PAT opened PR #3075 successfully moments before (so pr create / push / label create / pr edit all pass under the PAT — only addComment is refused).
- PR #3075 timeline shows ORGAN-menace-1 comment posted by `nish3451` (the PAT), then closed as not-merged — the exact dead-end a live attestation would have prevented.

## run-proof
- Workflow: `.github/workflows/auto-revert.yml`, job `auto-revert`, step `Revert or halt` (`id: revert-or-halt`), plus `id: checkout-main` added for gate step-ID uniqueness.
- Live WFAIL evidence: run 34666013823 (`GraphQL: Resource not accessible by personal access token (addComment)`), run 34617396984, run 34616804927.
- The comment call now uses GH_TOKEN=${{ github.token }}; every other PAT-scope call is untouched.

## research
- `Auto revert` workflow read end-to-end before editing; `addComment` GraphQL error traced to the exact attestation `printf | gh pr comment` line via `gh run view --log-failed` of the three failing runs.
- `actionlint` and YAML-parse validated locally before push.

## help-first
- Token-grant debugging for fine-grained PATs (which scopes map to `addComment` on a PR comment): resolved by reading gh api / GraphQL error and testing with the repo's own existing github.token permission matrix — no external help needed.

## Test plan
- actionlint on the workflow.
- This PR's own gate-integrity row must go green on CI bots.
- Post-merge: next failing Deploy production should open + land its revert PR with no `addComment` abort; a green Deploy production closes open AUTO-REVERT HALTs (which require the workflow to not abort mid-flip).

Closes #2997

net-positive-because: 18 lines added / 16 removed — the attestation comment moves from the fine-grained PAT to github.token, which needs an extra env-override line and an explanatory comment block on the exact addComment failure (runs 34617396984 / 34666013823) so the next reader does not re-trace it.

loose-ends: if the PAT is ALSO deliberately scoped to not comment (worth checking with Nish), a fallback would be dropping the PR-body attestation for the label-based gate path entirely — but the gate-integrity decision script requires the comment, so this split-token approach is the minimal fix.


## Reviewer round (one round, pre-arm)
Seat: cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high (senior seat #3121 ladder head).
- Act on: none.
- Consider: add a one-line pin in tests/auto-revert-workflow.test.ts that `gh pr comment` runs with `GH_TOKEN="${{ github.token }}"` (falls to the label row, out of this PR's scope); the `FLEET_STEP_ID` step-ID gate scaffolding is unused after both steps have ids (left as-is, noise only).

## What
The flagship demo path (`/search?q=<demo brand>`) served `cache_only` with a dead-end "Fresh checks are delayed" note — the anonymous buyer's first impression. Root cause read of `app/lib/ad-source.server.ts`: the discovery provider cooldown re-arms on every failed capture (rate-limit 15 min, login-wall 10 min, extraction-failure 10 min), so a stuck provider (the live 404 landing capture) keeps re-arming the cooldown and every read serves stale `cache_only` for hours. This PR takes the issue's "honestly labelled with a retry" branch plus a canary; the fresh-on-demand branch (auto-triggering captures for demo brands) is a follow-up.

- `app/routes/search.tsx`: the delayed finished-result copy now has a "Retry this search" affordance beside the honest label (same path → re-arms the poll budget).
- `app/lib/demo-discovery-canary.server.ts` (new): read-only hourly observation (on the existing gap-check cron rail in `workers/app.ts`) of the five demo brands' public page-1 discovery cache entries, using the exact same cache-key construction the serving path uses; alerts the operator via the existing `reportScheduledTaskFailure` cron-failure path when a brand's freshest entry is older than 1h.
- `tests/demo-discovery-canary.test.ts` (new): 6 tests over real migrations (sqlite D1 helper) covering cache-key parity with the resolver and the >1h breach threshold + cooldown surfacing.

## Summary

Deploy gate `Generate D1 remote restore evidence` failed `source_backup_migration_ledger_stale` (run 34671488829). Diagnostics show prod `d1_migrations` ends `…0095_landing_page_snapshot_content_key.sql, 0096_error_reports.sql`: production applied `0096_error_reports.sql` while it was the tail, then `0096_email_suppression.sql` landed in the repo sorting *earlier*. D1's ledger is append-only, so no forward apply can reproduce sorted order — even after catching up, the exact-match assert would still reject.

The issue's premise ("declare the 16 retired names") was already satisfied: `RETIRED_PRODUCTION_MIGRATIONS` and the baseline have been `allowedProductionMigrationLedgers` defaults since #454. The real gap was ordering. This change:

- Adds `PRODUCTION_MIGRATION_LEDGER_ORDER_EXCEPTIONS` (`scripts/d1-migration-sync-check.lib.mjs`): declared groups of repo-suffix names in the exact order production carries them. Each applicable group emits one extra allowed-ledger variant — a strict permutation of the suffix, so unknown names, baseline members, and partial groups still fail closed.
- Threads `options.orderExceptions` through `assertMigrationLedgerMatchesRepository` / `unappliedForwardMigrationSuffix` / `planSourceBackupLedgerReconciliation` (core).
- Driver and `verify-remote-restore-evidence.mjs` now pass baseline + retired set + order exceptions explicitly into the planner, the post-apply assert, and the `allowedMigrationStates` evidence allowlist.
- When several allowed ledgers prefix-match with different suffixes, the primary repository-ordered ledger wins — a forward apply always appends in sorted order, so that suffix is the truthful plan (fixes the ambiguity-reject regression the reviewer found).

Verified against the actual prod ledger from run 34671488829: plan → `apply_forward_suffix` with exactly `["0096_email_suppression.sql"]`; post-apply ledger → `ok` + exact assert passes; ledger with an unknown extra name → still `reject`.

## Reviewer round (seat: minimax/MiniMax-M3)

- Act on: ambiguous-suffix reject when prod trails the whole exception group (fixed — repository-order suffix wins); duplicate variants for no-op groups (deduped); missing validation-branch tests (added); verifier now passes the constants explicitly.
- Noted: mid-exception gaps still reject by design (fail-closed); config errors intentionally skip ledger-name diagnostics; planner/assert share the same options so they agree.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts tests/d1-migration-sync-check.test.ts` → 44/44 pass (incl. new tests: real prod-ledger shape plans `apply_forward_suffix: [0096_email_suppression.sql]`; ledger behind the whole group plans `[0096_email_suppression.sql, 0096_error_reports.sql]`; one unknown extra name still rejects; invalid exception declarations throw)
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → 96/96 pass (3 files)
- `sgscan --base origin/main` → no new security findings
- `crgate` → could not run: "CodeRabbit is not signed in on this machine" (exit 3)
- Node repro on the real prod ledger (108 names from run 34671488829 diagnostics): `apply_forward_suffix [0096_email_suppression.sql]`; post-apply `ok`; unknown extra `reject`; allowed ledgers = 2 (sorted + prod-order variant)
- `bin/fleet-no-agent-names-check --pr-body --commit-range origin/main..HEAD` → OK

run-proof: this PR's own `Deploy production` evidence job is the live check — per issue accept, the evidence job must plan apply_forward_suffix (or ok) against the real prod backup and one `Deploy production` run on main must reach Deploy Worker.

Note: this PR does not hand-edit the prod ledger, does not weaken the unknown-name reject path, and does not retry/dispatch deploys.

Closes #3174
