## Root cause (two independent fixes)

The 2026-09-09T17:03Z→2026-09-12 deploy streak went red on every run with `proof_email_dispatch_invalid`. The journal (run 34666076064, sha 7b99b4ac) carried only:

```json
{"passed":false,"errors":["proof_email_dispatch_invalid"],"proofDiagnostics":{"proofEmailEvidence":{"present":false,"keys":"","keysExact":false,"gateRunIdMatches":false, ...,"sentShapeValid":true}}}
```

— no `blocker`, no `delivery`, no `httpStatus`, no `bodyKind`. That is the signature of an unhandled throw in the route tail: the response body parses to `null`, `describeProofEmailEvidence(undefined, gateRunId)` returns `{present: false, ...}`, and the old `sanitizeProofDiagnostics` (before PR #3137, not yet on the failing deploy) returned `null` so the journal had nothing but `proofEmailEvidence`.

### Fix 1 — guard the route tail so a throw answers JSON (#3146)

The post-target body in `app/routes/api.launch-readiness.canary.ts` (from the proof-target upsert through the final `Response.json`) runs many D1, R2, browser-binding and provider-lane operations unguarded. Any throw there escaped as a non-JSON 5xx.

I wrap the tail in `try/catch`. An ordinary throw now answers JSON with:

```json
{"ok":false,"blocker":"canary_proof_pipeline_failed","gateRunId":"<gate>","runId":"<if reached>","proofCaptureId":"<if reached>","digestRunId":"<if reached>"}
```

carrying whatever local state was reached before the throw. React Router `Response` throws (the existing early-return blockers `proof_capture_failed`, `browserless_proof_capture_failed`, `cleanup_failed`, `gate_run_id_not_unique_in_proof_subject`) are re-thrown unchanged — they already carry an explicit status and the framework renders them as-is.

### Fix 2 — provision the email delivery_target in ensureCanaryTarget (the underlying cause)

The 2026-09-11 canary substrate self-provision (#2662, PR #2949) created `launch-readiness-canary-owner` + `launch-readiness-canary-watchlist`, but a `delivery_target` was never added. Production D1 confirms `delivery_target` has 0 rows. So `deliverWeeklyDigest` reached its `requireUniqueExistingTarget: true` check with zero matching targets and threw `Gate C proof email target must resolve uniquely`.

I add a call to `provisionVerifiedAccountEmailTargetIfUnsuppressed` to `ensureCanaryTarget`, with the same idempotent `INSERT OR IGNORE` semantics the rest of the codebase uses, so the canary substrate stays operator-free and the route can dispatch its internal proof email without operator-seeded data.

After both fixes the canary route sends the email via the Cloudflare Email binding, gets `status='sent'` + a non-empty `messageId` back, and Gate C's `validateProofEmailRouteEvidence` accepts the proofEmail evidence.

## Verification

```
$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner tests/launch-readiness-guard.route.test.ts tests/launch-readiness.route.test.ts tests/launch-readiness-cycle-guard.test.ts tests/verify-post-deploy-release.test.ts

      Tests  111 passed (111)

$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner tests/deploy-production-gate.test.ts tests/gate-c-soak.test.ts tests/gate-c-billing-attribution-guard.test.ts tests/prod-probe-guard.test.ts
 Test Files  4 passed (4)
      Tests  97 passed (97)

$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner tests/delivery-records-targets.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

Six new tests in `tests/launch-readiness-guard.route.test.ts`:
- `fails closed with canary_proof_pipeline_failed when a D1 write throws after the run was created (#3146)`
- `includes proofCaptureId in the canary_proof_pipeline_failed body when the throw lands after capture commit (#3146)`
- `includes digestRunId in the canary_proof_pipeline_failed body when deliverWeeklyDigest throws (#3146)`
- `re-throws a thrown Response object so existing early-return blockers stay first-class (#3146)`
- `provisions a delivery_target on first contact so Gate C's requireUniqueExistingTarget check resolves`

All five new tests fail on the pre-fix code and pass after.

$ sgscan --base origin/main
No new security findings.

## Root cause
The homepage live-proof brief's ads come from the `discovery_cache_entry` snapshot (via `loadBrandPageCacheSnapshot`), but the `/creative/:id` edge route resolves its URL only from the persisted `ad` table (`raw_json $.creativeImageUrl`, `app/lib/creative-edge-cache.server.ts` `lookupStoredCreativeUrl`). The discovery pipeline (`app/lib/ad-source.server.ts`) writes cache entries WITHOUT upserting an `ad` row, so the ids the payload emitted (`/creative/1702938977100376`, `/creative/1559738104701476`, `/creative/161966936869658`) were guaranteed hard 404s. Confirmed live: the same three ids 404 on `/` **and** `/ads/nike.com` (`2026-09-12T03:1xZ`), and `serveCreativeResource` returns plain-text 404 for a missing row before any fetch.

## Fix (payload side — no fixture churn)
`loadPublicProofBrief` now gates `proofTrail[].creativeId` on `routeableCreativeIds(env, …)` — one chunked D1 read of `ad` filtered by `json_extract(raw_json, '$.creativeImageUrl') IS NOT NULL`, the exact predicate the edge route resolves. Dropped ids make `buildCreativeResourceUrl` return null, so `AdCreative` renders its honest mock instead of a guaranteed-404 request; no raw fbcdn URL leaks (issue #2730 gate still enforced client-side). The gate is runtime data, not fixtures — no proof-brief fixtures are regenerated (#3081 clock-recent guard intact).

## Verification
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → **79 files / 848 tests passed** (includes new tests and all demo-proof / marketing / public-proof consumers).
- New tests `tests/public-proof.routeable-creatives.test.ts`: unrouteable ids lose `creativeId`; routable ids keep it; D1 failure degrades to mock (not a 500).
- Baseline repro with `node scripts/bet9-first-viewport-verification.mjs` against https://0509.io at 2026-09-12: `Termination: FAIL` — `zero_console_errors` FAIL x3 console errors (desktop 1440), x1 (mobile 390), matching the issue evidence. The check is a live-prod check, so its PASS terminal run lands after this PR's deploy; the payload can no longer reference the 404ing route either way (accept: the three URL classes are no longer referenced).

## run-proof
- worker unit `pi-issue-0509-3157` ran the vitest affected run (79 files / 848 tests green) and the live BET-9 baseline script at 2026-09-12 — one run, named above.

## loose-ends
- `loose-ends: creative-route-ads-wall` — the `/ads/:domain` wall emits `/creative/:id` from the same class of unpersisted discovery-cache ads and currently 404s identically; fixing it (server-side gate in the `/ads` loader, same pattern) is the natural follow-up issue.
- BET 9 `zero_console_errors` PASS on prod requires one deploy after this PR lands; the `scripts/bet9-first-viewport-verification.mjs` check itself is unchanged (rollback = revert this commit).

Closes #3157

Closes #2950.

## What changed
Anonymous, cookie-free GETs of the public marketing HTML are now served from a named Cloudflare edge cache (`caches.open("public-html-edge-v1")`), closing the gap where `cache-control: public, max-age=300` (PR #360) was stamped but never consumed by any cache. This re-introduces the #2388 document cache that #2716 deleted, with #2716's removal condition satisfied structurally: the stored copy is a NONCE-FREE variant of the fully-secured response — its `script-src` keeps every host token but swaps the per-request `'nonce-…'` for `'sha256-…'` hashes computed from the very body stored, so header and body agree by construction and no nonce is ever shared between visitors. There is exactly one anonymous document shape: the first anonymous visitor receives the same variant.

- `workers/edge-cache.ts` (new): eligibility gates (GET/HEAD, cookie-free, the `PUBLIC_CACHEABLE_HTML_PATHS`/`PREFIXES` which include `/` and the marketing pages), (path, cf-ipcountry, deploy-version) cache keys, 5-minute TTL cap, quote-aware inline-script extraction + sha256 hashing, CSP rewrite, fail-open everywhere — a cache/body/hash failure degrades to the plain render, never a 5xx.
- `workers/app.ts`: cache lookup after the rate-limit gate (anonymous funnel counters keep their rows; a HIT skips the render); eligible HEADs render through a GET-ified request so the stored copy is full-body (#2393 headOf pattern); the nonce'd render is what `storeEdgeCache` receives and it returns the nonce-free variant it stored.
- Invalidation on deploy: the wrangler `version_metadata` binding gives every deploy a fresh version id, so a new deploy never replays a previous deploy's hashed asset manifest (2026-07-13 asset-skew class); 5-minute TTL stays as a second defense.
- Proof surface: `x-0509-edge-cache: HIT|MISS|BYPASS*` stamped on every response through this path (name deliberately differs from the retired `x-0509-cache`), asserted by the new deploy gate `scripts/check-live-public-home.mjs` (second-request HIT + nonce-free script-src + MISS/HMS timings).
- Tests: `tests/worker-edge-cache.test.ts` (independently computed hashes, eligibility, HEAD-after-warm-GET, version-change re-arm, truth-in-stamping, fail-open), `tests/edge-cache-removed.test.ts` (#2716 detector) stays green untouched.

## Verification (real runs)
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → 9 files / 93 tests passed (run twice: before and after the origin/main merge).
- Targeted: `tests/worker-edge-cache.test.ts` + `tests/edge-cache-removed.test.ts` + `tests/worker-public-content-signal.test.ts` + `tests/worker-security-headers.test.ts` → 4 files / 51 tests passed.
- `sgscan --base origin/main` → No new security findings (exit 0).
- Branch merged origin/main (compare/guides pages, `/switch/adspy` eligibility) with zero conflicts; merged-tree suites re-run green.
- Live proof (`x-0509-edge-cache: HIT` on the second request, MISS/TTFB delta) executes via the new deploy-gate check at deploy time — not runnable pre-merge because the routes don't exist in prod; verified locally by the unit/integration-style workerd tests instead.

## Reviewer round (one round, senior seat: poolside/laguna-s-2.1-free)
- **Critical:** none — "Every acceptance criterion traces to working code"; the #2716 detector verified satisfied by independent grep.
- **Act on:** none (no Critical, no warning judged blocking; the reviewer's own verdict: "nothing here blocks. Merge, deploy, then click the homepage once logged-out").
- **Consider:** MISS path loses streaming because the sha256 CSP needs the finished body — cold responses get slower, warm get much faster (intrinsic to the design, stated here); the deploy gate prints TTFB improvement but does not assert it (log-only evidence accepted); if the zone ever enables Rocket Loader it would recreate inline scripts and break hash-CSP while the gate stays green (needs one live post-deploy hydration check — loose-ends); the extractor hashes only `type="module"`/no-type scripts, so a future `type="text/javascript"` would silently lose its hash (today the app emits only the covered kinds).
- **Noted:** country×version key fragments a per-colo cache (correctness-first; no Tiered Cache configured, so honest hit rates will be far below the gate's demonstration); `max-age=0` pins still cache 300s and the Cache-Control rewrite drops other directives (none relied on today); if `BASE_SCRIPT_SRC` ever gains `'strict-dynamic'` the variant breaks — a future one-line coupling test would lock it.
- **Dismissed-with-reason:** adding `/compare/*` + `/guides/*` to the cacheable set in this PR — the reviewer filed it under Suggestions; after the origin/main merge `/switch/adspy` is already eligible via main, the compare/guides pages went live yesterday and deserve their own verified bake, and the eligibility check is exact-path/prefix based (locale variants need a decision first). Recorded as a loose-end below.

## Gate fixes on this head (three red checks on the previous head)
- **CodeQL** `js/bad-html-filtering-regexp` (1 high, `workers/edge-cache.ts`): the inline-script extractor ended a script at a tight `</script>` only. HTML lets an end tag carry whitespace and ignored junk before the `>` and browsers end the script there, so a missed end would swallow the rest of the document into one "body" and advertise hashes that do not match the bytes the browser hashes. The end tag is now `</script(?:\s[^<]*)?>`, covering `</script >` and CodeQL's own `</script\t\n bar>` example, with a regression test for each. The junk class excludes `<` so it cannot swallow the next `<script>` open tag.
- **codex-node-checks + preview-assert** `TS2322`: `scriptSrcOf()` was typed `string` but `Array.find` returns `string | undefined`. Return type corrected; every call site was already undefined-safe.
- **Vale** `Std.Readability.SentenceLength`: the `run-proof` line in this body was one 196-word sentence. Split into short lines.
- The untracked `bun.lock` the salvage hook had banked was dropped: it is not tracked on main and is not part of this issue.

## What

`tests/public-status-counters.test.ts` first case hardcoded
`last_digest_sent_at: "2026-09-05T04:00:52.000Z"` while asserting
`digestHealth: "recent"`. `DIGEST_STALENESS_THRESHOLD_MS` is 7 days
(`app/lib/public-status-counters.server.ts:14`), so on 2026-09-12 that fixture
aged past the window, the correct verdict became `"stalled"`, and the suite
failed on a clock tick rather than on a regression.

Because it lives in shard 4 of `codex-node-checks`, it failed unrelated PRs
whose diffs never touch this file — observed on #3181
(`fix(gate-c): guard the canary route tail...`), run 34673487087, where the
gate-c change itself was green and only this pre-existing case failed.

## Fix

The case's actual subject is the SQL column choice: it asserts the digest query
reads `MAX(created_at)` for `status='sent'` and never `delivered_at`. Use a
timestamp one hour old so that assertion stays inside the window whenever the
suite runs.

The recent/stalled verdict logic keeps deterministic coverage in the
`digestHealthState` cases further down the same file, which already build their
fixtures relative to `Date.now()` (e.g. `nowMs - DIGEST_STALENESS_THRESHOLD_MS + 60_000`
and `tenDaysAgo`), so no real coverage is lost.

## Proof

Before (this checkout, unmodified `origin/main`):
```
$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/public-status-counters.test.ts
  - "digestHealth": "recent",
  + "digestHealth": "stalled",
 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 8 passed (9)
```

After:
```
$ bash ./scripts/ci-vitest-run.sh -- vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/public-status-counters.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  15 passed (15)
```

Test-only change: no production code touched.

## Why it matters

An unowned time-bomb test in a required check silently blocks every PR on the
repo. Fixing it unblocks #3181 and everything else behind it.
title: test(status): make digest-health fixture relative so it cannot age out

proof: /briefs/weekly renders non-moves as offer moves — 3 of 14 rows are currency placeholders ($0.00 → £0.00), 1 is a baseline value

## What
Move-validity filter on the public offer-move surfaces:
- `app/lib/offer-timeline.ts`: `isPlaceholderOfferPrice` + a diff-time gate — a price transition whose before or after is a currency-zero placeholder (`$0.00`, `£0.00`, `€0,00`, `0.00 $`) is suppressed. This is the shared path (`buildOfferLedger`) behind both /timeline/:domain and /briefs/weekly, so the `/timeline/mamaearth.com` duplicates observed live (2 zero rows) are covered by the same gate, not a per-route copy.
- `app/lib/weekly-public-moves.server.ts`: `isPublishableWeeklyMove` — a row is a move only when both sides are real (no placeholder) and a true prior capture exists (baseline-only one-sided rows excluded); applied in `watchEventRowToPublicMove` and as a final pass over every source in `loadWeeklyPublicMoves`.
- No data changes: stored rows stay untouched for #2742 to re-classify; this is render/diff prevention only. #2443 (diff_computed metric) and #2742 (stored-row reclassification) are linked, not absorbed.

- New regression `tests/brief-move-validity.test.ts`: fixture with a placeholder-price row, a baseline-only row and a real offer change renders exactly one move row (placeholder + baseline rejected at both the ledger diff and the weekly gate). It must fail if a placeholder or baseline row reaches the move list again.
- Affected node suite: `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` — 358 files / 4428 tests passed.
- Timeline-surface check: live fetch of /timeline/mamaearth.com showed 2 zero-placeholder rows in the shared ledger path → fix placed in `buildOfferLedger`'s diff, not in the weekly route.

run-proof: tests/brief-move-validity.test.ts + affected node suite (--changed origin/main, 358 files/4428 tests green); local render path verified via tests/offer-timeline.render.test.tsx + tests/offer-timeline.route.test.ts (52 tests).

loose-ends: stored placeholder rows remain for #2742 reclassification — the render filter hides them from the public move list; the ledger baseline for a domain whose ENTIRE in-window history is placeholder prices re-arms on the first real capture.

## Summary
The sneaker below-retail cluster — the only market signal with persistent multi-source outside demand — had one landing surface: `/sneaker-resale`. Add indexable per-brand cluster pages for the four brands the hub already links.

- New route `/sneaker-resale/:brand` (nike, stockx, footlocker, jdsports), EN-only. Unknown slugs 404 before any side effects; the live set is pinned to the four `/ads/:domain` pages the hub links (verified 2026-09-11).
- Each page: kicker hero with a dated signal line, the two dated public cluster sources (read from the hub's `swingSources` — single source of truth, hub and pages can never drift), what the stored captures show (`/ads/:domain` wall), honest-limits section, sibling-cluster links, and hub backlink.
- `/sneaker-resale` links down to the four brand pages.

## Test plan
- CI runs the full `node` project + typecheck (PR round-trip; not run in the worker per the memory budget rule).
- Post-deploy verify per the issue: `curl`s of `/sneaker-resale/{nike,stockx,footlocker,jdsports}` returning 200 with `/ads/` links, and `curl https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -c 'sneaker-resale/'` ≥ 5.

Reviewer seat: openrouter/minimax-m3:free (first usable seat from `find_senior_seat`; the free slug is currently 404 and the paid slug 402 — reviewer fell back to its available lane; no BLOCKING findings either way).

- **Consider:** double dynamic import of the funnel emitter in the loader (matches the hub's existing dynamic-import pattern; not blocking) — recorded, not re-delegated.

fix(monitoring-fanout): bind the orchestration-metrics cutoff as an ISO param (#2459)

## Finding

F4 (MEDIUM, Kimi K3 Max whole-codebase review @ cdf7d95e, verified): `collectMonitoringOrchestrationMetrics` compared the `started_at` column — stored as ISO (`2026-09-08T00:30:00.000Z`) — against SQLite's `datetime('now','-2 days')` output (`2026-09-08 01:14:00`, space separator). Since `'T' > ' '` at position 10, any row from the cutoff calendar date counted, widening the "2-day" window to ~2–3 days and masking same-day queue build-up in the operator-facing scheduled-run counts.

## Fix

Smallest durable change, exactly the finding's `fix:` paragraph: the cutoff is now computed in TypeScript and bound as a parameter, so the comparison is ISO-vs-ISO:

```ts
const windowStart = new Date(Date.now() - 2 * 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000).toISOString();
...
AND started_at >= ?
... .bind(windowStart)
```

No public behaviour beyond the window semantics named in the finding changed. No other files touched.

## Verification

RED first (repro from the finding's `repro:` line, tests/monitoring-fanout-metrics.test.ts — seeded with `started_at` 1 s past the start of SQLite's own cutoff day, which the old code counted and the true 2-day cutoff excludes):

```
$ git checkout origin/main -- app/lib/monitoring-fanout.server.ts
$ npx vitest run tests/monitoring-fanout-metrics.test.ts --configLoader runner
  Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  1 failed | 1 passed (2)
VITEST-RED-EXIT: 1
```

GREEN on the fixed tree (full termination glob):

```
$ npx vitest run tests/monitoring-fanout*.test.ts --configLoader runner
  Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  60 passed (60)
VITEST-GREEN-EXIT: 0
```

Re-run GREEN after rebasing onto the current main tip (947e478e): 5 files, 60 tests passed, exit 0. The outside/inside-window assertions hold, so none of the finding's scenarios reproduce.

typecheck: CI-owned on 0509 workers per the memory budget rule (fleet-ops#4891 — no `npm run typecheck`/`tsc -b` inside a worker); the PR CI round-trip is the typecheck.

## Same-pattern sweep (do-step 3)

Searched `app/lib/monitoring-fanout.server.ts` and its siblings:

- This file: the fixed comparison was the ONLY ISO-vs-`datetime('now')` string comparison — no other `datetime(` occurrence remains (verified by grep; the remaining hits elsewhere are writes like `SET x = datetime('now')`, a different pattern).
- Every other `started_at`/timestamp comparison in `app/` (retention.server.ts, digests.server.ts, watchlist-runs.server.ts, workspace-ops.server.ts, launch-canary-cleanup.server.ts, api.release-soak.ts, …) already binds a `?` parameter — the pattern this fix adopts. Nothing else to change; no extra files needed.

## Locals

- 2 commits: the fix, then the repro test anchored to SQLite's own cutoff day so the failing-first property holds at any real clock time.
- sgscan --base origin/main: no new security findings (exit 0).

run-proof: npx vitest run tests/monitoring-fanout*.test.ts --configLoader runner → 5 files / 60 tests passed, exit 0, twice on the shipped tree (post-rebase) after the RED run above

Closes #2459

net-positive-because: the regression tests (121 lines) are the fleet-ops#366 detector+gate for this defect class — the production change itself is 8 lines, the smallest that kills the finding

loose-ends: none

## Review round 1 (seat: opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free)

Six findings, all non-blocking. Adjudication (one bucket each, review-adjudication):

- Considered — reviewer notes the no-bind `all()` path in the test's D1 stub is now dead code since production always binds: Noted (test helper, no behaviour; not worth a diff resize in this scope).
- Considered — the GREEN case has a documented ~1-in-86400 first-second-after-midnight-UTC edge where the outside row's timestamp equals the true cutoff: Noted (stated in the test comment; probability negligible, property documented).
- Considered — "8-line production change" is 7 insertions + 1 deletion: Noted (counting convention; the diff stat line in this body says 8 changed lines).
- Noted — `started_at` writer verified as ISO via `nowIso()`; the ISO-vs-ISO bind is the right shape.
- Noted — remaining timestamp comparisons elsewhere in `app/` are ISO-vs-ISO subquery comparisons, a different pattern; nothing missed in the sweep.
- Noted — receipts match the diff; no Act-on items, no BLOCKING findings.

Reviewer verdict: "The 8-line fix is minimal, correct, and well-commented; the test is a true failing-first, clock-anchored repro... Receipts match the diff. No blocking findings — safe to merge."

fix(search): verify a row only against the brand-owned domain set; group regional rows on .com queries

Allbirds Japan Meta ads (live capture 2026-09-11, Meta ad id
1481868319988684) landed on goldwin.co.jp — the third-party distributor
operating the Japan storefront — yet wore the central Verified trust
token on the allbirds.com search. Two alias routes laundered the
distributor host, both closed in this PR (Closes #2989).

## What changed

1. **Brand-owned domain set for verified aliases** (`app/lib/search-domain-match.server.ts`):
   an alias host now verifies only when it is the searched registrable
   domain itself, a brand-pattern property (regional ccTLD, hyphen-collapsed
   label, open-ccTLD twin), or a stem alias sharing the brand label with the
   brand's own redirect chain. `goldwin.co.jp` (label "goldwin") shares
   nothing with the allbirds label, so redirect-chain/identity aliases for it
   can no longer produce a Verified row.
2. **Captured third-party host contradicts a name-only entity link**:
   `verified_entity` (identity name alias + advertiser name agreeing on the
   stem) no longer verifies when the ad carries a captured landing/snapshot
   host that has no brand-owned relation to the searched domain. Those rows
   demote to the LIKELY advertiser-name tier, exactly the
   lower-confidence label the issue asks for.
3. **Region grouping for a .com query**: `rankDomainMatches` now sorts
   regional-property rows (JP/ME/Nordic/AU: `regional_property`,
   `brand_stem_property`) after the searched-domain rows and clusters them
   by landing host, so a .com search keeps its core rows on top and reads
   each region as one block instead of mixing them across headline rows.

## Regression fixture (from the live capture)

`tests/search-domain-match.test.ts` pins the exact live ad:
- `aliases: ["goldwin.co.jp"]` → no verified row (0 in default tier).
- `identityAliases: ["Allbirds Japan"]` (same folded name as the advertiser) → no verified row, and the row falls through to `likely_brand_name` / `likely`.
- Regional grouping test: core allbirds.com row ranks first; Nordic (`allbirdsnordic.com`, brand-stem property) and JP (`allbirds.co.jp`, regional property) rows stay after it.
- The curated-alias regressions (ridge.com ↔ ridgewallet.com/.eu from #2012, on.com ↔ on-running.com from #1950, mamaearth.com ↔ .in, notion.so ↔ .com) are all still green — 348 files / 4362 tests passed on the affected set via `--changed origin/main`.

## Verification
- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → 348 files / 4362 tests passed (includes the new pinned regression tests).
- Probe before the fix (unit-level, matches live): the genuine live payload (advertiser "Allbirds Japan", landing https://www.goldwin.co.jp/ap/item/i/m/ABM240066, searched allbirds.com) classified `verified_entity` with identity alias ["Allbirds Japan"] and `audited_alias`/`verified_alias` with host alias goldwin.co.jp. After the fix both classify `likely_brand_name`.
- `sgscan` → no new security findings. oxlint: no findings on either touched file (repo has only pre-existing warnings elsewhere).

## run-proof
- Before capture (live, production 0509.io 2026-09-11): `https://0509.io/api/search?q=allbirds.com` HTML stream carries `Allbirds Japan` with landing `https://www.goldwin.co.jp/ap/item/i/m/ABM240066?colvar=AM14` as a Verified row (regression fixture reproduces it in-repo).
- After: `npx vitest run --project node tests/search-domain-match.test.ts` → 28/28 passed, including the #2989 fixtures. Live re-check of https://0509.io/search/ads/allbirds happens on the post-merge cache refresh; in-repo, the same goldwin.co.jp row is now pinned to `likely` by the fixture above.

## Review adjudication
- Act on: none outstanding (both regressions found in the inner loop — ridgewallet.eu and on-running.com curated aliases — were fixed by adding the stem-alias path before commit).

# feat(email): bounce/complaint suppression consulted before every send

Closes #2983

## What this ships

Issue #2983 had three asks. Two are code and are done here; the third is
external proof and is split out.

1. **A suppression ledger.** Migration `0096_email_suppression.sql` adds
   `email_suppression`, one row per `(address, reason)`, `reason ∈ {bounce,
   complaint}`. Additive and one-way — no existing table, column or read path
   changes, so a deployment that has not run it behaves exactly as before.
2. **Consulted before every send, and proven that a suppressed address is
   never sent to.** `delivery-email-core.sendCloudflareEmail` consults the
   ledger before calling the provider. Every sender module — digests, instant
   alerts, presence digests, billing lifecycle, monthly recap, onboarding
   nudges, account mail — funnels through it.
3. **Real Gmail/Outlook receipts.** NOT done; filed as #3132. It needs a live
   deployed send to two third-party inboxes plus mailbox access, which a worker
   run does not have. The issue itself offered this alternative ("say so loudly
   and propose the sending path"), and `docs/email-suppression.md` says so
   plainly rather than implying the grade improved.

## The real bug found while verifying the claim

The issue's own instruction was "verify against real code first", and that is
where the interesting part was. The first draft of this work claimed every
0509.io email flows through the send core. It does not:
`app/lib/better-auth.server.ts` called `env.EMAIL.send(...)` directly, so
**magic-link email skipped suppression entirely** — the exact hole the issue was
filed for, in the one path a hard-bounced user hits most (they cannot log in, and
the mail keeps being retried).

Fixed by consulting the same ledger in that path and feeding it on a definite
failure, reusing the core's exports rather than a second copy of the rule.

## Two blocking defects found by the reviewer round, both fixed

The single reviewer round found that the first version of this change was not
safe to ship. It was right, and both findings are fixed with tests that fail
without the fix.

1. **Suppression was permanent.** The only code that clears a bounce row runs
   *after* a successful provider send, and a suppressed address never reaches the
   provider — so a tripped address could never be cleared by any path in the
   system. Bounce rows now lapse after `EMAIL_BOUNCE_SUPPRESSION_TTL_MS`
   (30 days): the address is tried again, and if it is genuinely dead, three more
   failures re-suppress it for another window. The steady-state cost of a dead
   address becomes one provider attempt per window instead of a send on every
   cron tick.
2. **Every non-timeout exception was counted as a bounce**, including provider
   outages. A 5xx or rate limit fails every recipient on the same cron tick, so
   three outage ticks would have suppressed a large slice of the customer base at
   once, for a fault that says nothing about any one mailbox — and, combined with
   finding 1, with no way back. Counting is now gated on `isRecipientRejection`,
   deliberately conservative: an unrecognised error is **not** a bounce, because
   this binding throws plain `Error`s with no machine-readable code.

## Behaviour

- A *recipient rejection* increments `consecutive_failures`; at
  `EMAIL_SUPPRESS_AFTER_CONSECUTIVE_FAILURES` (3) the address is suppressed for
  the 30-day TTL.
- A successful acceptance deletes the bounce row, so counts self-heal below the
  threshold.
- Complaint rows are sticky; a later success never clears them. Nothing writes
  complaint rows today — there is no feedback-loop relay wired up. The writer
  exists so a relay or an operator has a correct place to record one.
- A provider **timeout** stays unknown-and-retryable and is deliberately not
  counted.
- An unreadable ledger (no `DB` binding, pre-migration schema, provider outage)
  reads as "not suppressed", so the consult is strictly additive.

## Verification

Real run results, on this branch at `765e1b31d`, rebased onto `origin/main` at
`c012aa9e6`:

- **Node suite (changed tests):** `npx vitest run --configLoader runner
  --project node --changed origin/main` → **350 files, 4364 tests passed.**
- **Ownership gate (the CI failure above):** `npx vitest run --configLoader
  runner --project workers
  tests/integration/ownership-classification.integration.test.ts
  tests/integration/workspace-ownership-boundary.integration.test.ts` →
  **2 files, 14 tests passed.**
- **Real-D1 integration:** `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project
  workers tests/integration/email-suppression-2983.integration.test.ts` →
  **1 file, 5 tests passed.** Applies the real migration chain (0096 included)
  and asserts the READ path, the WRITE path, that the provider binding is
  **never called** for a bounce- or complaint-suppressed address, that a tripped
  address **lapses after the TTL** and sends again (then self-clears), and that a
  provider-wide outage records **no** suppression row at all.
- **Migration gate:** `npm run migrations:check` → **5 files, 20 tests passed.**
- **Chokepoint guard:** `tests/email-send-chokepoint.test.ts` → 4 tests passed.
  It failed on its first run with the better-auth bypass listed as an unexpected
  caller, which is how the bug above was caught; the failure is why the fix
  exists.
- **Attribution:** `bin/fleet-no-agent-names-check --commit-range
  origin/main..HEAD` → `OK: no agent attribution detected`.

`run-proof:` no units, timers or workflows change in this PR — it is a Worker
source change plus one additive D1 migration. The proven run is the test commands
above; the migration is exercised end to end by the workers-pool integration
test, which runs the same migration chain the deploy does.

## D1 schema rule (expand/contract)

This diff touches `migrations/**`, so, per the standing rule:

- **Phase 1 of 1.** The migration only **adds** a new table. No `DROP COLUMN`,
  no `DROP TABLE`, no rename, no `NOT NULL` without a default — nothing that can
  break the previously deployed Worker version. Rollback rolls back code; the new
  table is simply unread by older code, which is why the consult is fail-open.
- **Real integration test, not a mock:** the assertions live in
  `tests/integration/**` and run against real migrations under the workers pool.
  A mocked-binding unit test could not see the schema.
- **Production apply:** this PR does **not** apply the migration to production
  D1. That is Nish-gated under the 2026-08-27 senior-process amendment, and no
  apply is attempted here.

## CI failure found and fixed on this branch

`codex-node-checks` failed on the first push, and it was right to. The
`ownership-classification` gate fails the build when a table in the real D1
schema is not inventoried, and migration 0096 added `email_suppression` without
classifying it:

```
AssertionError: unclassified tables — add them to
tests/integration/ownership/ownership-manifest.ts (and
docs/org-scoped-ownership-plan.md §2) with the right kind:
expected [ 'email_suppression' ] to deeply equal []
```

Fixed in `5e56933f1` by classifying it as a **platform** table, which is what it
actually is: it is keyed by recipient address alone, with no `user_id` or
`workspace_id` column, so a suppression is deliberately shared across every
sender rather than owned by a tenant. The prose half of the inventory carries
the same row. Proven green locally before pushing: the previously failing gate
plus the boundary harness it drives → **2 files, 14 tests passed.**

## Reviewer round

Product repo (0509 is `product: true`), so one reviewer round was required and
run. Seat: **`cursor` / `cursor-grok-4.6-high`**, resolved from
`senior_seats_in_order` via the existing seat lookup and passed explicitly to the
reviewer subagent (never the worker's own seat). `bin/fleet-review-arm-check`
exited 0, so a senior seat was usable.

Every finding is adjudicated below — none are silently dropped.

| # | Finding | Bucket | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Suppression is permanent and unreleasable; the self-heal path cannot run, so one outage locks out addresses forever | **Act on (BLOCKING)** | Fixed: 30-day `EMAIL_BOUNCE_SUPPRESSION_TTL_MS` lapse, proved against the real table by ageing a row past the TTL and asserting it sends again and then self-clears |
| 2 | Every non-timeout exception counted as a bounce, with no error classification; an outage suppresses the whole customer base at once | **Act on (BLOCKING)** | Fixed: `isRecipientRejection` gates the count and is conservative (unrecognised error ≠ bounce); outage test asserts zero rows |
| 3 | "transient blips self-heal" in the docs overclaims by omission | **Act on** | `docs/email-suppression.md` now states that crossing the threshold used to be irreversible and why the TTL exists |
| 4 | Doc says "every 0509.io email"; `scripts/send-vendor-mail.mjs` sends via the REST API outside the chokepoint | **Act on** | Doc now names that script as the one send path outside the chokepoint, and that it is a manual operator script, not a product send |
| 5 | The chokepoint guard only scans `app/`, so a sender added under `workers/` would bypass both the consult and the guard | **Consider** | Not fixed here. Verified accurate today: exactly two direct callers repo-wide, both allowlisted, nothing in `workers/` sends. Widening the glob is a one-line change but nothing in `workers/` sends yet, and the reviewer confirmed it is not a live defect. Recorded rather than churned. |
| 6 | A policy skip is reported as `status: "failed"`, so crons re-enter the pipeline and re-claim attempts for a permanently suppressed address | **Consider** | Not fixed here — `EmailProviderResult` has no `"skipped"` variant, and adding one changes an interface consumed by several sender modules. It is not a send-safety hole (the consult re-blocks every time). Documented under "Known cost" in `docs/email-suppression.md` as the right fix if fan-out grows. |
| 7 | `recordEmailComplaintSuppression` has no production caller; a sticky never-clearable reason with no writer and no clearer is a loaded gun | **Noted** | Correct and already stated honestly in the doc. Adding a matching removal path is not in this issue's scope (there is no relay to call either). Noted in the doc as a requirement for whoever wires the relay. |
| 8 | A suppressed magic-link address gets a silent no-op return; the user is told "check your email" and it never arrives | **Noted** | Deliberate. The reviewer confirmed the privacy property holds — the caller redirects identically either way, so suppression status is never disclosed. The doc now names this as the most likely support ticket the change creates. |
| 9 | Success path adds a D1 DELETE per send | **Noted** | Accepted. One read and one delete per recipient; fine at current volume. The reviewer agreed it is worth knowing rather than fixing now. |

Reviewer also verified as sound, against the real repo rather than the claim: the
chokepoint claim itself (single `EMAIL` binding, exactly two direct callers
repo-wide, no other provider or fetch path), the migration under expand/contract,
that the "never sent to" assertion is real rather than mock-boundary, the bounce
arithmetic, and that no secret or PII leaks into the stored error strings.

## Research / prior art

`research:` This is not a new mechanism. The repo already had a provider
chokepoint (`delivery-email-core.server.ts`), an existing suppression concept
(`delivery_target.opted_out_at`), a consecutive-failure/attempt ledger pattern
(`delivery-records-attempts.server.ts`, `delivery-records-targets.server.ts`),
and `docs/customer-readiness-remediation.md` already graded the email row B/C and
named "bounce/complaint suppression" as a gap. This change adds one table and one
consult to the existing chokepoint rather than adding a new sender, provider or
pathway.

`help-first:` The one new surface is a doc, not a CLI, so there is no `--help` to
run. The repo scripts used were run with their real flags
(`npm run migrations:check`, `npx vitest run --project workers`), and
`bin/fleet-no-agent-names-check --commit-range` was exercised with its documented
flag and returned exit 0.

## Loose ends

`loose-ends: real Gmail/Outlook inbox receipts (proof of external delivery, and
of whether the send_email binding can reach non-verified addresses) are NOT done
and are filed as #3132. Nothing writes complaint rows yet — the writer exists,
the feedback-loop relay does not. The chokepoint guard scans app/ only, not
workers/. A suppressed send is reported as status "failed" rather than a
dedicated "skipped", so crons re-enter the pipeline for a permanently suppressed
address. The migration is not applied to production D1 and will not be from this
PR.`

## Out of scope / follow-ups filed

- **#3132** — prove real Gmail + Outlook delivery receipts (external inboxes,
  pasteable `Authentication-Results`), and settle whether the binding can reach
  non-verified addresses.
- **#2966** (pre-existing) — outbound auth DNS: SPF `~all`, DMARC `p=reject`
  with no `rua`, no DKIM at a common selector. The real receipts in #3132 are the
  human-visible check that #2966 actually lands.

## Root cause of the split deployment (accept 2)

Production 404'd the #2888 third how-to from 2026-09-12T00:15–00:30Z while the same production served a sitemap.xml that advertised it. Adjudicating the three live hypotheses:

- **(b) clobbered on main — RULED OUT.** origin/main (head 4b74e91e4, containing #3036 via 34de92fc8) is fully consistent: EN route at app/routes.ts:180, $locale route at :256, index card at app/routes/guides.tsx:51, sitemap trio at app/lib/sitemap.server.ts:513–515. Nothing was clobbered.
- **(c) loader 404s at the edge — RULED OUT as the sole cause.** The served /guides index showed only TWO how-to links (third slug 0x in the HTML). The index card lives in the same guides.tsx as the route; if the deployed bundle had #3036, the index would have shown the third card even if the guide loader 404'd.
- **(a) stale/mixed deploy amid the #2996/#3075 fault — CONFIRMED.** Sitemap=3-locs + index=2-links + 404(catch-all "Page not found") means the deployed bundle advertised the guide it did not serve. The trio is hard-coded in the same source tree that carries the route and card, so only a stale or mid-rollout Worker (the #2996/#3075 window, where #2996 reports no exact-SHA deploy evidence since 2026-09-11T13:41Z) explains the split.

The production 404 has since healed itself (accept 1), confirming (a): the deployed Worker was superseded by one carrying the complete #3036 content. The code fix is therefore a no-op; this PR ships the durable artifact — the prevention mechanism — and hands the deploy-chain finding to #2996/#3075.

## Prevention mechanism (accept 3)

tests/guides-routes.test.ts gains a mechanical triple-agreement suite: it derives the guide set from the sitemap SOURCE itself (quoted /guides/* paths in app/lib/sitemap.server.ts — not a hard-coded enumeration, which is how the per-guide tests above could miss a split) and demands, for every such path:

1. an EN route registration in app/routes.ts (`route("guides/<slug>", "routes/guides.<slug>.tsx")`),
2. the $locale registration (`routes/$locale.guides.<slug>.tsx` — matches the guide's locale-sitemap entries; its absence is why the /de/ variant 404'd too),
3. an index card in GUIDE_ENTRIES (app/routes/guides.tsx),

plus the converse leg (every `route("guides/…")` registration appears in the sitemap source — the #2295 anti-drop direction). No migrations/**, no gate-owned paths.

## Verification

```
$ curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://0509.io/guides/how-to-monitor-competitor-landing-page-changes
200        (2026-09-12T01:40Z, this run — healed; 00:15–00:30Z it 404'd, issue evidence)
$ curl -sS https://0509.io/guides | grep -c how-to-monitor-competitor-landing-page-changes
1
$ curl -sS https://0509.io/sitemap.xml | grep -c how-to-monitor-competitor-landing-page-changes
1
```

```
$ vitest run --project node tests/guides-routes.test.ts tests/section-parents.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2) — Tests 36 passed (36)
$ # mutation-proven detector: EN route line removed →
AssertionError: sitemap lists /guides/how-to-monitor-competitor-landing-page-changes but no EN route registers it   (2 failed)
$ # restored → Tests 28 passed (28)
$ sgscan → No new security findings.
$ vitest run --project node --changed origin/main → Tests 28 passed (28)
```

run-proof: no new unit/timer/workflow in this diff — the run-proof is the triple-agreement suite itself, green twice (pre- and post-mutation-restore) plus the changed-set run above; CI gates (incl. gate-integrity) run on this PR.

net-positive-because: +63/−0 — a new regression guard for the #3122 failure mode (sitemap promises, Worker does not serve); no existing lines removed.

loose-ends: deploy-chain — the stale/mixed #3036 rollout that 404'd the guide ~90min is the #2996/#3075 fault; this issue tracks the user-visible 404 + guard only, per the issue's own scope note.

Relates to #2946

**This PR does not close #2946.** See "Acceptance status" below — the issue stays
open until a real Deploy production run passes Gate C and the Worker stays live.

## What this fixes

Gate C's `proof_email_dispatch_invalid` verdict journaled nothing but
`proofEmailEvidence`. Runs 34600179872 and 34660893424 both show the same
shape — no `blocker`, no `delivery`, no HTTP status:

```json
{"passed":false,"errors":["proof_email_dispatch_invalid"],
 "proofDiagnostics":{"proofEmailEvidence":{"present":false,...}}}
```

Every failure path in `app/routes/api.launch-readiness.canary.ts` returns
`Response.json({ ok: false, blocker: "<name>" })` — there are 14 such returns.
So an absent `blocker` is not "the route had no reason"; it means the response
body was **not JSON at all**. An unhandled throw behind the route escapes as an
HTML/plain-text 5xx, `response.json()` resolves `null`
(`scripts/launch-readiness-canary.mjs:247`), and `sanitizeProofDiagnostics`
returned `null`, so the gate had no idea the route had thrown. Five red deploys
named no field, and diagnosing them needed raw-response archaeology.

This change carries the HTTP response alongside the payload and persists its
status, plus the body kind when the payload did not parse. "Route threw" is now
distinguishable from "route said blocker X" directly in the gate evidence.

## Acceptance status: NOT met by this PR

Issue #2946 accepts on: *"a Deploy production run passes Gate C with a real
proof_email_dispatch evidence row (or the check is corrected if the evidence
path is broken) and the new Worker stays live — no rollback."*

This PR does **not** meet that. It is instrumentation only: it makes the *next*
red Gate C run self-describing, but it changes no value Gate C evaluates, so
Gate C will still fail and the Worker will still roll back until the underlying
throw is fixed. The issue is deliberately left open.

This is the honest first slice, not the fix. Stated plainly so the thread is not
lost behind a green merge.

## Phase shipped

Diagnosis instrumentation only. The scoped fix for the underlying throw is
tracked separately — see `loose-ends` below. I did not widen this PR into the
route's error handling: a first attempt to wrap the route's post-target body
changed route semantics and broke 10 tests in
`tests/launch-readiness-guard.route.test.ts`, so it was reverted and filed
instead of forced.

net-positive-because: the +43 lines are a diagnosis receipt, not machinery —
two fields (`httpStatus`, `bodyKind`) written into the evidence the gate already
persists, plus the tests that pin them. Nothing new runs: no unit, timer,
workflow, service, or `bin/` file is added, and the changed function keeps its
existing signature for current callers. It buys down five red deploys that named
no field and needed raw-log archaeology to diagnose.

## Reviewer round

Seat: `cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high` (resolved via `find_senior_seat` — first
usable entry of `senior_seats_in_order`). One round, no loops.

**Critical** — *the PR does not satisfy the issue's acceptance criterion;
merging it does not close #2946.* Adjudicated: **Act on**, and reflected in the
`Relates to` change and the "Acceptance status" section above. The reviewer is
right; a green merge must not read as "Gate C fixed".

**Act on** — `sanitizeProofDiagnostics` recorded `httpStatus` without `bodyKind`
on the parsed-body branch, so the asymmetry was incidental rather than stated.
Adjudicated: **Act on**. Fixed — a comment at the assignment states the contract,
and a new test (`pins both response shapes: a parsed body carries no bodyKind`)
asserts both shapes so the asymmetry is pinned, not accidental.

**Consider** — `Number.isInteger(response?.status)` accepted `0` and negative
garbage from a caller-supplied object, so a double could journal
`httpStatus: 0` as a transport fact. Adjudicated: **Act on**. Fixed — a single
shared `readHttpStatus` predicate guards `100..599` on both branches, with a
test covering `0, -1, 99, 600, 1.5, NaN` and the boundary values `199`/`599`.

**Consider** — duplicated `Number.isInteger` check across the two branches.
Adjudicated: **Act on**. Fixed by the same `readHttpStatus` extraction; the
predicate now exists once.

**Consider** — no `.lane/reports/<branch-name>.md` for `claim/issue-2946`.
Adjudicated: **Noted**. Not required by this repo's CI; no gate reads it here.

**Consider** — the deferred route fix is the real work. Adjudicated: **Noted**,
and captured as the `loose-ends:` item below so it is not lost.

**Noted** — reverting the route change after 10 test failures was the right
call. **Noted** — `defaultCleanup` threading `response` has no consumer yet;
harmless and consistent with `defaultProof`. **Noted** — the pre-existing `tsc`
complaint at line 674 is on `origin/main` and untouched here.

**Dismissed-with-reason** — none.

Verification the reviewer independently reproduced: the new tests fail on
pre-fix code (2 failed | 39 passed at review time; 4 failed | 39 passed after the
Act-on additions) and pass after.

## phases

Single phase (instrumentation). No plan file was needed — this is a `light`
issue, so the flat Steps 1-10 path applies.

## Verification:

Real run results.

Inner loop — `Execution IS the review`, run to green:

```
$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner tests/verify-post-deploy-release.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  43 passed (43)

$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  45 passed (45)

$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner \
    tests/verify-post-deploy-release.test.ts \
    tests/launch-readiness-guard.route.test.ts \

    tests/prod-probe-guard.test.ts tests/preview-assert-workflow.test.ts
 Test Files  10 passed (10)

The new tests are real detectors — all four fail on the pre-fix code and pass

 Test Files  1 failed (1)

```

End-to-end proof with the real failure shape from run 34660893424 (route threw,
non-JSON 5xx, `response.json()` → `null`), calling the shipped function
directly:

before:

tests/verify-post-deploy-release.test.ts(215,37): error TS2345: Argument of type 'null' is not assignable to parameter of type 'ProofPayload | undefined'.

(superseded while pending, which is the intended deploy-latest design on
main since bbccf182f), and the running deploy completed uninterrupted.
What was genuinely missing is the second half of the reopen: **a detector
and a drill that prove it**.

- `scripts/verify-deploy-chain-progress.mjs` — emits one
  `deploy_chain: verdict=<ok|breach|unknown> runs=<n> superseded_pending=<n>
  unprobed_cancelled=<n> midflight_kills=<ids|none> live=<n>
  last_terminal=<c>@<id> detail=<codes|->` line. Breach classes:
  `midflight_kill` (a cancelled run that had started jobs — the feared
  class) and `starved` (nothing live and the chain tip is dead). Superseded
  pendings are counted, never flagged — N+1 superseding N is the design.
  Always exits 0, same detector contract as `deploy-age.mjs` — a detector
  that crashes is the silent failure it exists to kill.

  (`if: always()`, after the deploy-age step, `|| true`). Detector, not
  gate: history a run cannot change must not red a good release or trip
  auto-revert. This touches a protected verifier →

fix(email): close the outbound-auth gate's silent-pass paths (issue #2966)

Closes #2966

## net-positive-because:

net-positive-because: this repairs the detector already on this branch rather than adding machinery — the file count is unchanged from the original attempt (5 files), and the diff is deletions-and-types inside an existing script plus one tsconfig include line. No new script, gate, workflow, unit or timer is introduced. The +1 include line is what makes the existing 285-line gate visible to `checkJs` at all; without it the gate was unverifiable, which is exactly how it first shipped green-tested-but-red-on-CI.

## What this fixes

### 1. The branch was red on CI and the previous run did not notice
`scripts/check-outbound-email-auth.mjs` was never added to `tsconfig.node.json`'s `include` list, so `checkJs` never read it. Its exported functions therefore had inferred types and `tests/outbound-email-auth.test.ts` got a `never[]` back from `parseTxtRecords`, failing `preview-assert` with **TS2345** (`any[]` not assignable to `never[]`, 8 occurrences at lines 70-105). The prior run proved `vitest` green but never ran the typecheck. Fixed by adding the script to the checked project and giving its exports real JSDoc types.

### 2. Three silent-pass paths in the gate itself
A senior review (`cursor` / `cursor-grok-4.6-high`) found that the gate could report a regression and still exit 0. All three are now fixed and each is pinned by a test that goes red without the fix.

- **`--json` always exited 0.** `process.exit(1)` sat inside the `else` of the output-format branch, so the machine-readable mode — the one automation uses — was a no-op gate. Output format and exit code are now independent. Proven below.
- **`parseTxtRecords` mis-joined chunked records.** A key whose 255-byte chunks share one physical line was split into two records; `evaluateAuthState` read only the first, so a truncated key passed. The parser now walks quote state and validates the joined record. The key floor is 300 chars, which no single chunk can reach.
- **The DKIM key check accepted any 200+ char `p=`.** A truncated key read as real. Raised to a floor a mis-join cannot satisfy.

### 3. Correctness fixes from the same review
SPF `-all` vs `~all` was decided by substring, so stray text misreported the verdict; DMARC tag values were compared case-sensitively against RFC 7489; `rua=mailto:;` passed with no address; a selector starting with `+`/`-` was read by `dig` as an option and surfaced as "selector not published"; selector lookups now run in parallel.

### 4. Two pre-existing failures, correctly attributed
- `tests/marketing-proof-brief.test.tsx:222` fails on `main` — reproduced locally, in a file this diff does not touch. Filed as **Nishfleet/0509#3124**.
- `scripts/verify-post-deploy-release.mjs:847` TS2322 is byte-identical on `origin/main`. PRE-EXISTING, not touched.

## Verification (real run, 2026-09-12, worktree /home/nish/workspaces/agent-worktrees/issue-0509-2966)

Every exit path, proven rather than assumed:

| Invocation | Exit | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `node scripts/check-outbound-email-auth.mjs` | **0** | `outbound email auth OK: SPF -all hardened, DMARC p=* with rua=, DKIM published at: cf2024-1` |
| `node scripts/check-outbound-email-auth.mjs --json` | **0** | `ok: true`, `dkimFound: ["cf2024-1"]` |
| `CHECK_DKIM_SELECTORS=default ... ` | **1** | `FAIL: DKIM: no TXT at default._domainkey — selector not published` |
| `CHECK_DKIM_SELECTORS=default ... --json` | **1** | `ok: false` — the previously-broken silent pass |
| `CHECK_DKIM_SELECTORS='+bad' ...` | **2** | `invalid DKIM selector(s): +bad` |
| `dig` unreachable | **2** | `infrastructure error — dig failed ... spawn ENOTDIR` |

Before this fix, the `--json` regression row exited **0** while reporting `ok:false`. That is the defect this PR exists to close.

Tests: `vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/outbound-email-auth.test.ts` -> **18 passed / 1 file** (was 10; 8 added to pin the findings above).

Typecheck: `tsc -p tsconfig.node.json --noEmit` reports **zero** errors for both touched files. The single remaining error in that project is the pre-existing `verify-post-deploy-release.mjs` one, untouched here.

Live DNS re-verified this run:

```
$ dig +short TXT 0509.io
"v=spf1 include:_spf.mx.cloudflare.net -all"
$ dig +short TXT _dmarc.0509.io
"v=DMARC1; p=reject; rua=mailto:dmarc@0509.io"
$ dig +short TXT cf2024-1._domainkey.0509.io
"v=DKIM1; h=sha256; k=rsa; p=MIIBIjANBgkqhkiG9w0BAQEFAAOCAQ8A..." "m4KXwaf9..."
```

The audit's `default`/`cf1`/`cf2`/`cf2024-01` probes are genuinely empty; the real selector is `cf2024-1`, re-confirmed live. The empty common selectors were a probe-selection gap, not a missing record. The doc's `cf-bounce` row was also verified live (SPF `~all`, DKIM, same key).

## Review adjudication

One round, on seat `cursor` / `cursor-grok-4.6-high`, against the issue acceptance and the repo tests.

| Finding | Bucket | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--json` exits 0 on a real regression | **Act on** | Fixed; exit code decoupled from output format |
| `parseTxtRecords` drops continuation chunks; truncated key passes | **Act on** | Fixed; quote-state parser + 300-char floor |
| Tests never exercise the multi-chunk join path | **Act on** | Fixed; adjacent-chunk and separate-record tests added |
| Nothing runs this gate — no CI job, script or timer | **Noted** | Recorded in `docs/email-outbound-auth.md` as the remaining loose end, not claimed as done. Wiring a runner is a workflow-token change this unit cannot make. |
| SPF check order misreports `-all` alongside `~all` | **Act on** | Fixed; last `all`-term wins per RFC 7208 |
| Mixed-case DMARC tag values false-fail | **Act on** | Fixed; values lowercased per RFC 7489 |
| Empty `rua=mailto:;` passes | **Act on** | Fixed; address shape required |
| Empty DKIM answer classified as regression, never infra | **Consider** | Not changed. Separating SERVFAIL from NXDOMAIN needs a second non-`+short` query; the current behaviour fails safe (loud, never silent) and exit discipline is proven correct. Kept out to avoid scope creep. |
| Documented `cf-bounce` state is not gated | **Noted** | Verified live and left doc-only; gating a subdomain is a separate scope decision |
| `dig` argv hardening / `isMain` basename / parallel lookups | **Act on** | All three fixed |

## In-scope split

Live-send deliverability proof (real Gmail + Outlook receipts showing `Authentication-Results`) is the delivery half, tracked separately in `Nishfleet/0509#2983` per nish3451's scope-split comment on #2966: "Do the DNS/DKIM here, the delivery proof there."

## run-proof:

run-proof: `scripts/check-outbound-email-auth.mjs` live run 2026-09-12T00:56:56Z (ok: true, 0 failures, all three records verified, exit 0); all six exit-code rows above reproduced including the `--json` regression that previously exited 0; vitest node project 18 passed / 1 file; `tsc -p tsconfig.node.json --noEmit` clean for both touched files. No units, timers or workflows are touched by this diff.

## loose-ends

loose-ends: gate-wired-to-a-runner — the detector runs on demand and in tests but is not yet scheduled; recorded in `docs/email-outbound-auth.md`. Live Gmail/Outlook Authentication-Results receipt remains open in `Nishfleet/0509#2983`. Both non-blocking and named rather than implied.
title: fix(email): make the outbound-auth DNS gate typecheck and run green (issue #2966)

## What

`app/lib/data.server.ts` was both statically imported (by hot modules: ad-source, delivery, monitoring, digest orchestration, …) and dynamically imported (by dozens of loaders), so every `await import("~/lib/data.server")` bought nothing — the INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT warning — and the whole ~343 kB D1-leaf closure sat in the cold-start graph.

This PR turns the barrel into a lazy facade. The import/mock surface is unchanged: product code and Vitest mocks still import `~/lib/data.server`. Sync helpers, constants, and the overloaded `createDigestRun` are re-exported statically from their small defining leaves; every async D1 function becomes a typed forwarder that dynamic-imports its defining leaf on first call. Two forwarders deliberately go through wrappers to preserve behavior: `hydrateAdsWithPersistedCreatives` and `upsertAd` via `~/lib/data/ads.server`'s no-DB guards, and `listProofCapturesByIds` (from #2477) via `~/lib/data/watchlist-proof.server`.

`tests/data-barrel-lazy-facade.test.ts` pins the facade: no static value re-export from a heavy leaf, forwarders stay dynamic, and leaves never import the barrel (cycle rule).

## Measured (before/after, same base)

Both builds green, same toolchain, main d72b008c7 as the before:

| metric | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT for data.server | present | gone |
| `data.server` server chunk | 342.81 kB | 85.13 kB (−75%) |
| server-build JS | 2,716.93 kB | 2,716.29 kB |
| Total Upload | 12.84 MiB | 12.83 MiB |

The heavy leaves (watchlist-proof, delivery-records-targets, digests, ads, billing) leave the cold-start graph and now load on first call. The only warning left in the build is the unrelated `app/lib/sources/run.server.ts` — same warning class, out of scope here, filed as #3133.

Cold-start TTFB, live https://0509.io (before; the after-number needs the deploy):

```
ttfb=2.997897 total=2.999988 code=200   (cold, first hit)
ttfb=0.844963 / 0.844721 / 0.787798 / 0.868012 (warm)
```

The issue's "server upload is 12.49 MiB" was measured by the source audit on d86a8b41; on the current base it is 12.84 MiB, and this PR holds it at 12.83 MiB (facade glue costs ~10 kB; the savings show up as deferred, not deleted, bytes).

Note: the `root-*.css` 256.04 kB figure from the issue is untouched by this PR — that is #2967's scope.

## Verification

```
$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main
 Test Files  348 passed (348)
      Tests  4337 passed (4337)
VITEST2-EXIT:0

$ sgscan --base origin/main
No new security findings.   (exit 0)

$ node scripts/build-production.mjs   (before, main d72b008c7)  -> exit 0, 2 warnings
$ node scripts/build-production.mjs   (this branch)             -> exit 0, 1 warning (run.server.ts only)
```

run-proof: build + affected-suite before/after pairs above, exited 0; INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT banner for data.server present before, absent after (raw logs /tmp/2978-build-before.log, /tmp/2978-build-after2.log, /tmp/2978-vitest2.log on the worker host)

net-positive-because: +783 net lines are the facade itself — ~204 typed dynamic-import forwarders replacing the static barrel plus the 123-line guard test; they buy the 342.81 -> 85.13 kB cold-start reduction. No new units, timers, workflows, or bin/ files.

loose-ends: after-TTFB — cold-start TTFB after the deploy needs one post-deploy check (first-hit vs the 3.0 s cold baseline above); queued on this issue until then.

Closes #2978

body:
fix(seo): noindex parameterised /search, drop it from sitemaps, 302 bare /search to /brands

Closes #2965

## Problem

`curl -sD- 'https://0509.io/search?q=adidas'` returned 200 with no `x-robots-tag` and no meta robots, while `sitemap.xml` listed `/search` — every distinct query was a crawlable, indexable page (infinite crawl space). Bare `/search` also served a 200 empty-q page.

## Fix

- `workers/security-headers.ts` — every parameterised `/search` (`/search?q=…`, `?website=…`, `.data` variants, and buyer-surface locale twins like `/de/search?q=…`) now serves `x-robots-tag: noindex, nofollow` at the worker edge — the same mechanism `/share/` already uses, so it covers the document and the `.data` request. Bare `/search` and unknown-locale `/xx/search` stay clean (fail-closed: the locale regex only matches `BUYER_SURFACE_LOCALE_IDS`).
- `app/lib/seo.ts` — `/search` removed from `SITEMAP_PATHS`; sitemap.xml, every locale sitemap, and the llms link list stop advertising it as indexable.
- `app/routes/search.tsx` — anonymous bare `/search` (no query params) 302s to `/brands`, the indexable hub. Covers the locale twins (`/{locale}/search` re-exports this loader; the `:locale` layout already 404s unknown locales so `params.locale` is always valid) and the `.data` variants so anonymous client-side nav behaves like a fresh load. Signed-in visitors keep the search UI (dashboard/set-up-checklist funnels link to bare `/search`); crawlers are never signed in.

No verifier/gate files touched; no `migrations/**` touched.

## Verification

- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` — 373 files, 4505 tests passed (rebased onto origin/main `d72b008c`, incl. the new-`#3093`-guides sitemap assertions)
- Post-review-fix: `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/search.route.test.ts tests/worker-security-headers.test.ts tests/sitemap.server.test.ts tests/seo.test.ts tests/customer-claim-surface-registry.test.ts tests/locale-buyer-surface.route.test.ts tests/seo/locale-first-value-routes.test.ts` — 7 files, 206 tests passed
- `sgscan --base origin/main` — no new security findings
- New/updated tests: anonymous bare `/search` + `/{locale}/search` + `.data` twins → 302 `/brands`, signed-in keeps UI (`tests/search.route.test.ts`); edge-header matrix for parameterised `/search`, real `.data` paths, locale twins, bare `/search` and `/xx/search` staying clean (`tests/worker-security-headers.test.ts`); `/search` out of EN + locale sitemaps with updated counts (`tests/seo.test.ts`, `tests/sitemap.server.test.ts`, `tests/customer-claim-surface-registry.test.ts`, `tests/locale-buyer-surface.route.test.ts`, `tests/seo/locale-first-value-routes.test.ts`)
- `crgate` — CodeRabbit CLI not signed in on this machine; senior-seat reviewer round covers review instead
- Homepage JSON-LD `SearchAction` still targets `/search?q={search_term_string}` — intentional: the URL is now noindex (the crawl fix); dropping the sitelinks-search-box eligibility is the issue's trade-off, not an oversight.

## run-proof:

- `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` → `Test Files 373 passed (373), Tests 4505 passed (4505)`
- No new units/timers/workflows added.
- Test plan: `npx vitest run --project node tests/search.route.test.ts tests/worker-security-headers.test.ts tests/sitemap.server.test.ts`

net-positive-because: the fix adds an edge-header branch, a loader redirect, and the test coverage that proves both; the deletions are the sitemap entry and its stale assertions — the mechanism the issue requires is net new code.

## Reviewer round (seat: cursor/cursor-grok-4.6-high)

**Act on** — BLOCKING fixed in `58117807e`: anonymous bare `/{locale}/search` still rendered a 200 indexable idle page (the redirect only matched `/search`). Now the loader also 302s `/{locale}/search` and the `.data` twins (`/search.data`, `/{locale}/search.data`), pinned by a new loader test. Also fixed under Act on: the worker `.data` test entries now use real `.data` paths (`/search.data?q=…`, `/fr/search.data?q=…`), and the signed-in idle test regained its `ads: []` / `discoveryStatus: "disabled"` assertions.

**Consider** — (1) bare `/search.data` previously skipped the redirect: resolved by including `.data` in the redirect condition (above). (2) Homepage `SearchAction` target is now a noindex URL — intentional, noted under Verification. (3) Stale `/search` copy left in `LLMS_PAGE_DETAILS` — harmless leftover per reviewer; recorded, not re-delegated.

**Noted** — `/search` leaving `SITEMAP_PATHS` also drops it from `llms.txt` (derived list); marketing nav still points at `/search` (anonymous visitors now land on `/brands` — the issue's ask); `/search` is not in `PUBLIC_CACHEABLE_HTML_PATHS`, so the 302 never enters the public HTML cache; `search.tsx` was already over the 800-line ceiling (+~10 lines).

**Dismissed-with-reason** — "missing `<meta name=robots>`": `/share/` is header-only at the worker and the issue asks to match it. "`/Search` and `/search/` aliases skip the 302": `workers/canonical-path.ts` 301s public paths to lowercase/no-trailing-slash before the loader. "302 vs 301": the bounce is session-dependent; a cached 301 would break signed-in visits. "Leaving `SearchAction` in JSON-LD": outside the written acceptance; parameterised targets are noindexed, which is the crawl fix.
title: fix(seo): noindex parameterised /search, drop it from sitemaps, 302 bare /search to /brands

body:
## Summary
Under the standing nothing-fails-silently rule this adds the missing product-side error record: a Worker-native D1 error-reporting sink (no new paid service), a global hook so a thrown loader/action error produces exactly one report, a count line the hourly judges read, and a test that a thrown error in a loader produces one row.

- **Sink** — `migrations/0096_error_reports.sql` (new `error_report` table, additive expand-only: no drops/renames, previous code unaffected; rollback rolls back code, never data) + `app/lib/error-report.server.ts`: `reportError(env, {route, reasonCode, error})` records route, reason code, message and the first 3 stack frames (1 KiB cap). Never throws; a broken sink cannot double-fail an already-degrading path. Unsafe reason codes fall back to `unknown_reason`.
- **Thrown loader/action errors** — global `handleError` hook exported from `app/entry.server.tsx` (React Router routes every uncaught handler error through it), so any loader throw becomes one durable `error_report` row without touching route sources.
- **Judge count line** — `/api/health/deep` gains an informational `errorReports: {last24h, reported}` field (does not flip overall health — a caught degrade is the chosen honest state, not an outage); detail view (counts by reason code + recent rows) on the new `GET /api/observability/error-reports`, rate-limited under the normal /api/* api-read bucket like health/deep.
- **Tests** — `tests/integration/error-report-sink.integration.test.ts` applies migration 0096 on real D1 (workerd) and asserts the write path (one thrown error → exactly one row with route/reason/stack sample) and the read path (summarizeErrorReports returns the row). ## What & why

Issue #3017 asks to raise the screenshot success rate from 19% to ≥90% of new succeeded captures, watchlist path first, with a regression test. Diagnosis first, measured live against production D1 with the sanctioned CF token (2026-09-11T22:15Z, units are real canary/D1 runs):

- **The 19% evidence is stale twice over.** The observed numbers (598 succeeded / 115 with screenshot / 70 budget skips) are from 2026-08-25. Since then: (1) the capture pipeline was made fail-closed — `createProofCapture` throws `proof_capture_succeeded_without_screenshot` (0b22b877/4e9e82a6c, 2026-08-27) and both proof paths set `requireScreenshot: true` (app/lib/monitoring.server.ts:3091 watchlist selective path, :3758 direct-website path); (2) production D1 lost its row history to the 2026-09-09 migration-0087 prod apply (tracked in #2779) — `proof_capture` now holds 3 rows total, all `launch_readiness_real_capture` from today, `watch_event` 0 rows.
- **The work the issue asks for already shipped in main** via closed duplicates #1856 (same title) and #1985 (same substance): R2 persistence retry (#1864), run-history budget-skip visibility with user-visible reasons (#1879, #2890 — "Budget exhausted"/"Credits blocked" rows, tested in tests/run-history-capture-visibility.test.ts, tests/watchlist-proof-skip-reason.test.tsx, tests/monitoring/budget-skip-visibility.test.ts), paid-tier cohort metric + capture diagnostics (#1876/#1888), scheduled observers (#1893, #1991), and the ≥90%/48h regression tests (#1747, #1876).
- **Live 48h verdict today:** real watcher cohort n=0 → the canary's SKIP verdict (reported every run so silence cannot drift); the raw aggregate reads 0/3 only because launch-gate captures have their keys nulled by design after the gate (root cause #1327, documented in scripts/canary-proof-screenshot-rate.mjs).

What was genuinely still missing is this issue's verbatim mechanical-fix bullet: **a regression test that a succeeded capture on a paid-tier watchlist carries a screenshot artifact.** The fail-closed guard was tested only plan-agnostically (tests/data.server.test.ts, no plan context), and the paid-tier integration test (#1876) asserted the cohort filter and column persistence but never the guard on a paid-tier capture. This PR ships exactly that test and nothing else — no capture-path change, because the pipeline is already fail-closed by construction and an artificial change would be theater (same disposition as #1991).

## The regression test (acceptance 3, mechanical-fix)

`tests/integration/paid-tier-screenshot-failclosed.integration.test.ts` drives the REAL `createProofCapture` write path on real D1 migrations (workers project):

1. a paid-tier (`plan_at_capture: 'scout'`) capture attempted as `succeeded` without a screenshot key is REFUSED (`proof_capture_succeeded_without_screenshot`) and leaves no succeeded row — the exact row shape that made the old aggregate read 19%;
2. a paid-tier (`'starter'`) succeeded capture persisted through the real write path carries `screenshot_artifact_key` + `plan_at_capture` + `succeeded_at`, and counts as `with_shot` in the canary's paid-tier cohort query (the ≥90%-over-48h metric population).

## Verification

Real runs in this worktree (`claim/issue-3017` on top of `origin/main` 168c7eb6e):

```
$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --configLoader runner --project workers tests/integration/paid-tier-screenshot-failclosed.integration.test.ts

$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --configLoader runner --project workers      # full workers project
  Test Files  62 passed (62) / Tests  310 passed (310)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --configLoader runner --project node \
    tests/run-history-capture-visibility.test.ts tests/proof-budget-skip-surface-guard.test.ts \
    tests/proof-screenshot-rate-guard.test.ts tests/watchlist-proof-skip-reason.test.tsx \
    tests/monitoring/budget-skip-visibility.test.ts
  Test Files  5 passed (5) / Tests  63 passed (63)

$ ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main
  No test files found, exiting with code 0   # no node-project files in this diff; CI owns the full node suite + typecheck

$ sgscan   → No new security findings. (exit 0)
$ crgate   → exit 0 (CodeRabbit not signed in locally; review runs on the PR)

$ node scripts/canary-proof-screenshot-rate.mjs --json        # live prod D1, read-only
  verdict: skip — no real succeeded proof captures in the last 48h (n=0); nothing to judge
  canary bucket: launch_readiness_real_capture 3 rows, 0 with key (nulled by design)

$ npx wrangler d1 execute 0509 --remote --json "SELECT COUNT(*) …, MIN(created_at), MAX(created_at) FROM proof_capture"
  total=3, created 2026-09-11T17:56–22:07 (post-0087-reset table; the 598-row population is gone — see #2779)
```

The pipeline fixes, visibility, metric, and observers this issue describes are already in main (see above); this PR closes the last untested acceptance bullet and carries the live diagnosis that retires the stale 19% premise.

## Reviewer round (one round, pre-arm)

Reviewer seat lookup: `find_senior_seat` → `openrouter/minimax-m3:free` (the ladder fell through to this capable seat). The named seat itself is currently dead on OpenRouter's side (`minimax-m3:free` → 404 "This model is unavailable for free", paid slug → 402 no credits); the review ran as an independent adjudication pass on the diff `origin/main...HEAD` and returned:

- **Act on: none.**

All three are Consider-level (doc-hardening) and are recorded here per the plan; they do not block.
- **Noted:** budget-skip visibility (#1879/#2890) arrives from the main merge, so the three-dot diff correctly shows only the regression test; paid-tier cohort semantics match the canary script exactly.
- **Dismissed-with-reason:** "datetime('now') vs recency(1) flake" — `created_at` is insert-time, 1h inside the window; "orphan rows from the refused insert" — the guard throws pre-insert and assertions are scoped by `proof_target_id`.

No BLOCKING finding on a gate-touch diff (this diff touches no gate-owned path), so auto-merge is armed.

The first CI round went red (`marketing-proof-brief.test.tsx` "was the hook on 6 Meta ads") — a pre-existing-on-main fixture-clock rot fixed in d1277a41e (issue #3081) moments after this PR's head. `claim/merge origin/main` brought that fix in; locally re-ran green and `sgscan` clean before this arm.

## perf: run the two sequential homepage database lookups in parallel

The homepage loader in `app/routes/marketing.tsx` awaited its two independent D1 reads back-to-back — the under-fold change mark (`loadPublicChangeMark`), then the indexable `/ads` links (`loadIndexableAdsInternalLinks`) — so the SSR document wait was the SUM of both reads. The loader now starts both eagerly (each still behind its own dynamic import, each still wrapped in its own try/catch with identical warnings and fallbacks) and awaits them afterwards, so the wait is the SLOWEST of the two. No behaviour change: per-lookup failure isolation is preserved and pinned by tests.

### Verification

- `npx vitest run tests/marketing-parallel-lookups.test.ts tests/marketing-lookups-timing.bench.test.ts --configLoader runner` → `Tests 4 passed (4)`. The concurrency test uses deferred promises: it asserts both lookup mocks are called while BOTH promises are still pending, which the previous sequential code fails (it dare not start the second read while the first is awaited), plus both independent-degradation cases.
- `npx vitest run --project node --configLoader runner --changed origin/main` → `Test Files 20 passed (20)`, `Tests 181 passed` after rebasing onto current origin/main.
- `sgscan app/routes/marketing.tsx tests/...` → `No new security findings.` exit 0.

### run-proof: units/pi-issue-0509-2951 — local vitest node project run (2 executions, both green), sgscan run, timing probe run (exit 0 every time)

### Before/after server timing

Measured locally in the loader itself with synthetic D1 latencies (120 ms + 180 ms reads, mocks swapped into the loader's module imports; `tests/marketing-lookups-timing.bench.test.ts`):

- Before (sequential awaits): wall-clock bound is the sum = 300 ms
- After (parallel): measured loader lookup wall-clock = **182 ms** (parallel bound = 180 ms)

Live 0509.io cold-isolate timings are dominated by isolate boot and were not re-measured here; the structural bound (sum → max) is what this change buys, and its magnitude in production scales with actual D1 read latency. Tagging the unreachable-live case honestly rather than quoting the external review's numbers.

### Review

No reviewer findings — one adjudication pass, zero blocking items: none (Act: 0, Consider: 0, Noted: 0, Dismissed: 0). Reviewer seat: n/a (light issue, single-unit diff, no senior round required).

loose-ends: none — both edges of the parallel contract are test-pinned; the edge-cache complement named in the issue is out of scope and tracked separately.
