fix(monitoring): run the full-site scan before the degraded (cache-only) throw

Closes #3103

## Root cause

`runWatchlist` placed the Full-Site Watch block **after** the degraded
(`cache_only`) throw inside the first lease-fenced effect closure. A shared
discovery-provider cooldown degrades every scheduled run while the ads
pipeline still shows life, so the sitemap/robots inventory manifest — which
shares nothing with that provider — silently stopped writing too. The Meta
discovery canary went red (`website_site_scan rows: 0`):
- last green canary: 2026-09-10T23:15Z
- first red run: 34657821618's predecessor at 2026-09-11T04:52Z, red through 23:22Z

Code: the ordering has been there since the feature landed (`d3a645312`) and
stayed in that slot through the withRunLease re-thread (PR #2660, `b58a8e897`).
#2919's telemetry-cleanup hypothesis is **refuted** for this table: neither
`app/lib/retention.server.ts` nor `app/lib/data/launch-canary-cleanup.server.ts`
deletes `website_site_scan` rows; the `watchlist_run` FK cascade only removes
manifests for runs beyond the newest-N retention, which cannot zero the table.

## Fix

Run the site scan **before** the degraded check (same closure, same lease).
Cache-only runs now still produce an honest inventory manifest; everything
after the degraded throw is unchanged. The Meta discovery canary and
`scripts/check-d1-fullsite-runs.mjs` are untouched — they stay the live
detector. No verifier/gate files, no migrations/** touched (code-only per the issue).

## Verification

- `npx vitest run --project workers --configLoader runner tests/integration/website-site-scan-write.integration.test.ts` — 2 passed (new; proves orchestrator WRITE path on real migrations: healthy + degraded run each lands a `website_site_scan` manifest; verified RED on pre-fix code, green after)
- `npx vitest run --project workers --configLoader runner --changed origin/main` — 4 files, 22 tests passed
- `npx vitest run --project node --configLoader runner --changed origin/main` — 82 files, 977 tests passed
- `sgscan` — no new security findings
- `git grep -q "website_site_scan" scripts/check-d1-fullsite-runs.mjs` — canary intact

## run-proof:

- integration proving file: `tests/integration/website-site-scan-write.integration.test.ts` (workers vitest project, real migrations via `applyD1Migrations`)
- live detector kept: Meta discovery canary workflow (`.github/workflows/meta-discovery-canary.yml`) + `npm run canary:fullsite-runs`; next cron run after deploy is the green confirmation
- Test plan: `npx vitest run --project workers tests/integration/website-site-scan-write.integration.test.ts`

## loose-ends: website-site-scan-green-canary

The canary only proves green on the **next** scheduled cron after this deploys; until then prod stays red. Key: website-site-scan-green-canary.

Recorded, not re-delegated. (2) assert the manifest finalized (`status != 'running'`), not just that the row exists. Recorded, not re-delegated.

## Summary The watchlist detail loader pulls the 24 newest events but only the 12 newest proof captures. A confirmed `website_page_changed`/`landing_page_offer_changed` event whose `proofCaptureId` aged out of the 12-cap resolved to `null` in `proofCapturesById`, so `canRenderEventDiffPlate` refused the verified plate and `resolveEventChangeQuietCopy` printed `EVENT_CHANGE_UNVERIFIED_COPY` — "no successful stored capture behind it" — while the succeeded capture sat in D1, unloaded. Loader-only fix per the binding judge edits: after the `?event=` pin block, the loader unions in the loaded events' referenced captures via one new `listProofCapturesByIds(env, watchlistId, ids)` call (added to `app/lib/data/watchlist-proof.server.ts`, watchlist-scoped through the `proof_target` join, `queryIn` like its siblings). The merged list becomes `recentProofCaptures`, so every rendered event resolves its own capture; `buildProofSummary` keeps the original 12-recent input so summary semantics do not shift. No copy constants or component code changed. ## RED -> GREEN RED (before the fix — `tests/event-changes-section.test.tsx`, committed first at 5b70b7be): ``` FAIL loads the event's stored capture by id so the map can resolve it AssertionError: expected "vi.fn()" to be called with arguments: [ Anything, 'watch-1', ...(1) ] Number of calls: 0 FAIL never claims there is no successful stored capture behind a verified change AssertionError: expected '
' not to contain 'no successful stored capture' Received: "...Recorded, not verified. This change has no successful stored capture behind it, so we do not show it as a before-and-after...

..." ``` GREEN (after the fix): the loader calls `listProofCapturesByIds(env, "watch-1", ["cap-old"])`, the capture lands in `recentProofCaptures`, and the verified `f9-evidence-diff-plate` renders. ## Verification ``` $ npx vitest run tests/event-changes-section.test.tsx --configLoader runner --project node Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 2 passed (2) $ npx vitest run tests/watchlists.route.test.ts tests/watchlist-route-loader.test.ts tests/event-changes-section.test.tsx --configLoader runner --project node Test Files 3 passed (3) Tests 38 passed (38) $ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main Test Files 337 passed (337) Tests 4230 passed (4230) ``` run-proof: `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main` -> 337/337 files, 4230/4230 tests green (exit 0, rebased onto origin/main d06540ed0 2026-09-12). Typecheck is CI-owned (`npm run typecheck` runs in `ci.yml`); per fleet-ops#4891 / repo AGENTS.md it is intentionally not run inside the worker. ## Same-pattern sweep (do-step 3) Only this loader paired a bounded recent-capture list with a wider event set: - `app/lib/report-loader.server.ts` — uses `listProofCapturePairsForEventIds` (per-event fetch). Already correct. - `app/lib/digest-orchestration.server.ts` — event->capture via `listProofCapturePairsForEventIds`; its `listRecentProofCapturesForWatchlist` call is period triage counting, not id-paired. Already correct. - `app/lib/monitoring.server.ts`, `app/lib/first-brief.server.ts`, `app/lib/digest-email.server.ts` — only check `proofCaptureId` presence, never resolve through a bounded map. - `app/routes/api.v1.$resourceType.$resourceId.ts`, `app/routes/api.mcp.ts` — do not touch `proofCaptureId`. No other instance to fix. ## Manager-mode record (difficulty: heavy) Plan: `.fleet/plan.md` (3 phases). Phase outputs: - Phase 1 — RED test (`tests/event-changes-section.test.tsx`): reviewer verdict PASS; all seven checks NOTED; CONSIDER carried forward — the fix must import `listProofCapturesByIds` through the `~/lib/data.server` barrel (it does, via lazy `await import` matching the file's `listWatchEventsByIds` pattern, because the strict `vi.doMock` in `tests/watchlist-route-loader.test.ts` rejects an undeclared top-level destructure). - Phase 2 — query fn + barrel + loader union: reviewer verdict PASS. CONSIDER (noted, not acted): the unioned `recentProofCaptures` also feeds `classifyWatchPeriodTriage` — an event-referenced older non-succeeded capture can inform triage copy in the no-confirmed-events case; truthful data, spec-conformant, and the confirmed-events path short-circuits earlier anyway. Closes #2373.

## Scope (binding judge edits)
`do:` exactly: bisect the pollution, fix the shared state, then delete the `npm run test` step from `preview-assert.yml` keeping typecheck/build/versions-upload. `deploy-production.yml:514` is out of scope and untouched.

## What the bisection actually found
Two full-suite runs on `origin/main` (d06540ed0, 171s + 195s under load, 8288 tests) plus a 60-iteration race-probe harness found **no polluter** — the divergence was never cross-file pollution. It is two races **inside the victim spec itself**:

1. **Pidfile publish race**: the child published its pid with plain `writeFileSync(process.argv[1], …)`, so `provider.pid` exists **empty** between the child's `open()` and `write()`; suite-wide load stretches that gap past the reader's `existsSync`/`readFileSync` poll → `Number("")` → `NaN` (run 33561746667, 9 of 120 merges auto-reverted). **Fixed here:** the SIGTERM handler is installed **before** publishing and the pid is published **atomically** (write to `.tmp` → `renameSync`), so the pid is visible complete or not at all.
2. The 50ms liveness probe racing the child's 250ms graceful exit (run 34582626439) was already fixed on main by `411df4a9e`; this branch keeps that marker approach and adds a reader-side finiteness assertion.

With the race fixed at the source, the duplicate unsharded suite run in `preview-assert` buys nothing per PR: ci.yml's four node shards own coverage on every PR, and the deploy job's post-merge suite run is unchanged.

## What changed
- `tests/d1-remote-restore-evidence.test.ts`: handler-before-publish + atomic `write`+`renameSync` pid publish; reader asserts a real positive integer pid; `.sigterm` forwarding marker retained. No assertions weakened or skipped.

## Summary

The deploy gate's lone red test was fixture drift, not a homepage regression.

`tests/marketing-proof-brief.test.tsx` hard-coded its real-proof fixture's
`fetchedAt`/`capturedAt` to `2026-08-11T22:17:00.000Z` (written 2026-08-11 in
d32ab0d11). On 2026-09-10 that frozen clock aged past
`PROOF_CAPTURE_FRESH_DAYS` (30 days), so `marketing.tsx` honestly swapped the
proof strip to the "on record" branch (`is a hook on record across 6 Meta
ads`) — and the `was the hook on 6 Meta ads` assertion went red on schedule,
blocking every production deploy.

Fix at the root: the fixture claims to be "a real capture checked about 4
hours ago", so its capture clock is now computed as `Date.now() - 4h` and the
`proofStatus`/`freshness` labels derive from it the way `formatCapturedAt`
does in `app/lib/public-proof.server.ts`. The surface code is unchanged and
correct; every assertion is unchanged; the fixture can never rot again.

Checked for siblings with the same rot: `homepage-proof-capture-age.test.tsx`
pins `vi.setSystemTime`, `marketing-hero-fold.test.tsx` asserts only DOM order
("We saved the proof" renders in both branches). No other test asserts on the
fresh/stale copy.

Verification:

```
$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/marketing-proof-brief.test.tsx
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)

$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node --changed origin/main
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  13 passed (13)

$ npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/marketing-proof-brief.test.tsx tests/marketing-hero-fold.test.tsx tests/homepage-proof-capture-age.test.tsx tests/marketing-rebuild.test.ts tests/bet9-first-viewport-verification.test.ts
 Test Files  5 passed (5)
      Tests  77 passed (77)

$ sgscan
Scanning changes since origin/HEAD (168c7eb6)…
No new security findings.
```

crgate: not run — `crgate` exits 3, "CodeRabbit is not signed in on this
machine" (host auth, not fixable from the worker).

Reviewer round (seat: opencode/nemotron-3-ultra-free, via `Use reviewer`):

- Act on: none — diff correct and complete
- Consider: none
- Noted: surgical root fix — relative capture clock matches the fixture's own
  "checked about 4 hours ago" story; zero app code, zero weakened assertions
- Dismissed-with-reason: (1) `Date.now()` flake risk — 4h can never cross the
  30-day `captureAgeDays` gate; (2) "was" vs "is the hook on" wording —
  `freshForLiveClaim: false` + fresh capture renders "was the hook on" per
  marketing.tsx:554, matching the assertion
- REVIEW-VERDICT: SHIP

run-proof: `npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project node tests/marketing-proof-brief.test.tsx` on claim/issue-3081 @ d1277a41e -> 13/13 tests passed, exit 0 (previously the 'was the hook on 6 Meta ads' assertion failed)
net-positive-because: one test file touched; the deploy-blocking assertion and every other assertion are byte-identical — only the fixture's clock moved
research: n/a — no new bin/ files added
help-first: n/a — no new bin/ files added
organ-heartbeat: n/a — test-fixture-only diff, no organ paths touched
loose-ends: none

Closes #3081
